algorithm: Definite: norm-form isometry via Minkowski/dominant diagonal reduction. Indefinite: connecting ideal + right ideal isomorphism **[KV10]**.

description: For two isomorphic definite quaternion orders S, T over Z or F_q[X] (q odd): returns an algebra isomorphism. For orders over number rings, use `IsIsomorphic` with `FindElement`.

For ideals I and J of the same order O over Q, F_q(X) (q odd) or a number field: true iff I and J are isomorphic O-ideals. For definite algebras, also returns x with xI = J (left) or Ix = J (right). For indefinite algebras, a search is made and x is returned if found.
algorithm: Colon ideal principality via Minkowski/dominant diagonal/reduced basis **[KV10, DD08]**.

description: For a left or right ideal I over Z, F_q[X] or a number ring: true iff I is principal; if so, returns a generator.
For two definite ideals with the same left (resp. right) order S: true iff they are isomorphic as S-modules. Returns the isomorphism and the transforming scalar in A.
For two left (resp. right) ideals with the same left order O: true iff isomorphic as O-modules. Returns the isomorphism (given by multiplication) if true.
For two isomorphic left ideals over a definite order S over Z or F_q[X]: the S-module isomorphism and the quaternion algebra element defining it by right-multiplication.
For two isomorphic right ideals over a definite order S over Z or F_q[X]: the S-module isomorphism and the quaternion algebra element defining it by left-multiplication.
Returns a group G isomorphic to S¹ (elements of S with reduced norm 1), or if `ModScalars := true` (default `false`), G isomorphic to S¹/{±1}. Also returns a map G → S.
algorithm: Reduced Gram matrix / **[Vig76]** for number rings.

description: For the definite order S: the set of units S*. Over Z or F_q[X]: all units. Over a number field: representatives modulo the unit group of the base ring (since the unit group is infinite in general).
algorithm: Reduced Gram matrix (over Z/F_q[X]); **[Vig76]** (over number ring).

description: The unit group S* of the definite quaternion order S: returns an abstract group G and a map G → S. Over Z or F_q[X]: G is the full unit group. Over a number field: G is the unit group modulo the base ring's unit group.
algorithm: Reduced Gram matrix (over Z/F_q[X]); **[Vig76]** (over number ring).

description: Returns the group of isometries of the (possibly degenerate) reflexive form represented by matrix F over a finite field F_{p^e}. Parameter `Auto` (RngIntElt, default 0): the Frobenius exponent f in x → x^{p^f}; default treats F as bilinear over its base ring.
Returns the group of similarities of the (possibly degenerate) reflexive form represented by matrix F over a finite field F_{p^e}. Parameter `Auto` (RngIntElt, default 0): same convention as above.
Returns a system of forms associated to the p-group G. For matrix groups the input must be a class-2 p-group; PC-group input is preferred when readily available.
Returns true if and only if A has an assigned involution.
Returns the involution map associated to the *-algebra A.

Given a sequence S containing a nondegenerate system of reflexive forms over a finite field, returns the *-algebra of adjoints. Individual forms in S may be degenerate. Parameter `Autos` (SeqEnum, default [0,…,0]): list of Frobenius exponents, one per form; default treats all forms as bilinear over their common base ring.
Attaches the natural involution (induced by inversion in the underlying group) to the group algebra A and returns it.
Constructs the group algebra R[G] already equipped with the natural involution afforded by inversion in G.
Constructs the standard copy of the simple *-algebra of the given type name, defined naturally on a K-vector space of dimension d.
Returns the Jacobson radical J and a semisimple complement W to J in the *-algebra A. A may be a matrix algebra or a group algebra over any field.
algorithm: Adapted from W. de Graaf's structure-constant algebra procedure

description: Returns the Jacobson radical J and a *-invariant Wedderburn complement T to J in the *-algebra A. Requires char(base ring of A) ≠ 2. A may be a matrix *-algebra or a group algebra.
Decides whether the matrix *-algebra A is a simple *-algebra of classical type. If so, returns the standard *-algebra T, a *-isomorphism A → T, and its inverse T → A.
Decides whether the matrix *-algebra A is a simple *-algebra of exchange type. If so, returns the standard *-algebra T, a *-isomorphism A → T, and its inverse T → A.
Constructively recognises the *-algebra A (matrix *-algebra or group algebra). Also initiates recognition if not yet done, and is called implicitly by the access functions below.
Returns true if and only if A is a simple *-algebra. Initiates recognition if needed.
Returns the parameters (as a sequence of tuples) that determine, up to *-isomorphism, the minimal *-ideals of the semisimple quotient A/J. Initiates recognition if needed.
Returns the group of unitary elements of A: all units x ∈ A satisfying x* = x⁻¹.

Given a sequence S of reflexive forms (a system of forms), returns the group of isometries of the system. Handles degenerate individual forms and degenerate systems. Parameter `Autos` (SeqEnum, default [0,…,0]): Frobenius exponents for each form. Parameter `DisplayStructure` (BoolElt, default false): if true, prints the structure of the isometry group.

Given a sequence S of classical groups, each preserving (up to similarity) a unique nondegenerate reflexive form on a common finite vector space V, returns the intersection of the groups. It is not required that each group in S be the full isometry group.
Given a quadratic form Q, returns a triple C, V, f where C is the Clifford algebra of Q, V is the quadratic space of Q, and f is the standard embedding of V into C.
algorithm: Structure constant algebra construction; theory from **[Che97]**, **[Art57]**.

description: Given a quadratic space V with quadratic form Q, returns the pair C, f where C is the Clifford algebra of Q and f is the standard embedding of V into C.
Given a Clifford algebra C of dimension m = 2ⁿ over a field F and field elements r1, r2, …, rm ∈ F, constructs the element r1 ∗ C.1 + r2 ∗ C.2 + ⋯ + rm ∗ C.m of C.
Given a Clifford algebra C of dimension m = 2ⁿ and a sequence L = [r1, r2, …, rm] of elements of the base ring R of C, constructs the element r1 ∗ C.1 + r2 ∗ C.2 + ⋯ + rm ∗ C.m of C.
Returns the product of the i-th and j-th basis elements of the Clifford algebra C.
algorithm: Direct multiplication in the structure constant algebra.

description: Returns the basis element C.j of the Clifford algebra C corresponding to the subset L of {1, 2, …, n}, where j = 1 + Σ_{k ∈ L} 2^{k−1}. If e1, e2, …, eₙ is the standard basis for the underlying vector space, this corresponds to the product e_{i1} ∗ e_{i2} ∗ ⋯ ∗ e_{ih}, where L = {i1, i2, …, ih} and i1 < i2 < ⋯ < ih.
algorithm: Bijection between subsets and basis index; theory from **[Che97]**.

description: Given a subalgebra A of Mₙ(K), creates the right A-module M with underlying vector space K^(n); the action of a ∈ A on m ∈ M is m * a.
Given the subalgebra A of Mₙ(K) generated by the terms of sequence Q, creates the right A-module M with underlying vector space K^(n); the action of a ∈ A on m ∈ M is m * a.

Given a group G with r generators and a sequence Q of r invertible elements of Mₙ(K) or GL(n, K), constructs a K[G]-module M of dimension n where the action of G.i is Q[i]. Parameter `Check` (BoolElt, default `true`) verifies that the mapping is a group homomorphism.
Given a permutation group G and a field K, creates the natural permutation module for G over K.
The i-th generator of the A-module M.
Given an A-module M where A is an algebra over the field K, returns K.
The generators for the A-module M, returned as a set.
Given an element u of the A-module M, returns M.
Given an A-module M, returns the matrix algebra A giving the (right) action of A on M.
Given an R[G]-module M, returns the matrix group whose generators are the (invertible) generators of the acting algebra of M. Parameter `Check` (BoolElt, default `true`).
The i-th generator of the (right) acting matrix algebra for M.
The number of action generators (the number of generators of the algebra) for M.
Given an R[G]-module M, returns the group G.

Given an A-module M with base ring R and a ring S admitting a natural homomorphism from R, constructs the module N with base ring S (components coerced into S). Also returns the corresponding homomorphism M → N.
As above, but uses the explicit homomorphism f : R → S to map components. Also returns the corresponding homomorphism M → N.
Given R-modules M and N, constructs the direct sum D together with the embedding maps from M and N into D and the projection maps from D onto M and N.
Given a sequence Q of R-modules, constructs their direct sum D together with all embedding and projection maps.
Given a K[G]-module M of dimension n over K and a nonsingular n × n matrix T over K, constructs the K[G]-module N obtained by taking the rows of T as a new basis for M.
Constructs the element (a1, …, an) of M from elements a1, …, an of K. Errors if the result is not in M.
Given a sequence Q = [a1, …, an] with universe K, constructs the element (a1, …, an) of M. Errors if the result is not in M.
The zero element of the A-module M.
Given a module M defined over a finite ring or field, returns a random vector.
Given an element u of the A-module M, returns u as a sequence of elements of K.

subsection: 89.2.4.3 Action of the Algebra on the Module
description: Given a vector u in an A-module M and an element a ∈ A, returns the image of u under the action of a.

subsection: 89.2.4.3 Action of the Algebra on the Module
description: Given a vector u in a K[G]-module M and an element g ∈ G, returns the image of u under the action of K[G].
Sum of elements u and v in the same A-module M.
Additive inverse of element u.
Difference of elements u and v in the same A-module M.
Scalar product of k ∈ K and element u in A-module M (A a K-algebra).
Scalar product of element u and k ∈ K in A-module M (A a K-algebra).
Scalar product u * (1/k) for non-zero k ∈ K in A-module M.
Given an element u of a submodule M of R^(n) and 1 ≤ i ≤ n, returns the i-th component of u (as an element of R).
Redefines the i-th component of u to be x ∈ R; the parent of u is changed to R^(n) since the modified element need not remain in M.
Returns true if element u of A-module M is the zero element.
A set of integers giving the positions of the non-zero components of vector u.

Given an A-module M, constructs the submodule N generated by the elements of M specified by list L. Each term Li may be: (a) a sequence of n elements of R defining an element of M; (b) a set or sequence of elements of M; (c) a submodule of M; or (d) a set or sequence of submodules of M. Returns N together with the inclusion homomorphism f : N → M.
Given a basis matrix X for an A-submodule of the A-module M, returns the submodule N of M such that the morphism of N into M is X. Parameter `Check` (BoolElt, default `true`).
If the A-module M was created as a submodule of N, returns the inclusion homomorphism φ : M → N as an element of HomA(M, N).
Returns true if element u lies in the A-module M.
Returns true if A-module N is contained in A-module M.
Returns true if A-modules N and M are equal (both contained in a common A-module).
Sum of submodules M and N (in a common A-module).
Intersection of submodules M and N (in a common A-module).

Given an A-module M, constructs the quotient module P = M/N where N is generated by the elements specified by list L (same term types as `sub<>`). Returns P together with the natural homomorphism f : M → P.
If A-module N was created as a quotient of M, returns the natural homomorphism φ : M → N as an element of HomR(M, N).

Given an A-module M with finite-field base ring, attempts to find a proper submodule N of M or prove M is irreducible. If a splitting is found, returns: (a) the A-module N for the induced action on S; (b) the A-module P = M/N; (c) an invertible matrix T conjugating the matrices of ρ(A) into reduced form with ν(a) in the top-left block and π(a) in the bottom-right block. If M is proved irreducible, returns M alone and records irreducibility in M's data structure.
Returns true iff the A-module M is irreducible. If reducible, also returns a proper submodule S and the quotient Q = M/S.
Returns true iff the A-module M is absolutely irreducible. Also returns a matrix algebra generator for the endomorphism algebra E of M (a field) and the dimension of E.

Given an irreducible A-module M that is not absolutely irreducible over K, returns an absolutely irreducible module N that is a constituent of M considered over the splitting field for M. N is not unique.
Given an A-module M over a finite field K, returns the smallest subfield of K over which M can be realised.
Returns true iff the generators of the matrix algebra A are permutation matrices.

Given an A-module M, constructs a composition series by repeatedly applying the Meataxe. Returns: (a) the series as a sequence of A-modules; (b) the composition factors in series order; (c) a transformation matrix t such that for each a ∈ A, t * a * t⁻¹ is in reduced form.

Given an A-module M, constructs the composition factors by repeatedly applying the Meataxe. Returns a sequence of R-modules in series order; if M is irreducible, returns a sequence containing M alone.

Given an A-module M, returns: a sequence C of representatives for the isomorphism classes of composition factors; and a sequence I of indices so that the i-th element of C is the I[i]-th composition factor of M.
As `Constituents(M)` but also returns the multiplicity of each constituent. A sequence I of indices is also returned.

Given an A-module M that is a K[G]-module (ModGrp) for a field K, returns whether M is semisimple. For a semisimple module defined over a matrix algebra, also returns a list of ranks of the primitive idempotents (equivalently, multiplicities of simple modules as composition factors).

Given an A-module M, returns a sequence containing the maximal submodules of M. Parameter `Limit` (RngIntElt, default 0): if non-zero, at most Limit submodules are computed; second return value indicates whether all were returned.
The Jacobson radical of the A-module M (intersection of all maximal submodules).

Given an A-module M, returns a sequence containing the minimal (irreducible) submodules of M. Parameter `Limit` (RngIntElt, default 0): if non-zero, at most Limit submodules are computed; second return value indicates whether all were returned.
Given an A-module M and an irreducible module F, returns those minimal submodules of M isomorphic to F. Parameter `Limit` (RngIntElt, default 0).
Returns a single minimal (irreducible) submodule of M; if M is itself irreducible, returns M.
The socle of M, i.e. the sum of all minimal submodules of M.

A socle series S for M, together with the socle factors corresponding to the terms of S and a matrix T giving the transformation of M into semi-simple reduced form. The series does not include the trivial module but does include M.
The factors of the socle series for M as a sequence of A-modules in series order. If M is irreducible, returns a sequence containing M alone.
Given an A-module M, returns true iff M is decomposable. If decomposable and defined over a finite field, also returns proper submodules S and T of M such that M = S ⊕ T.

Given an A-module M, returns a sequence Q of indecomposable summands of M. Each element of Q is an indecomposable submodule; M equals the direct sum of the terms of Q. If M is indecomposable, Q contains M alone.
Given an A-module M and a submodule S of M, determines whether S has an A-invariant complement in M. If so, returns true and a submodule T such that M = S ⊕ T; otherwise returns false.
Given an A-module M and a submodule S of M, returns all A-invariant complements of S in M.

Constructs the lattice L of all submodules of M. Parameter `Limit` (RngIntElt, default 0): if non-zero, at most Limit submodules are computed; second return value indicates whether L is the full lattice. Parameter `CodimensionLimit` (RngIntElt, default −1).
algorithm: Works down a composition series of M.

description: Constructs the lattice of submodules of M provided their number does not exceed n. Returns true and the lattice if successful; false if M has more than n submodules.
Controls verbose printing for the submodule lattice algorithm. Level i = 1 for moderate printing, i = 2 for maximal printing; a summary is printed per level of the composition series.
Returns a sequence of all submodules of M sorted by dimension. Parameter `CodimensionLimit` (RngIntElt, default `Dimension(M)`).
The cardinality of L (the number of submodules of M).
Creates the i-th element of lattice L (index i serves as a unique identifier; elements are not ordered in any meaningful way).
Creates the element of lattice L corresponding to the submodule S of M.
Creates the bottom element of L (corresponding to the zero-submodule of M). If the lattice is partial (created with a limit), the bottom may not be the zero submodule.
Creates a random element of L.
Creates the top element of L (corresponding to M itself).
The integer corresponding to lattice element e.
The lattice element corresponding to the sum of the submodules for e and f.
The lattice element corresponding to the intersection of the submodules for e and f.
Returns true iff lattice elements e and f are equal.
Returns true iff e lies below f in L (i.e. the submodule of e is a submodule of that of f).
The maximal submodules of e, returned as a set of lattice elements.
The minimal supermodules of e, returned as a set of lattice elements.
The submodule of M corresponding to lattice element e.
The dimension of the submodule of M corresponding to e.
The lattice element corresponding to the Jacobson radical of the submodule corresponding to e.
The morphism (as a matrix) from the module corresponding to e to M.
Given A-modules M and N, creates the (map) homomorphism from M to N given by matrix X.
Given matrix space H = HomA(M, N) and a homomorphism f from M to N, creates the matrix corresponding to f.
Given a matrix X ∈ HomK(M, N) where M and N are A-modules, returns true if X is an A-homomorphism.
Given A-modules M and N, constructs the vector space HomK(M, N) (K-homomorphisms, not necessarily A-equivariant).
Given A-modules M and N, constructs the vector space HomA(M, N) as a submodule of HomK(M, N).
Given A-modules M and N, constructs HomL[G](M, N) as a subspace of HomK(M, N), where L is the centralizing field of M.
Given an A-module M with base ring K, constructs E = EndA(M) as a subring of the complete matrix ring K^(n×n). Parameter `Direct` (BoolElt, default `false`).
Given an A-module M with base ring K, constructs the centre of EndA(M) as a subring of K^(n×n). Equivalent to `Centre(EndomorphismRing(M))` but typically much faster.
Given an A-module M with base ring K, constructs Aut(M) as a subgroup of GL(n, K) — the group of units of End(M).

Returns true if A-modules M and N are isomorphic, false otherwise. If isomorphic, also returns a matrix T such that M^T = N (i.e. T⁻¹ * ActionGenerator(M, i) * T = ActionGenerator(N, i) for each i). Requires matching action generators.
For an algebra A, creates a module over A. For a left-module, m is a map from A × M → M; for a right-module, m is a map from M × A → M (M must be an R-module where R is the coefficient field of A).

description: Returns the ground field of the algebra module M.

description: Returns a sequence containing the basis vectors of the algebra module M.
Returns true if the algebra module M is a left-module, false if it is a right-module.

The dimension of the algebra module M.

description: Given an algebra module M over algebra A and a subalgebra B of A, returns M as a B-module.

description: Returns the submodule of M containing the elements in sequence S or the elements e1, …, en.

description: Constructs the quotient module of M by the submodule S of M (or the submodule generated by S or e1, …, en).

Create the trivial K[G]-module for group G.

description: As `GModule(G, A, B)` with trivial B. Returns M and the homomorphism φ: A → M.

description: Given group G, subgroup H of finite index, and field K, create the K[G]-module for G acting on the cosets of H.

description: Given G as above, ideal I of P = K[x₁,…,xₙ], and zero-dimensional subideal J of I, create the K[G]-module for G acting on the finite-dimensional quotient I/J. Returns M, isomorphism f, and indexed set of monomials forming a basis of I/J.

Given G as above and Q = I/J a finite-dimensional quotient ring of P = K[x₁,…,xₙ], create the K[G]-module for the action of G on Q. Returns M, isomorphism f, and indexed set of monomials forming a basis of Q.

description: Given sequence Q of K[G]-modules over finite field K of characteristic p and finite field F of characteristic p, return the sequence of modules obtained by applying `AbsoluteModuleOverMinimalField` to each element of Q.

description: Given sequence Q of K[G]-modules over finite field K and subfield F of K of index n, return the sequence of F[G]-modules obtained by applying `ModuleOverSmallerField` to each element.

description: Given K[G]-modules M and N, change their base fields to K, where K is the smallest field containing both base fields.

description: Returns `true` iff Coxeter matrices `M1` and `M2` give rise to Coxeter-isomorphic groups. Also returns a sequence encoding the permutation of the basis taking `M1` to `M2`.
algorithm: Checks equality of matrices up to simultaneous row/column permutation.

description: The (factored) order of the Coxeter group with Coxeter matrix `M`.
Returns `true` iff `M` is the Coxeter matrix of an irreducible Coxeter system. If reducible, also returns a nontrivial subset I ⊆ {1,…,n} with mᵢⱼ = 2 for i ∈ I, j ∉ I.
algorithm: Connectivity check on the associated Coxeter graph.

description: Returns `true` iff all entries of the Coxeter matrix `M` are in {1, 2, 3} (no edge labels > 3).
Returns `true` iff the graph `G` is the Coxeter graph of some Coxeter group.
algorithm: Checks that the graph is standard (vertex set {1,…,n}), undirected, and all edge labels are in {0, 3, 4, 5, …}.

description: The Coxeter graph corresponding to a Coxeter matrix `M`, Cartan matrix `C`, or Dynkin digraph `D`.
The (factored) order of the Coxeter group with Coxeter graph `G`.
Returns `true` iff the Coxeter graph `G` is simply laced (unlabelled, i.e. all edges have mᵢⱼ = 3).

Returns `true` iff `C` is a Cartan matrix. Parameter `RealInjection` (default `false`): for number-field or cyclotomic-field base, supply an injection into R (resp. C) so that conditions (2) and (4) can be checked; without it those conditions are skipped.
algorithm: Checks the four defining conditions; conditions (2) and (4) require a real injection for non-real base fields.

description: A Cartan matrix for the Coxeter matrix `M` or Coxeter graph `G`. Default: cᵢⱼ = −4cos²(π/mᵢⱼ), cⱼᵢ = −1 for mᵢⱼ ≠ 2 and i < j (crystallographic when a crystallographic form exists). Parameter `Symmetric` (default `false`): if true, returns the symmetric form cᵢⱼ = cⱼᵢ = −2cos(π/mᵢⱼ). Parameter `BaseField` (default `"NumberField"`): `"NumberField"`, `"Cyclotomic"` / `"SparseCyclotomic"`, or `"DenseCyclotomic"` (overridden to Z when crystallographic).
algorithm: Conversion from Coxeter data; default form is chosen to be crystallographic when possible.

description: The crystallographic Cartan matrix corresponding to the Dynkin digraph `D`.
algorithm: Reads edge labels as −cᵢⱼ entries of the Cartan matrix.

description: Returns `true` iff Cartan matrices `C1` and `C2` give Coxeter-isomorphic groups (i.e. their Coxeter matrices are equal up to basis permutation). Also returns the permutation sequence.
algorithm: Reduces to comparing Coxeter matrices up to permutation.

description: Returns `true` iff crystallographic Cartan matrices `C1` and `C2` are Cartan equivalent (equal up to basis permutation). Also returns the permutation sequence. Stronger than Coxeter isomorphism (e.g. B₅ and C₅ are Coxeter isomorphic but not Cartan equivalent).
algorithm: Checks equality of matrices up to simultaneous row/column permutation.

description: The number of positive roots of the root system with Cartan matrix `C`. See §96.1.3 for the definition.
The (factored) order of the Coxeter group with Cartan matrix `C`.
The fundamental group Zⁿ/Γ of the crystallographic Cartan matrix `C`, where Γ is the lattice generated by the rows of `C`. Also returns the natural map Zⁿ → Zⁿ/Γ.
algorithm: Abelian-group quotient by the row lattice.

description: Returns `true` iff `C` is the Cartan matrix of an irreducible Coxeter system. If reducible, also returns a nontrivial subset I with cᵢⱼ = 0 for i ∈ I, j ∉ I.
algorithm: Connectivity check on the associated Coxeter graph.

description: Returns `true` iff the Cartan matrix `C` is crystallographic (all entries integers).
Returns `true` iff `C` is simply laced (all entries of its Coxeter matrix are in {1, 2, 3}).
Returns `true` iff the digraph `D` is the Dynkin digraph of some crystallographic Cartan matrix.
algorithm: Checks that the graph is standard, and that the edge labels are consistent with a valid Cartan matrix.

description: The Dynkin digraph of the crystallographic Cartan matrix `C`.
algorithm: Reads off the negative off-diagonal entries of `C` as directed edge labels.

description: The (factored) order of the Coxeter group with Dynkin digraph `D`.
The fundamental group Zⁿ/Γ of the Dynkin digraph `D`, where Γ is the row lattice of the corresponding Cartan matrix. Also returns the natural map Zⁿ → Zⁿ/Γ.
algorithm: Abelian-group quotient by the row lattice.

description: Returns `true` iff the Dynkin digraph `D` is simply laced (unlabelled, i.e. all edges have label 1).
Returns `true` iff the corresponding Coxeter group is finite. Input may be a Coxeter matrix `M`, Coxeter graph `G`, Cartan matrix `C`, Dynkin digraph `D`, or Cartan name string `N`.
algorithm: Classification **[Car52, Cox34]**: tests whether all irreducible components match a finite type.

description: Returns `true` iff the corresponding Coxeter group is affine. Input as above.
algorithm: Classification **[Car52, Cox34]**: tests whether all components are finite or affine and at least one is affine.

The Coxeter graph with Cartan name given by string `N`.

The irreducible Dynkin digraph with Cartan name `Xn`. The name must be crystallographic.

algorithm: Reduces to comparing the corresponding Coxeter matrices up to permutation.

algorithm: Reduces to comparing the corresponding Cartan matrices up to permutation.

description: The Cartan name (string) of a Coxeter matrix `M`, Coxeter graph `G`, Cartan matrix `C`, or Dynkin digraph `D`. Raises an error if the Coxeter group is neither finite nor affine.
algorithm: Reverse lookup in the classification table.

description: Prints the Dynkin diagram of the given Coxeter data. Raises an error if the group is neither affine nor crystallographic.
algorithm: Formatted ASCII display from the classification table.

description: Prints the Coxeter diagram of the given Coxeter data. Raises an error if the group is not affine or not crystallographic.
algorithm: Formatted ASCII display from the classification table.

algorithm: Classification: rank-3 groups are automatically hyperbolic if infinite and non-affine; rank > 3 is checked against the table of 72 groups.

description: Returns `true` iff the graph `G` is the Coxeter graph of a (compact) hyperbolic Coxeter group.
algorithm: As above but for graph input.

subsection: 96.5.3 Operations and Properties for Roots and Coroot Indices
description: Indices of the left string through αs in direction αr in the crystallographic root system R: the sequence [r₁, …, rp] with αri = αs − i·αr, where αs − (p+1)·αr is not a root. Requires αr ≠ ±αs.

subsection: 96.5.3 Operations and Properties for Roots and Coroot Indices
description: Indices of the right string through αs in direction αr: [r₁, …, rq] with αri = αs + i·αr, where αs + (q+1)·αr is not a root. Requires αr ≠ ±αs.

subsection: 96.5.3 Operations and Properties for Roots and Coroot Indices
description: The largest p such that αs − p·αr is a root. Requires R crystallographic and αs ≠ ±αr.

subsection: 96.5.3 Operations and Properties for Roots and Coroot Indices
description: The largest q such that αs + q·αr is a root. Requires R crystallographic and αs ≠ ±αr.

subsection: 96.5.3 Operations and Properties for Roots and Coroot Indices
description: An additive order on the positive roots of R: a sequence containing 1, …, N such that αr + αs = αt implies t lies between r and s.

(Procedure.) Explicitly force a Gröbner basis for ideal I to be constructed. Normally not necessary (computed automatically when needed), but allows control via parameters. Parameters: `Al` (`"Default"`, `"Direct"`, `"FGLM"`, `"Walk"`; default `"Default"` — FGLM for zero-dimensional ideals over finite field or Q, Walk otherwise); `Faugere` (BoolElt, default `true` — use F4 if field is finite or Q, else Buchberger); `HomogeneousWeights` (BoolElt, default `true` — search for homogeneous weight vector); `Homogenize` (BoolElt, default `true` over Q, `false` elsewhere — homogenize before computing); `DegreeStart` (RngIntElt — ignore S-polynomial pairs of degree < this value); `AllPairs` (BoolElt, default `false` — F4: include all pairs in queue at each step, not just current degree); `PairsLimit` (RngIntElt, default 0 — F4: max pairs per step to limit matrix size); `ReversePairs` (BoolElt, default `false` — F4: reverse pairs list when `PairsLimit` is active); `HFE` (BoolElt, default `false` — F4: apply HFE optimisations for F₂ systems with secret degree ≤ 127); `Boolean` (BoolElt, default `false`); `Nthreads` (RngIntElt, default 1 — F4 multi-threading over Fp); `ReduceInitial` (BoolElt, default `true` — Buchberger: reduce basis before S-pairs); `RemoveRedundant` (BoolElt, default `true` — Buchberger: remove redundant input polynomials first); `ReduceByNew` (BoolElt, default `true` — Buchberger: reduce current basis by each newly inserted polynomial); `SigmaEpsilon` (FldRatElt, default 1/2 — Walk: perturbation factor for initial weight vector σ); `TauEpsilon` (FldRatElt, default 1/n — Walk: perturbation factor for final weight vector τ); `SigmaVectors` (RngIntElt, default n — Walk: number of weight vectors of initial order used for σ perturbation); `TauVectors` (RngIntElt, default ⌈n/2⌉ — Walk: number of weight vectors of final order used for τ perturbation). Over Euclidean rings, only `Homogenize` applies.
algorithm: F4 **[Fau99]** / Buchberger **[CLO96]**, both with pair elimination **[Möl88]**; order conversion via FGLM **[FGLM93]** or Gröbner Walk **[CKM97]**. Over Euclidean rings: Steel's extension of F4 **[Fau99]** (unpublished).

description: Given an ideal I, force the Gröbner basis to be computed and return it. Parameters are the same as for `Groebner`.

Given an ideal I, return the Gröbner basis of the easy ideal of I.
Given an ideal I, return the shortest-length basis of I currently known (either the original basis or a Gröbner basis, always in the same monomial order as I).

Given a set or sequence S of polynomials, return whether S is a (not necessarily minimal or reduced) Gröbner basis of the ideal it generates.

Given an ideal I with basis b₁,…,bₖ and a polynomial f ∈ I, return a sequence [g₁,…,gₖ] with f = Σ gᵢ·bᵢ. If I was created by `IdealWithFixedBasis`, the fixed basis is used; otherwise the Gröbner basis is used. Result is not necessarily unique.

Given an ideal I with a fixed basis (created via `IdealWithFixedBasis`), return the coordinate matrix C: the i-th row gives the coordinates of the i-th Gröbner basis element w.r.t. the fixed basis. Computes the Gröbner basis first if not already done.
Given a polynomial f from polynomial ring P and an ideal I of P, return the unique normal form of f w.r.t. the Gröbner basis of I. The normal form is 0 iff f ∈ I.

Given a polynomial f and a set or sequence S of polynomials, return a normal form g of f w.r.t. S (not unique in general; zero iff f ∈ Ideal(S) only when S is a GB). If S is a sequence, a second return value C gives the coordinates: g = f − Σ C[i]·S[i].
Given polynomials f and g from a polynomial ring P, return the S-polynomial of f and g.

Given a set or sequence S of polynomials, return the reduced sequence: each element reduced to normal form w.r.t. the others, zero elements removed, result sorted. Normally used only for simplifying non-GB sets; all Gröbner bases returned by Magma are automatically reduced.

Given a set or sequence S assumed to be a (not necessarily minimal or reduced) Gröbner basis, return its reduction: first remove polynomials whose leading terms are multiples of another's, then reduce remaining polynomials as in `Reduce`. Let S be a set or sequence of homogeneous polynomials in P = K[x₁,…,xₙ] (K a field), I = Ideal(S). Let H be the Hilbert series H_{P/I}(t) (as a rational function in Z(t)) or N ∈ Z[t] be the weighted numerator of the Hilbert series (H_{P/I}(t) multiplied by ∏(1−t^{dᵢ}) where dᵢ is the weighted degree of the i-th variable). Attempts to construct the reduced Gröbner basis of I using this Hilbert data. Returns: `true`, Gröbner basis (if Hilbert data is correct or an under-estimate of the true numerator coefficient-wise) or `false` (if data is provably wrong, i.e. claimed coefficient exceeds the true coefficient at some degree).
(Procedure.) Set verbose level for the Hilbert-driven Buchberger algorithm. Legal values: `true`, `false`, 0, 1.

Given a sequence B of boolean polynomials in a rank-n boolean polynomial ring (or a rank-n polynomial ring over F₂), call MiniSat on the associated boolean system and return: (1) whether the system is satisfiable, and (2) if so, a solution S as a length-n sequence of elements of F₂. Parameters: `Exclude` ([RngMPolElt], default [] — sequences of length-n F₂-vectors to exclude as solutions, implemented by adding exclusion relations to the system); `Verbose` (BoolElt, default `true` — controls MiniSat's own verbose output).
algorithm: MiniSat SAT solver (external). Boolean polynomial to CNF transformation.

description: Sum of ideals I and J (same ring P): ideal generated by the generators of both.
Product of ideals I and J: ideal generated by all pairwise products of generators.
k-th power of ideal I.
For I, J ideals of P over a field with J ⊂ I: the affine algebra I/J.
Dimension of P/I as a K-vector space. Returns `Infinity` if I is not of Krull dimension 0. Distinct from `Dimension` (which returns Krull dimension).
Colon ideal I : J — all f ∈ P such that f·g ∈ I for all g ∈ J.

Saturation I : f^∞ — all g ∈ P such that f^i·g ∈ I for some i ≥ 1. Also returns an integer s ≥ 1 with I : f^∞ = I : f^s (only if a second return value is expected; omitting it greatly speeds up the computation). Computed by eliminating variable t from ⟨I, 1 − f·t⟩.
Returns the saturation C = I : f^∞ and a polynomial g of minimal degree such that C = I : ⟨g⟩; irreducible factors of g are a subset of those of f.
Saturation I : J^∞ = {f ∈ P : ∃n > 0, f^n J ⊆ I}.
Saturation of I with respect to the irrelevant ideal (all elements of positive degree).
Returns the ambient polynomial ring P of I.
The leading-monomial ideal of I (ideal generated by all leading monomials).
Intersection of ideals I and J in the same ring P.
Intersection of all ideals in set or sequence S.
Computes and returns a maximal regular sequence in I. If `Homogeneous` is true (default) and I is homogeneous w.r.t. variable weights, the sequence is also homogeneous.

Computes the Rees ideal K such that R1/K ≅ R(I)/⟨a-torsion⟩, where R(I) = R ⊕ I ⊕ I² ⊕ … is the Rees algebra. For the second/third signature R = P/J or an affine quotient algebra. Parameter `a` specifies a non-zero divisor (default 1); setting a ≠ 1 removes a-torsion, giving the coordinate ring of the maximal flat subscheme of the blow-up.
algorithm: Rees algebra construction; see **[Har77 Ch. 2 §7]** for the geometric interpretation.

description: True iff I = J (same ring P).
True iff I ≠ J.
True iff I ⊄ J.
True iff I ⊆ J.
True iff I is the zero ideal.
True iff I ≠ P (Gröbner basis does not contain 1).
True iff I has a basis of homogeneous polynomials (w.r.t. variable weights). Checks current basis first; if not Gröbner, checks an easy Gröbner basis.
True iff I is principal; if so, also returns a generator. True iff any Gröbner basis has a single element.
True iff I is primary (ab ∈ I ⟹ a ∈ I or b^n ∈ I for some n ≥ 1). Computes or retrieves primary decomposition and checks it has one element. Same field restrictions as `PrimaryDecomposition`.
True iff I is prime. Computes or uses stored primary decomposition. Same restrictions as `PrimaryDecomposition`.
True iff I is maximal. First checks zero-dimensionality; if zero-dimensional, checks primality.
True iff I = Radical(I). Computes or uses stored radical. Same restrictions as `Radical`.
True iff I is zero-dimensional (P/I has finite non-zero dimension as K-vector space). Note: the full ring P as an ideal has dimension −1 and is not zero-dimensional.
True iff the monomial order of I is grevlex.
True iff polynomial f ∈ P lies in ideal I. Computes the normal form of f w.r.t. a Gröbner basis of I and checks for zero.
True iff f ∉ I. As with `in`, uses normal-form computation.
True iff f is in the radical of I. Much faster in general than computing the full radical.
Returns the ideal generated by all first partial derivatives of polynomial f.

For a zero-dimensional ideal I of P over K: returns the variety as a sequence of n-tuples, one per solution. If a superfield L of K is given, the variety is computed over L. Over the free complex field, uses a special root-finding algorithm; `Digits` controls complex precision (see Chapter 25).
algorithm: Triangular or radical decomposition, then univariate root-finding.

description: As `Variety` but returns a sequence of sequences (instead of tuples); requires the order of P to be of lexicographic type.

For a zero-dimensional ideal I over K: returns the size of the variety over the algebraic closure K′ of K, without explicitly computing the variety. Finds the prime radical decomposition and places each component in normal position.
algorithm: Prime radical decomposition; counting argument. Much faster than computing the full variety.

description: Milnor number of f at the origin: dimension of the quotient of the localization of K[x₁,…,xₙ] at the origin by the ideal of partial derivatives of f. See **[CLO98 p. 147]** or **[DL06 Remark 9.37]**.
algorithm: `QuotientDimension` of Jacobian ideal in local ring.

description: Tjurina number of f at the origin: dimension of the quotient of the localization by the ideal generated by f and its partial derivatives. See **[CLO98 p. 148]** or **[DL06 Def. 9.35]**.

k-th elimination ideal Iₖ = I ∩ R[xₖ₊₁,…,xₙ] (all polynomials with the first k variables eliminated). If k = n, returns I ∩ R. If R is a field, this is P or the zero ideal. If R is not a field, returns the ideal generated by the normalised smallest element in I∩R. Parameters are as for `Groebner`; setting `Al := "Direct"` can give much better performance.
algorithm: Gröbner basis with elimination order. If a lex Gröbner basis is already stored, elimination ideals can be read off directly.

signature: `EliminationIdeal(I, S)` (S a set of integers or variables)
description: Elimination ideal IU = I ∩ R[U], where U is the subset of variables specified by S (integer indices or variable elements of P). S = ∅ is equivalent to `EliminationIdeal(I, n)`.
algorithm: Gröbner basis with elimination order; see **[AL94 Ex. 4.3.8]** for an example over Z[√−5].

description: For a zero-dimensional ideal I of K[x₁,…,xₙ] and 1 ≤ i ≤ n: the unique monic generator of I ∩ K[xᵢ].
For a zero-dimensional ideal I of K[x₁,…,xₙ]: the sequence of n monic generators, one per variable xᵢ.

For a sequence Q of k polynomials in P over S: the relation ideal U ⊆ S[y₁,…,yₖ] of all algebraic relations r with r(Q[1],…,Q[k]) = 0. If T (a polynomial ring of rank k) is given, U is returned as an ideal of T.
algorithm: Introduces k new variables yᵢ and relations yᵢ − Q[i], then eliminates the original xᵢ variables — image of an affine polynomial map.

description: Creates a k-variable extension Q of the ring of I = R[x₁,…,xₙ]: if b = true, Q = R[y₁,…,yₖ,x₁,…,xₙ]; if b = false, Q = R[x₁,…,xₙ,y₁,…,yₖ]. Returns the corresponding ideal J of Q and the embedding map f : P → Q. The inverse image under f of an ideal H of Q is the restriction I ∩ R[x₁,…,xₙ] (elimination performed automatically). The order argument specifies the monomial order of Q (default: grevlex).
algorithm: Ideal extension + elimination for inverse image.

description: Creates a single-variable extension H of the ring of I, introducing a homogenization variable h. If b = true, H = R[h,x₁,…,xₙ]; if b = false (or b omitted), H = R[x₁,…,xₙ,h]. Returns the homogenized ideal J and the homogenization map f : P → H. Inverse image under f of a polynomial of H is obtained by setting h = 1; inverse image of an ideal J is the ideal obtained by setting h = 1. The order argument specifies the order of H (default: grevlex).
algorithm: Homogenization map + elimination for inverse image.

description: For ideal I of P = K[x₁,…,xₙ] (K a field) and sequence U = [u₁,…,uₖ] of variable indices: constructs the ring-of-quotients extension Q = K(xu₁,…,xuₖ)[remaining variables] and returns the ideal J of Q together with the map f : P → Q. Inverse image under f of a polynomial of Q is obtained by clearing denominators (making it monic then multiplying by the LCM of denominators); inverse image of an ideal H of Q is the ideal generated by inverse images of the basis elements (not always the contraction — see **[BW93 p. 389]** for the contraction algorithm).
algorithm: Extension to a polynomial ring over a rational function field.

description: For I an ideal of P over a field: returns the dimension d of I and a sorted sequence of d variable indices forming a maximally independent set modulo I. If I = P, dimension is −1 and the second return value is not set.
For I an ideal of P over a field: returns the radical R = {f ∈ P : f^n ∈ I for some n ≥ 1}. Works for any field over which polynomial factorisation is available.
algorithm: Standard radical algorithm; works via `PrimaryDecomposition` internally or dedicated radical computation.

description: For I an ideal of P over a field: returns two parallel sequences Q (primary components) and P (associated primes) such that: (a) ideals of Q are primary; (b) their intersection is I; (c) P[i] = Radical(Q[i]) is prime; (d) Q is minimal (no redundant components, distinct associated primes); (e) P is always unique and Q is unique if I is zero-dimensional. Works for any field with polynomial factorisation; inseparable extensions handled by **[Ste05]**.
algorithm: Algorithm of **[BW93 Ch. 8]** (based on Gröbner bases), with a triangular decomposition pre-step (since V2.4). Inseparable field extensions: **[Ste05]**.

description: For I an ideal of P over a field: returns the prime decomposition of the radical of I as a sequence P of minimal prime ideals whose intersection is Radical(I). Equivalent to `PrimaryDecomposition(Radical(I))` but often much more efficient.
algorithm: As `PrimaryDecomposition` but applied to the radical; may avoid computing primary components.

description: As `RadicalDecomposition` but probabilistic: the returned ideals may not be prime. Much faster in practice.
For a set/sequence S of ideals with I = ∩J∈S J: returns a minimal subset M ⊆ S with the same intersection (no redundant ideals).
Sets verbose level v (legal values: `true`, `false`, 0, 1, or 2) for the primary/radical decomposition algorithms.

For I a zero-dimensional ideal of P over a field with lexicographic order: returns a sequence Q of ideals whose intersection equals I, where each radical J ∈ Q is triangular. Second return value indicates whether I is proven radical (if so, all entries are triangular).
Returns the highest-dimensional equidimensional component of I.
algorithm: For homogeneous I: module-theoretic method via Noether normalisation (kernel of M → double dual over linear Noether normalisation S). General case: **[GP02]**.

description: Returns the full equidimensional decomposition as a sequence of ideals, one per dimension.
algorithm: As `EquidimensionalPart`; module method for homogeneous I, **[GP02]** in general.

description: Finer decomposition: each equidimensional component is further split so that each factor has a single set of variables constituting a maximally independent set of all its primary components. Returns a sequence of pairs (factor, variable index set).
algorithm: Same base algorithm; additional splitting for unique maximally independent sets.

description: Computes a Noether normalisation of I using linear combinations of variables. Guaranteed to work in characteristic 0; may fail in small characteristic. Returns: (1) the sequence [f₁,…,fₐ]; (2) an automorphism h : P → P (linear change of variables) mapping the fᵢ to the last d variables of P; (3) the inverse of h.
algorithm: Algorithm of **[GP02]** with a simpler test for homogeneous I (considering subsets of variables before general linear combinations).

intrinsic: Normalisation, Normalization, UseFF, true, FFMin, UseMax, false
description: Computes the normalisation (integral closure) of the radical ideal I. Returns a list of pairs (ideal Iᵢ of generic ring Gᵢ, homomorphism φᵢ : P → Gᵢ). I must be radical; base field K must be perfect. `UseFF` (default true): if rank(P) = 2, uses Magma's function-field machinery (much faster). `FFMin` (default true, when `UseFF` is true): uses a filtration by Riemann–Roch spaces to minimise the number of generators (slower but usually faster than the general algorithm, much nicer output; set false to skip minimisation). `UseMax` (default false, only affects general algorithm): assumes I ⊆ ⟨x₁,…,xₙ⟩ and P/I is locally normal away from this maximal ideal — speeds up the general algorithm when the variety is singular only at the origin. Incorrect if P/I is locally non-normal at other primes.
algorithm: General algorithm: De Jong, as described in **[GP02]**. Function-field case: Riemann–Roch-based algorithm using Magma's function-field machinery.

description: For a homogeneous ideal I of P over a field: the Hilbert series Hₚ/ᵢ(t) as an element of Z(t). Note: equivalent to `HilbertSeries(QuotientModule(I))`; for the Hilbert series of I as a P-module, call `HilbertSeries(Submodule(I))`.
As above but returns the Hilbert series as a power series to precision p.
The unreduced Hilbert denominator D = ∏ᵢ (1 − t^wᵢ), where wᵢ is the weight of the i-th variable (default 1). Returned as a univariate polynomial over Z.
The unreduced Hilbert numerator N = D × Hₚ/ᵢ(t), as a univariate polynomial over Z. Often more convenient for computation.

For a homogeneous ideal I with all variable weights 1: returns the Hilbert polynomial H(d) ∈ Q[d] and the index of regularity k (minimum k ≥ 0 such that H(d) agrees with the Hilbert function for all d ≥ k).
For a sequence Q of k polynomials in P: returns the module of syzygies as an r×k matrix S whose rows span all v with Σ v[i]·Q[i] = 0. The base ring may be a field or a Euclidean ring.
algorithm: Standard module Gröbner basis with a particular elimination order; see **[GP02 §2.5]**.

description: Returns the kernel of f as an ideal in R = {a ∈ R : f(a) = 0}. Computed as the relation ideal for the polynomials defining f; see `RelationIdeal`.
For polynomial p ∈ S: returns whether p is in the image of f.
Returns whether f is surjective. Checks via `IsInImage` whether each codomain variable lies in the image.
Extension of ideal I by φ (homomorphism from the generic ring of I): the ideal generated by the image of I under φ.
algorithm: Direct application of φ to generators.

description: For polynomial map φ : Kⁿ → Kᵐ parametrising a variety V (as the image of φ): constructs the ideal of S corresponding to V. If V is not a true variety, returns its Zariski closure.
algorithm: Algorithm of **[CLO96 p. 97]**: introduce variables, add relations, then eliminate.

description: For polynomial ring P of rank n and 1 ≤ k ≤ n: returns the k-th elementary symmetric polynomial of P.

For polynomial f ∈ P of rank n: returns whether f is symmetric in all n variables. If true, also returns g in a new ring of rank n (or in the given ring S of rank n) such that f = g(e₁,…,eₙ), where eᵢ is the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial of P.
algorithm: Decomposition in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials.

section: 106.17 Functions for Polynomial Algebra and Module Generators
description: For a set/sequence L = {f₁,…,fₖ} ⊆ K[x₁,…,xₙ]: returns a minimal generating set (as a sorted sequence drawn from L) for the subalgebra A = K[f₁,…,fₖ].
algorithm: Redundancy elimination by algebraic independence testing.

section: 106.17 Functions for Polynomial Algebra and Module Generators
description: For homogeneous polynomials P = [p₁,…,pₖ] and S = [s₁,…,sᵣ] in R, and F ∈ R: returns whether F lies in the A-module M = A[s₁,…,sᵣ] (where A = K[p₁,…,pₖ]). If true, also returns a sequence C = [c₁,…,cᵣ] with cᵢ ∈ K[t₁,…,tₖ] such that F = Σ cᵢ(p₁,…,pₖ)·sᵢ. Typical use: P = primary invariants, S = secondary invariants, F = arbitrary invariant.
algorithm: Splits F into homogeneous components; for each degree d, constructs a K-basis for M^d and tests membership by linear algebra.

section: 106.17 Functions for Polynomial Algebra and Module Generators
description: As above but for a sequence L of l homogeneous elements all of the same degree d. Returns parallel sequences B (booleans) and V (coefficient sequences), one per element of L. More efficient than calling the single-element version repeatedly (one echelonisation suffices for the whole batch).
algorithm: Batch version: single echelonisation of the degree-d basis of M, then linear algebra for all elements of L.

section: 106.17 Functions for Polynomial Algebra and Module Generators
description: For homogeneous P, S (as above) and a sequence L of l homogeneous elements of the same degree d: returns a sequence I of integer indices such that the subsequence of L indexed by I extends any basis of the degree-d part of M = A[s₁,…,sᵣ] to a basis of U + V (U = M^d, V = K-span of L). Used to extend a minimal module generating set while ensuring minimality.
algorithm: Echelonisation of M^d; extends to U + V by selecting linearly independent residues.

description: Create a local polynomial ring in n > 0 variables over field K. Default order: local lexicographical (`"llex"`).

description: Create a local polynomial ring in n > 0 variables over ring K with the given monomial order string `order` (see §107.2).

description: Create a local polynomial ring in n > 0 variables over field K with the order given by tuple T. T must have components matching the valid order arguments from §107.2; such a tuple is also returned by `MonomialOrder`.

subsection: 107.3.1 Creation of Local Polynomial Rings and Accessing their Monomial Orders
description: Given a local polynomial ring R (or an ideal thereof), return a description of the monomial order of R as a tuple (matching the relevant arguments in §107.2). The tuple may be passed directly as the third argument to `LocalPolynomialRing`.

subsection: 107.3.1 Creation of Local Polynomial Rings and Accessing their Monomial Orders
description: Given a polynomial ring R of rank n (or an ideal thereof), return the weight vectors of the underlying monomial order as a sequence of n sequences of n rationals (see [CLO98, p. 153]).

subsection: 107.3.1 Creation of Local Polynomial Rings and Accessing their Monomial Orders
description: Given a (global) multivariate polynomial ring R = K[x₁,…,xₙ] (or an ideal I of such R), return the localization K[x₁,…,xₙ]⟨x₁,…,xₙ⟩ of R (or the corresponding ideal of the localization). Variable print names are carried over.

description: Given a local polynomial ring R, return the ideal generated by the elements in list L. Each term of L may be: (a) an element of R; (b) a set or sequence of elements of R; (c) an ideal of R; (d) a set or sequence of ideals of R.

subsection: 107.3.2 Creation of Ideals and Accessing their Bases
description: Given a set or sequence B of polynomials from a local polynomial ring R, return the ideal of R generated by B, with basis B. Equivalent to the `ideal< >` constructor but more convenient for a sequence.

subsection: 107.3.2 Creation of Ideals and Accessing their Bases
description: Given a polynomial f from a local polynomial ring R, return the principal ideal of R generated by f.

subsection: 107.3.2 Creation of Ideals and Accessing their Bases
description: Given an ideal I, return the current basis. Returns the standard basis if it has been computed; otherwise the original basis.

subsection: 107.3.2 Creation of Ideals and Accessing their Bases
description: Given an ideal I and integer i, return the i-th element of the current basis of I. Equivalent to `Basis(I)[i]`.
Given an ideal I of a local polynomial ring, force computation of the standard basis and return it.
algorithm: Mora normal form + standard basis algorithm with homogenization **[CLO98, Sec. 4.4]**.

description: Given a set or sequence S of polynomials of a local polynomial ring R, return a standard basis of the ideal generated by S as a sorted sequence.
algorithm: Mora normal form + standard basis algorithm with homogenization **[CLO98, Sec. 4.4]**.

description: Sum of ideals I and J of the same polynomial ring P: the ideal generated by the union of their generators.
Product of ideals I and J of the same polynomial ring P: the ideal generated by all pairwise products of generators.
k-th power of ideal I of polynomial ring P, for integer k.
Given an ideal I of a local polynomial ring R over a field K, return the dimension of R/I as a K-vector space. (Distinct from `Dimension`, which returns the Krull dimension.)
Given an ideal I of a local polynomial ring R, return R.
Given an ideal I, return the leading monomial ideal of I: the ideal generated by all leading monomials of I.
Intersection of ideals I and J of the same polynomial ring P.
Given a set or sequence S of ideals of the same local polynomial ring R, return the intersection of all ideals in S.
Return whether ideals I and J of the same polynomial ring P are equal.
Return whether ideals I and J of the same polynomial ring P are not equal.
Return whether I is not contained in J (ideals in the same polynomial ring P).
Return whether I is contained in J (ideals in the same polynomial ring P).
Return whether ideal I of the local polynomial ring R is the zero ideal (contains only zero).
Return whether ideal I of the local polynomial ring R is proper (strictly contained in R, i.e. the standard basis does not contain 1).
Return whether ideal I is zero-dimensional: whether R/I has non-zero finite dimension as a vector space over the coefficient field. (Note: R itself has dimension −1 and is not zero-dimensional.)
Given a polynomial f from a local polynomial ring R and an ideal I of R, return whether f is in I.
Given a polynomial f from a local polynomial ring R and an ideal I of R, return a normal form of f with respect to (the standard basis of) I. The normal form is zero if and only if f is in I.
Given a polynomial f from a local polynomial ring R and an ideal I of R, return whether f is not in I.

Given an ideal I of local polynomial ring R = K[x₁,…,xₙ] and a field L, construct the ideal J of S = L[x₁,…,xₙ] by coercing the coefficients of the basis of I into L. Requires that all elements of K can be automatically coerced into L.

Given an ideal I of local polynomial ring R = K[x₁,…,xₙ] and a local polynomial ring S of rank n (possibly with a different order), return the ideal J of S corresponding to I and the isomorphism f: R → S mapping R.i to S.i for each i.

Given an ideal I of polynomial ring P = R[x₁,…,xₙ] and a monomial order string `order` (see §107.2), construct Q = R[x₁,…,xₙ] with that order, and return the ideal J of Q corresponding to I and the isomorphism f: P → Q (mapping P.i to Q.i).

Given an ideal I of a local polynomial ring R defined over a field, return the Krull dimension d of I, together with a sorted sequence U of integers of length d such that the variables of P corresponding to U form a maximally independent set modulo I. If I is the full local ring R, the dimension is −1 and the second return value is not set.
Given a multivariate polynomial ring `P` and an ideal `J` of `P` (or generators `a1, …, ar` of `J`), return the quotient ring `P/J`. Angle bracket notation assigns names to indeterminates.
algorithm: Quotient ring construction via Gröbner basis reduction.

description: Given a multivariate polynomial ring `P` and an ideal `J` of `P`, return the quotient affine algebra `P/J`.
Given a ring `R`, a list `X` of `n` identifiers, and a list `L` of polynomial relations in the variables `X`, create and return `R[X]/⟨L⟩`. Angle bracket notation assigns names to indeterminates.
algorithm: Quotient ring construction via Gröbner basis reduction.

description: Return the `i`-th indeterminate of affine algebra `Q` as an element of `Q`.
Return the coefficient ring of the affine algebra `Q`.
Return the rank of `Q` (number of indeterminates).
Given an ideal `I` of the affine algebra `Q = P/J`, return the defining ideal `J` of `Q` as an ideal of the polynomial ring `P`.
Given an ideal `I` of `Q = P/J`, return the ideal `I′` of `P` such that the image of `I′` under the natural epimorphism `P → Q` is `I`.
Given `Q = P/J`, return the polynomial ring `P`.
Return the generic polynomial ring `P` such that `Q = P/J` for some ideal `J`.
Return `true` if and only if ideals `I` and `J` of the same affine algebra are equal.
algorithm: Equality via preimage ideals and Gröbner bases.

description: Return `true` if and only if ideal `I` is contained in ideal `J`.
Return the sum `I + J` of two ideals of the same affine algebra.
Return the product `I * J` of two ideals of the same affine algebra.
Return the power `Iⁿ` of ideal `I` (integer `n`).
Return the intersection `I ∩ J` of two ideals of the same affine algebra.
Return whether ideal `I` of affine algebra `Q` is proper (strictly contained in `Q`).
Return whether ideal `I` is the zero ideal (equivalently, whether the preimage ideal of `I` equals the divisor ideal of `Q`).
Return whether ideal `I` of affine algebra `Q` is prime.
Return whether ideal `I` of affine algebra `Q` is primary.
Return whether ideal `I` of affine algebra `Q` is radical.
Return the primary decomposition of ideal `I`, together with the associated prime ideals.

description: Return the (prime) decomposition of the radical of ideal `I`.
algorithm: Mapped through preimage polynomial ring; radical decomposition algorithms.

description: Return the kernel of the homomorphism `φ` of affine algebras.
algorithm: Kernel computed via preimage ideal methods.

description: Given an affine algebra `Q` defined over a field, return whether `Q` has finite dimension as a vector space.
Given a finite dimensional affine algebra `Q` over a field, return the vector-space dimension of `Q`.
algorithm: Monomial basis count from Gröbner basis.

description: Given a finite dimensional affine algebra `Q` over a field, construct the vector space `V` isomorphic to `Q` and return `V` together with the isomorphism `f : Q → V`.

Given a finite dimensional affine algebra `Q` over a field, return the basis `B` of monomials of `Q` as a sequence of length `d = Dimension(Q)`, such that `f(B[i]) = V.i` where `V` and `f` are the returns of `VectorSpace`.
algorithm: Reduced monomials modulo Gröbner basis of `J`.

description: Given a finite dimensional affine algebra `Q` over a field, construct the matrix algebra `A` isomorphic to `Q` and return `A` together with the isomorphism `f : Q → A`.
Given an element `f` of a finite dimensional affine algebra `Q` over a field, return the `d × d` representation matrix of `f` over the coefficient field (where `d = Dimension(Q)`).
algorithm: Multiplication-by-`f` matrix in the monomial basis.

description: Given an element `f` of a finite dimensional affine algebra `Q` over a field, return whether `f` is a unit.
Given an element `f` of a finite dimensional affine algebra `Q` over a field, return whether `f` is nilpotent, and if so the smallest `q` such that `fq = 0`.
Given an element `f` of a finite dimensional affine algebra `Q` over a field, return the minimal polynomial of `f` as a univariate polynomial over the coefficient field.

description: Given an element `a` from the ring of fractions of affine algebra `Q`, return the numerator of `a` as an element of `Q`.

Submodule of M generated by {f·v : v ∈ M} resp. {v·f : v ∈ M} for f ∈ R.

Return whether M equals N (compatible modules). Checks equality of appropriate module Gröbner bases.
Return whether M is free (isomorphic to R^k for some k). Checks whether a minimised presentation of M has trivial relations.

Return a minimal basis B of M. If M is graded or R is local, #B is the unique minimal number of generators (the rank). Otherwise #B satisfies only the rule that the i-th element is not in the submodule of elements 1..i−1.

description: Given a set or sequence S of homogeneous module elements, return a minimal basis of the submodule generated by S.
Return the rank of M: the cardinality of `MinimalBasis(M)`. Unique iff M is graded or R is local.

Return the colon module M : J — the submodule of the ambient A of M consisting of all f ∈ A with f·g ∈ M for all g ∈ J. For principal J, reduces to a syzygy computation; in general, intersect colon modules for each generator of J.
Return the colon ideal M : N — the ideal of R of all f ∈ R with f·N ⊂ M, for M, N submodules of a common supermodule.
Return the annihilator ideal of M — the ideal of R of all f with f·M = 0. Equals the colon ideal 0_M : M.
Return the i-th Fitting ideal of M: ideal generated by the (r−i)-th minors of the presentation matrix of M, where r = Degree(M). See **[CLO98, p.229]**, **[Eis95, §20.2]**.
Return the Fitting ideals for i = 0 to r = Degree(M) as a sequence.
Return the syzygy module S of M. If the basis B of M has length k, S has degree k and elements of S express syzygies among the k basis elements. Note: degree of result depends on the current basis.
algorithm: Module Gröbner basis; syzygies are computed as a by-product.

description: Return the syzygy module S of the **minimal** basis of M. S has degree equal to the cardinality of the minimal basis.
algorithm: Module Gröbner basis of the minimal basis.

description: Given a sequence Q of polynomials from a multivariate polynomial ring P, return the module of syzygies of Q — a P-module of degree #Q consisting of all vectors v with Σ v[i]·Q[i] = 0.

Given R-module M (R a polynomial ring) and polynomial ring S of the same rank as R, construct the S-module obtained by coercing the coefficients of M's basis and relations into S. All old coefficient ring elements must be automatically coercible into the new coefficient ring.
Given graded R-module M, return the Hilbert series H_M(t) as a univariate rational function over Z. The i-th coefficient is the vector-space dimension of the degree-i graded piece.
Return H_M(t) as a Laurent series to precision p. (Laurent series needed when grading has negative weights.)
Return the unreduced Hilbert denominator D = ∏ᵢ(1 − t^{wᵢ}) (where wᵢ are the variable weights of R).
Return the unreduced Hilbert numerator N and valuation shift s, where N = D × t^s × H_M(t). s is non-zero only when M has negative column weights.
Given graded R-module M, return the Hilbert polynomial H(d) ∈ Q[d] and the index of regularity (minimal k ≥ 0 such that H(d) agrees with the Hilbert function for all d ≥ k).

Given R-module M, return a free resolution C (a complex) and a comparison homomorphism f : C₀ → M. Parameters: `Minimal` (default `true` — construct minimal resolution; if `false`, construct non-minimal by successive syzygy modules); `Limit` (default 0 — if non-zero, compute at most l terms; set to rank(R) by default for affine/exterior algebras); `Homogenize` (default `true` — force/suppress internal homogenization trick); `Al` (default `"LaScala"` — select algorithm).
algorithm: **La Scala (LS) algorithm [SS98]** extended with Faugère F4 **[Fau99]** block-normal-form techniques, used by default for homogeneous M over a finite field or Q. **Iterative algorithm** (`Al := "Iterative"`): successive syzygy modules, with optional minimization at each step. If M is non-homogeneous over a global ring, Magma may internally homogenize M to use the LS algorithm, then specialize.

description: (Procedure.) Set verbose printing level for the free resolution algorithm and related functions to v.
Return Betti numbers of M: the sequence of degrees (ranks) of non-zero terms of the free resolution. Unique if M is graded or over a local ring.
Return the graded Betti number β_{i,j}: number of generators of degree j in the i-th term F_i of the resolution.
Return the maximum degree of generators in the i-th term of the resolution (maximum j with β_{i,j} ≠ 0).
Return the Betti table of M as a sequence S of sequences and a shift s, designed so that S[1,1] ≠ 0 and S[i,j] = BettiNumber(M, i, j−i+s).

For graded M or M over a local ring: return the **Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity** — the least r such that in the minimal free resolution the maximum generator degree of F_i is at most i + r. See **[Eis95, §20.5]**, **[DL06, p.167]**.
Return the homological dimension of M: the length (number of non-zero boundary maps) of a minimal free resolution.

Given R-modules M and N, return H = Hom_R(M, N) as an abstract reduced module, together with a transfer map f : H → {homomorphisms M → N}. An element h ∈ H maps to an actual `ModMPolHom`; f is invertible. If M and N are graded, H is graded: the degree of h ∈ H equals the degree of the corresponding homomorphism.
algorithm: Free resolution of M, then Hom applied termwise.

description: Given a complex C of R-modules and R-module N, return the complex Hom_R(C, N). The i-th term is Hom_R(C_i, N); boundary maps are induced by those of C via the functor Hom_R(−, N) (arrows reversed). See **[Eis95, p.63]**.
Given integer i ≥ 0 and R-modules M, N, return Ext^i(M, N): the homology at the i-th term of the complex Hom_R(C, N), where C is a free resolution of M.
Given R-modules M and N, return the tensor product T = M ⊗_R N as an ambient module, together with the bilinear map f : M × N → T. If M and N are graded, T is graded.
Given a complex C of R-modules and R-module N, return the complex C ⊗_R N. The i-th term is C_i ⊗_R N; boundary maps are induced via the functor − ⊗_R N. See **[Eis95, p.64]**.
Given integer i ≥ 0 and R-modules M, N, return Tor_i(M, N): homology at the i-th term of the complex C ⊗_R N, where C is a free resolution of M.

Given graded module M over P = k[x₀,…,x_m] (k an exact field), return dim_k H^r(P^m_k, M̃(n)) where M̃ is the coherent sheaf associated to M and M̃(n) is its n-th Serre twist. r must be a non-negative integer; n can be any integer. Parameter `Verbose Cohom` (maximum 1): verbose output level.
algorithm: BGG correspondence + Tate resolution **[EFS03, DE02]**; non-commutative Gröbner bases for the exterior algebra resolution; results cached per M.

description: Molien series of G as an element of Z(t). For permutation groups: always exists and equals the Hilbert series for any field K. For matrix groups: requires char(K) coprime to
Approximation to the Molien series of a permutation group G as a Laurent series with n known coefficients. Can handle far larger groups than `MolienSeries`.
Construct optimal primary invariants for R = K[V]^G as a sorted sequence of n polynomials (increasing degree), where n is the degree of G.

description: Variant for modular R only: use subgroup H ≤ G. Secondary invariants for K[V]^H (with respect to the primaries of G) are computed first, then used as in **[KS97]**. Mainly useful when a particular subgroup H is better than the automatic strategy.

Return the irreducible secondary invariants (primary invariants + these generate R as an algebra over K). In the non-modular case these may be a proper subset of the secondary invariants; in the modular case they coincide with the secondary invariants minus 1. The expression of secondaries in terms of irreducible ones is the second return value of `Algebra(R)`.

Construct fundamental invariants for R = K[V]^G as a sorted sequence of polynomials (increasing degree). Parameter `Al`: `"King"` (default for non-modular, since V2.15) **[Kin07]** or `"MinPrimSec"` (minimises the union of primary + secondary invariants, always used in the modular case). Parameter `MaxDegree`: set to d if an a-priori degree bound is known, allowing early termination in the King algorithm (non-modular).
algorithm: Non-modular: S. King's algorithm **[Kin07]** by default. Modular (or `Al := "MinPrimSec"`): minimisation of primary + secondary union.

description: Return a sorted sequence of algebraic relations among the algebra generators, as elements of A. So R ≅ A/⟨relations⟩.

description: The ideal in A generated by `Relations(R)`.

description: The graded polynomial ring corresponding to the primary invariants of R (with weights = degrees of the primary invariants).

section: 110.15 The Algebra of an Invariant Ring and Algebraic Relations
description: The ideal in P generated by the primary invariants of R (stored in R).
Hilbert series of R = K[V]^G as an element of Z(t). Uses Molien series if available; otherwise computes secondary invariants.
algorithm: Molien series (non-modular permutation/matrix case) or secondary-invariant construction (modular case).

description: Hilbert series of R as a Laurent series with n known terms, computed using conjugacy classes of G.
Whether R is Cohen-Macaulay. Always true in the non-modular case; in the modular case secondary invariants are constructed to determine the result.
Free resolution of (the module of) R; same as `FreeResolution(Module(R))`. Returns a sequence F: F[1] = M, F[i+1] = syzygy module of F[i], last element is free.
algorithm: Syzygy computation over the primary algebra.

description: Minimal free resolution of (the module of) R; same as `MinimalFreeResolution(Module(R))`.
Homological dimension of R: length of the minimal free resolution minus 1 (M itself is included).
Depth of R; equal to n − d by the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula, where n is the rank and d is the homological dimension.
The i-th Steenrod operation P^i(f) of multivariate polynomial f with coefficients in a finite field; i must be a non-negative integer.
algorithm: Steenrod algebra action on polynomial rings in characteristic p.

description: For a set or sequence L = {p₁,…,pₖ} of polynomials in R = K[x₁,…,xₙ]: return a minimal generating set of the subalgebra K[p₁,…,pₖ] as a sorted sequence of elements from L.
algorithm: Gröbner basis / membership test iteratively removing redundant generators.

description: For homogeneous P = [p₁,…,pₖ], S = [s₁,…,sᵣ], and a single element F ∈ R: test whether F lies in the A-module M = A[s₁,…,sᵣ] (A = K[p₁,…,pₖ]). If true, also return coefficients cᵢ ∈ K[t₁,…,tᵣ] such that F = Σ cᵢ(p₁,…,pₖ)·sᵢ.

As above but for a sequence L of l elements homogeneous of degree d. Returns parallel boolean sequence B and coefficient sequence V. B[i] = true iff L[i] ∈ M; V[i] = the coefficients (or zero coefficients if B[i] = false).
algorithm: Gröbner basis over A applied to each element.

section: 110.20 Invariant Rings of Linear Algebraic Groups
description: Construct the invariant ring R for the algebraic group G defined by ideal I and representation matrix A. Parameters: `Reductive` (BoolElt, default `false`) — assume G is reductive; `LinearlyReductive` (BoolElt, default `false`) — assume G is linearly reductive (required for Derksen's algorithm); `PolynomialRing` (RngMPol, default auto) — use a specified polynomial ring P for the invariants.
algorithm: Lazy construction; Derksen's algorithm **[Der99]** invoked when `FundamentalInvariants` is called (requires `LinearlyReductive`).

section: 110.20 Invariant Rings of Linear Algebraic Groups
description: For N = [n₁,…,nₖ] a sequence of positive integers and p a prime or 0: define the action of G = SL₂(K̄) (char K = p) on a direct sum of spaces of binary forms of degrees nᵢ. Returns: ideal IG defining G, representation matrix A (as sequence of sequences of polynomials), and a polynomial ring with appropriate variable names. Second form takes a single integer n and sets N = [n].
algorithm: Standard SL₂ action on binary forms.

description: Return the ideal I defining the algebraic group G of invariant ring R.

description: Return the representation matrix A for the algebraic group G of invariant ring R.

description: K-basis of R_d (homogeneous invariants of degree d) in the invariant ring R of an algebraic group, as a sequence of polynomials.

section: 110.20 Invariant Rings of Linear Algebraic Groups
description: Fundamental invariants of R (algebraic group), as a sequence. Parameters: `Optimize` (BoolElt, default `true`) — extend basis at each degree by multiplying lower-degree invariants by monomials; `Minimize` (BoolElt, default `true`) — minimise the generators; `MinimizeHilbert` (BoolElt, default `true`) — minimise the Hilbert ideal basis; `Force` (BoolElt, default `false`) — force Derksen's algorithm even if group may not be linearly reductive. Requires `LinearlyReductive` (or `Force := true`).

section: 110.20 Invariant Rings of Linear Algebraic Groups
description: Generators of the Derksen ideal of R: an ideal D of P[y₁,…,yₙ] defined as the intersection of ideals ⟨y₁−g(x₁),…,yₙ−g(xₙ)⟩ over all g ∈ G; geometrically the vanishing ideal of {(x,g(x)) : x ∈ Kⁿ, g ∈ G}. Returned with a Gröbner basis.

section: 110.20 Invariant Rings of Linear Algebraic Groups
description: Hilbert ideal of R: the ideal in P generated by all non-constant homogeneous invariants. Returns a sequence of homogeneous generators (not necessarily invariant). Parameters: `Minimize` (BoolElt, default `true`); `Force` (BoolElt, default `false`).
Create the invariant field for permutation group G over field K.
Create the invariant field for matrix group G (field K from G).
Create the invariant field for the algebraic group defined by ideal I and representation matrix A. Parameters: `Reductive`, `LinearlyReductive`, `FunctionField` (FldFunRat, default auto).
Return the underlying rational function field of invariant field F.
Return the underlying group of invariant field F.
For invariant field F over an algebraic group: return the ideal I defining G.
For invariant field F over an algebraic group: return the representation matrix A.

Fundamental invariants of invariant field F as a sequence generating F as an algebra over the base field. Parameters: `Al` (`"BethMuellerQuade"` default, or `"FleischmannKemperWoodcock"` for the Fleischmann–Kemper–Woodcock alternative); `Minimize` (BoolElt, default `true`) — return irredundant set; `Min` (RngIntElt, default 0) — stop when generating set of this size is reached; `BottomUpTo` (RngIntElt, default 0) — for minimisation, first try small subsets.
algorithm: Beth–Müller-Quade algorithm **[MQB99]** by default; Fleischmann–Kemper–Woodcock alternative via parameter.

description: Derksen ideal of invariant field F: an ideal D in K[y₁,…,yₙ] (K = k(x₁,…,xₙ)) defined as the intersection of ideals ⟨y₁−g(x₁),…,yₙ−g(xₙ)⟩ for g ∈ G. Returned with a Gröbner basis.

For L a set or sequence of non-constant elements of a rational function field: select a minimal (irredundant) subset generating the same subfield. Parameters: `Min` (RngIntElt, default 0) — stop at a generating set of this size; `BottomUpTo` (RngIntElt, default 0) — use bottom-up approach up to this size. Returns a sequence of minimal generators.

For L a non-empty set or sequence of non-constant elements from F = k(x₁,…,xₙ) generating K = k(L): the Quade ideal in F[y₁,…,yₙ] (kernel of K[y₁,…,yₙ] → F, yᵢ ↦ xᵢ), introduced in **[MQS99]**, returned with a Gröbner basis. Parameters: `Fy` (polynomial ring of rank n over F, to make result an ideal of a specific ring); `LargeIdeal` (BoolElt, default `false`) — return an ideal in a larger ring whose intersection with F[y₁,…,yₙ] is the Quade ideal.
