True iff X is nonsingular and equidimensional over an algebraic closure; tests emptiness of the scheme defined by appropriate minors of the Jacobian matrix.
True iff X has a singular point or fails to be equidimensional.
Subscheme defined by appropriate-sized minors of the Jacobian; lower-dimensional components of X are included even if nonsingular.
Irredundant prime (irreducible) components of X.
Irredundant primary components of X.
Subscheme of X with reduced structure, with the map to X; uses Groebner basis to compute the radical.
algorithm: Radical of ideal via Groebner basis.

description: True iff X has a unique prime component; Groebner basis needed if not a hypersurface; projective X is saturated first.
True iff the defining ideal equals its radical; hypersurface case uses derivatives only; otherwise Groebner basis (projective X saturated first).
True iff every scheme-theoretic point of X has a Cohen-Macaulay local ring; requires X equidimensional and ordinary projective. Parameter `CheckEqui`.
True iff X is Cohen-Macaulay and the canonical sheaf is locally free of rank 1; computationally heavy. Requires X equidimensional and ordinary projective.
algorithm: Minimal free resolution + canonical sheaf check.

description: True iff the coordinate ring of X satisfies the Cohen-Macaulay property; implies `IsCohenMacaulay`; ordinary projective, equidimensional.
True iff the coordinate ring of X is Gorenstein; implies `IsArithmeticallyCohenMacaulay`.
Base change of ambient or scheme A to field K (automatic coercion from BaseRing(A) to K required). No cached data transferred.
Base change of A via ring homomorphism m whose domain is BaseRing(A).
Base change of a sequence F of schemes in a common ambient, to field K or via map m.
Base change of scheme X into ambient A of the same type and dimension; equations transferred via coercion or map m.
Base change of X (over a finite field) to the degree-n extension of its base field.
Projective closure of affine scheme X; cached and referentially stable (always returns the identical object). For X already a projective scheme (or computed from a patch) returns the stored closure.
The i-th affine patch of projective scheme X; cached. Order: the first patch has its final coordinate nonzero.
A standard affine patch of X containing point p; also returns the corresponding point on the patch.
Whether affine space A is a standard affine patch of its projective closure and, if so, which index; false if no projective closure exists.
Number of standard affine patches of X (0 for affine X).
Whether the i-th patch of X can be created.
The hyperplane complement of affine scheme X in its projective closure.
The map from affine space A to its projective closure.
A sequence of maps from affine spaces to projective space P giving the standard disjoint decomposition P^n = A^n ∪ A^{n-1} ∪ … ∪ {p}; also returns the point p = (1:0:…:0).
An affine patch of S centred at point p (via translation of a standard patch) and the embedding into S.
Set a given affine-to-projective map (defined by polynomials S, or a map m) as the projective closure map of A; used when no standard relationship between A and P exists.

section: 112.13 Arithmetic Properties of Schemes and Points
description: Exponential height of point P in its ambient affine or projective space (possibly weighted). Parameters: `Absolute` (default false; if true returns the absolute height), `Precision` (default 30). Works for P defined over Q, a number field, or a function field.

section: 112.13 Arithmetic Properties of Schemes and Points
description: Weil restriction of affine scheme S (base ring K) to subfield F. Returns: the restriction scheme Sres over F, a map (Sres)⊗K → S, a function Sres(R) → S(R⊗F K), and a map S(K) → Sres(F). Parameters: `SubfieldMap` (inclusion F→K if not automatic), `ExtensionBasis` (basis of K/F).
algorithm: Direct substitution using basis of K/F.

section: 112.13 Arithmetic Properties of Schemes and Points
description: For X a scheme over a number field K, Xm = X(L) where L is a p-adic completion, tests if X(L) is empty; returns an approximation to a local point if false. Parameters: `Smooth` (test only nonsingular points, plane curves only), `AssumeIrreducible`, `AssumeNonsingular`, `Verbose LocSol`. Special cases: (i) hyperelliptic curves over large odd residue field (Bruin generalisation of [MSS96]); (ii) hyperelliptic over small/even residue field (depth-first backtrack); (iii) nonsingular curves with possibly singular planar model (backtrack with Hensel criterion); (iv) cone-plus-quadric intersections in P3; (v) general schemes (primary decomposition then backtrack). **[Bru04]**

section: 112.13 Arithmetic Properties of Schemes and Points
description: For projective X over a number field or Q, tests local solvability at prime ideal p (or prime number p); returns true and an approximation if locally solvable. Same optional parameters as IsEmpty. **[Bru04]**

section: 112.13 Arithmetic Properties of Schemes and Points
description: Lift a p-adic point P in X(L) (L a completion) to precision n using quadratic Newton iteration; `Strict` (default true) causes an error if desired precision is unattainable.

section: 112.13 Arithmetic Properties of Schemes and Points
description: Same, but requires all input data over L: F is the defining equations of a scheme of dimension d, P is coordinates of an approximate point. Parameter `Strict` (default false).

section: 112.13 Arithmetic Properties of Schemes and Points
description: Search for points on scheme S over Q up to roughly height H; S in affine or non-weighted projective space. Parameters: `Dimension` (skip dimension computation), `Primes` (one or two small primes), `OnlyOne` (stop at first point).
algorithm: p-adic lift (find local points, lift p-adically, recognise globally via LLL lattice reduction).

signature: `map< X -> Y | F >` / `map< X -> Y | F, G >` / `map< X -> Y | u, F >`
description: Create map X → Y from sequence F of polynomials or rational functions on X (inverse from G if given; base-ring map u if given). F and G may each be a sequence of sequences for alternative defining sets. Parameters: `Check` (default true), `CheckInverse` (default true).
Create a map X → Y (from F) with birational inverse Y → X (from G); X and Y must have the same base ring.
The identity map X → X.
The constant map sending all points of X to point p of Y (coordinates Q).
Linear projection from projective space X to projective space Y omitting the first dim(X)−dim(Y) coordinates.
Projection of scheme X away from point p (default p = (1:0:…:0)) into projective space Q (if given).
Projection of X from nonsingular rational point p; returns the image, the projection map, and the image of the blowup of p.
Map X → Y from list L of function field elements used as projective coordinates; Y is a projective space of dimension #L−1 (created if omitted).
Shorthand for `ProjectiveMap([f,1],X,Y)`.
Affine scheme obtained by eliminating variables at indices V from the equations of affine scheme X; result lives in the affine subspace where those variables are 0.
The inverse of map f if inverse equations are stored; error otherwise.
Tests birationality of f; if so, returns a birational inverse computed via Groebner basis on affine graph ideals.
True iff f has an inverse stored.
Composition g ∘ f (g acts first; order matches `p @ g` then `@ f` notation); stored in factored form unless expanded.
The constituent maps composed to form f.
Restriction of map f to subscheme X of the domain; codomain is Y. Parameter `Check` (default true) controls subscheme relationship checks.
If phi is stored in factored form, return it in expanded form (may be expensive).
Return an expanded map with extra alternative equations reducing the base scheme to the maximal domain of definition; computationally heavy (Groebner basis on affine graph ideals).
Remove alternative equations in expanded phi that do not reduce the base scheme.
Remove common factors from the defining polynomials of phi.
Domain of map f.
Codomain of map f.
Sequence of functions defining map f (expands composites).
If f is an unexpanded composite: sequence of sequences of defining equations of each component; otherwise `DefiningPolynomials(f)`.
Sequence of functions defining the inverse of f (expands composites).
Factored form of inverse defining equations.
Polynomials of all alternate definitions of f.
Polynomials of all alternate inverse definitions of f.
The underlying polynomial-ring map; if F is the sequence of defining equations and x is the first variable of the codomain, then F[1] = x under AlgebraMap(f).
Degree of the homogeneous polynomials defining projective map f; minimum over all alternate defining sets.
True iff f and g have the same domain, codomain, and define the same rational map.
True iff f is defined at all points of its domain (no denominators).
True iff f has (or can easily compute) inverse defining equations; returns a recognised isomorphism map as second value.
True iff the closure of the image of f is the whole codomain.
True iff f is a regular map defined by linear polynomials.
True iff f is a map between affine spaces defined by polynomials of degree ≤ 1.
Image of point p under map f; p must not lie in the base scheme (except for curves with a function field, where the function field machinery is used). Handles sets and sequences of points.
algorithm: Function field for curve base-scheme points (from V2.17).

description: Preimage of point p; if f is an isomorphism with inverse g, returns g(p); otherwise returns Pullback(f, Cluster(p)).
Same as `Pullback(f,p)` except for isogenies between elliptic curves, where a single rational preimage point is returned.
The map of point sets X(K) → Y(K) induced by f; or X(m) → Y(m(u)) where u is the base-ring map.
Scheme in the domain of f given by pulling back the equations defining subscheme X of the codomain; contains the base scheme of f.
Scheme-theoretic closure of f(X∩U) in the codomain (U = complement of base scheme); stored with f for reuse. Multi-graded domain: X is saturated first.
Basis of degree-d polynomials in the codomain containing f(X); linear algebra over the field.
The subscheme of the domain where f is "naively" undefined (intersection of base schemes of all alternate equation sets).
Sequence of points in the base scheme of f defined over the base ring (or over extension field L); error if base scheme is not finite.
Map between projective closures of domain and codomain; if either is already projective it remains unchanged.
Set the map (given by polynomials S or by a scheme map m) as the projective closure map of affine space A.
Restriction of affine-to-projective map f to a rational map from its domain to the j-th standard affine patch of its codomain.
Restriction of projective-to-projective map f to a rational map from the i-th patch of its domain to the j-th patch of its codomain.
Automorphism of scheme X determined by polynomial sequence F; uses Groebner basis to find the inverse.
The identity map X → X.
True iff domain and range of f are equal.
True iff f is an automorphism; if so, returns f as a `MapAutSch` with its inverse computed.
algorithm: Groebner basis (if inverse not yet known).

description: Automorphism of affine space A from polynomial sequence F (computes inverse via Groebner basis).
Linear automorphism of affine space A from matrix M (acting from the right on points).
Translation of affine space A taking rational point p to the origin.
Automorphism of affine space A permuting coordinates according to permutation g.
Automorphism adding polynomial p (not involving x) to the first coordinate x of affine space A.
For affine linear endomorphism f (degree ≤ 1), returns a linear endomorphism ℓ and a translation t such that f = ℓ ∗ t.
The Nagata automorphism (u,v,w) ↦ (−u²w³−2uv²w²−2uvw+u−v⁴w−2v³, uw²+v²w+v, w) of affine 3-space A; not known to be tame.
Restriction to affine space A of the linear automorphism of its projective closure determined by matrix M; not regular on A in general.
Automorphism of projective space P from polynomial sequence F.
Matrix corresponding to linear automorphism f of a projective space.
Linear automorphism of projective space P from matrix M (acting on the left of coordinates).
Parent object (set) of all automorphisms of projective space P.
Automorphism group of P (P must be over a finite field) as a general linear group, together with a map matching group elements to automorphisms. Currently returns GL not PGL.
Unique automorphism of n-dim P mapping the n+2 standard simplex points to the n+2 linearly independent rational points in Q.
Automorphism mapping the n+1 standard coordinate points to the n+1 linearly independent rational points of Q (does not fix (1:…:1)).
A choice of linear automorphism of P taking rational point p to rational point q.
Linear automorphism of projective space P (containing X) taking (0:…:0:1) to rational point p; for affine X, takes p to the origin.
Standard quadratic transformation (x:y:…) ↦ (1/x:1/y:…) of projective space P; second form conjugates with the translation mapping points of Q to standard basis vectors.
Birational pullback of projective scheme X by the quadratic transformation (of the ambient P, or conjugated by Q); removes exceptional components in the total pullback.

Create a graph map from X to Y where I is a bihomogeneous ideal in a grevlex-ordered polynomial ring of n+m+2 variables defining the closure of the graph (first m+1 vars for domain, last n+1 for codomain). Parameter `Saturated` (default false); if false, I is domain-saturated internally via ColonIdeal.
Convert graph map f to a usual scheme map; if f is known invertible, inverse defining polynomials are added. May produce very high-degree polynomials and a large base scheme.
Returns whether graph map f is birationally invertible; if so, returns the inverse (as a reversed graph). Also performs codomain-saturation if needed.

section: 112.15 Tangent and Secant Varieties and Isomorphic Projections
description: Subscheme of the ambient whose closed points form the closure of the union of all tangent spaces to closed points of X. Parameter `PatchIndex` (default 0; if i>0, uses the i-th affine patch and takes the projective closure, which is faster).
algorithm: Projection from a 2n-dimensional ambient (tangent map image).

section: 112.15 Tangent and Secant Varieties and Isomorphic Projections
description: Fast test whether a given ambient point P lies in the tangent variety of projective X; much faster than computing the full tangent variety.

section: 112.15 Tangent and Secant Varieties and Isomorphic Projections
description: Subscheme of the ambient whose closed points form the closure of the union of all secant lines through distinct pairs of closed points of X. Parameter `PatchIndex` (default 0; if i>0 uses the i-th affine patch). Note: the union of secants is not necessarily closed even when X is projective.

section: 112.15 Tangent and Secant Varieties and Isomorphic Projections
description: Fast test whether ambient point P lies in the union of secants of projective X (not its closure); no affine-patch restriction.

section: 112.15 Tangent and Secant Varieties and Isomorphic Projections
description: Isomorphically project X (assumed reduced) to a linear subspace of dimension 2d+1 (or less if possible). Parameter `Verbose IsoToSub`. Returns the image scheme and the explicit projection map.
algorithm: Random point selection + IsInSecantVariety/IsInTangentVariety, iterated projection.

section: 112.15 Tangent and Secant Varieties and Isomorphic Projections
description: Embed a plane curve C as a nonsingular projective curve in P2 or P3 over the base field, using the function field machinery followed by IsomorphicProjectionToSubspace. Parameter `Verbose EmbCrv`. Returns image and map C → image.
Complete linear system on affine or projective space P of degree d; sections = all monomials of that degree (all polynomials of degree ≤ d for affine P); d must be positive.
Complete linear system of multi-degree d (sequence of degrees, one per grading); positive entries required.
Linear system generated by polynomials (homogeneous of common degree for projective P, or arbitrary degree for affine P) in sequence F; linearly dependent inputs trigger recomputation of a basis.
Monomials in the coordinate ring of the ambient of X having degree D[i] with respect to the i-th grading.
Linear system on the codomain of map f consisting of degree-d hypersurfaces containing f(S); S must be in the domain of f.
algorithm: Linear algebra (evaluating map on degree-d monomials).

description: Subsystem of L comprising hypersurfaces passing through point p or all points of sequence S. Nonrational points impose conditions as the union of their Galois conjugates.
Subsystem of L comprising hypersurfaces passing through p with multiplicity ≥ m.
Subsystem of L comprising elements containing scheme X; sections = polynomials in the defining ideal of X of the same degree as L.
Trace of L on scheme X: sections of L modulo the equations of X; result is still a linear system on the common ambient.
Subsystem of L generated by polynomials in sequence F (must already be sections of L); linearly dependent inputs trigger recomputation of a basis.
Subsystem of L determined by subspace V of the complete coefficient space of L.
The projective space on which L is defined.
True iff L and K are equal as linear subsystems of some common complete linear system; error if they lie in different complete systems.
True iff L is the complete linear system of polynomials of some degree.
True iff L has no base points.
Basis of sections of L (maximal linearly independent set of polynomials).
A random section of LS (small rational coefficients for Q; zero if no random generator).
Degree (or multi-degree) of the sections of L.
Projective dimension of L (= number of independent sections − 1).
Scheme defined by the sections of L; not tested for emptiness.
The hypersurface common to all elements of L (codimension-1 base locus).
L with its codimension-1 base locus removed (common factors of sections removed).
Sequence of base points of L if the base locus is finite.
Generic multiplicity of hypersurfaces of L at point p.
The vector space whose vectors are coefficient vectors of sections of L.
Map from the polynomial ring to the coefficient space: evaluates a polynomial f to its coefficient vector w.r.t. the basis of L.
Map from the coefficient space of L to the polynomial ring: maps a coefficient vector to the corresponding section of L.
Maximal subsystem of L not containing any hypersurface of L that lies in K.
Maximal subsystem of L comprising hypersurfaces not containing scheme X.
Linear system whose coefficient space is the intersection of coefficient spaces of L and K; error if they lie in different complete systems.
True iff scheme X occurs among the hypersurfaces of L.
True iff polynomial f is a section of L.
True iff the coefficient space of K is contained in that of L; error if not in a common system.
The pullback system f*L on the domain of map f, where L is a linear system on the codomain; produces the system of homaloids via substitution of the map equations.
The divisor group of variety X (type `DivSch`).
The variety of divisor group G.
True iff G1 and G2 are divisor groups of the same variety.
The divisor of a global function f: zeroes minus poles.
Same for f in the field of fractions of the coordinate ring of the ambient.
The effective divisor on X defined by f; subscheme of X with ideal generated by ideal(X) and f.
Effective divisor defined by the ideal generated by ideal(X) and the sequence Q. Parameters: `CheckSaturated`, `CheckDimension`, `UseCodimensionOnePart`.
Effective divisor defined by subscheme Y of X. Parameters as above.
Effective divisor defined by ideal I in the coordinate ring of the ambient of X (saturation should contain ideal(X)). Parameters as above.
Divisor given by a hyperplane section of projective variety X.
The zero divisor on X.
A canonical divisor on X (must be ordinary projective Gorenstein); uses the canonical sheaf and `SheafToDivisor`.
For invertible (locally free, rank 1) coherent sheaf S on variety X, return an effective Cartier divisor D such that S ≅ L(D).
For Q-rational D in prime factorisation, return the integral divisor obtained by rounding down all rational coefficients.
As above, rounding up.
D − RoundDownDivisor(D).
Find positive integer N such that N*D is integral; returns N*D and N.
Defining ideal of an effective integral divisor D.
Subscheme of the variety of effective Q-divisor D giving its support.
Ideal in the coordinate ring of the ambient defining the support of effective Q-divisor D.
Decompose D = A − B with A, B effective; returns A and B (not guaranteed relatively prime).
Current stored factorisation of D as a sequence of (ideal, rational multiplicity) pairs.
Simplify the current factorisation of D by combining terms with the same ideal.
Replace the factorisation of D with an equivalent one where all ideals are primary.
Replace the factorisation with an equivalent prime factorisation.
Multiplicity of prime divisor E in divisor D.
True iff D is the zero divisor.
True iff D is an integral divisor; may convert to prime factorisation.
True iff D is effective; may convert to prime factorisation.
True iff D is a prime divisor.
True iff the current factorisation of D has all ideals prime.
True iff D is integral and divisible by some n > 1; if so, returns the maximum such n.
Addition, subtraction, and negation of divisors; one argument may be a toric divisor for the same variety.
Multiply divisor D by integer n or rational r.
True iff D1 and D2 lie on the same variety and are equal.
True iff D is a canonical divisor; tests whether its sheaf is isomorphic to the canonical sheaf. Variety must be ordinary projective Gorenstein.
True iff D is anticanonical; tests whether its sheaf is isomorphic to the dual canonical sheaf.
True iff D = hyperplane-section divisor of degree d + canonical divisor; also returns d.
True iff D is a principal divisor; if so, returns f in FunctionField(ambient of X) with D = div(f). Uses Riemann-Roch space of D.
True iff D and E are linearly equivalent; if so, returns f with D = E + div(f).
Base locus of
Intersection pairing D1.D2 on a surface (dim X = 2); one divisor assumed Cartier.
Self-intersection number D.D on a surface.
Intersection number of D with a hyperplane divisor (first form) or with H (second form, equivalent to IntersectionNumber(D,H)); dim X = 2.
True iff D (a Q-Cartier effective divisor on projective surface X) has non-negative intersection with all effective divisors on X.
True iff D is nef and has positive self-intersection.
Sequence of prime divisor components of D with negative intersection with D.
Returns Q-divisors P (nef) and N (negative-definite support) such that D = P + N; Zariski decomposition on a surface.
The invertible sheaf corresponding to the divisor class of [D]; uses the coherent sheaf package.
Basis of the Riemann-Roch space of [D] as a sequence of function field elements.
algorithm: Coherent sheaf (or variant for non-effective D).

description: Riemann-Roch space as an abstract vector space V over the base field, with a map V → FunctionField.
True iff f lies in the Riemann-Roch space of D after coercion to the function field; if so, returns coordinates w.r.t. the RiemannRochBasis.
True iff there exists an effective divisor linearly equivalent to D; if so, returns such a divisor.
Iteratively eliminate variables appearing strictly linearly in some equation of scheme S; parameter `EliminationOrder`. Returns a map from the reduced scheme to S with inverse.

Given affine n-dimensional scheme over Q (defined by ≥ n equations) and a sequence of primes P, find liftable points modulo the primes. Parameters: `LinearElimination` (order for linear elimination), `ResultantElimination`, `FactorizationInResultant` (default true; apply squarefree factorisation to resultants).
algorithm: p-adic search with optional resultant/linear preprocessing.

description: Given a scheme S and a finite-field point P (from IsolatedPointsFinder) with maximal-rank Jacobian, lift via Newton's method and recognise over a number field via LLL. Returns (true, point) or false. Parameters: `LiftingBound` (default 10; number of Newton steps → precision p^(2^LiftingBound)), `DegreeBound` (default 32; max degree of number field to check), `DegreeList` (explicit degrees to try), `OptimizeFieldRep`.
algorithm: p-adic Newton lifting + LLL lattice recognition.

description: As IsolatedPointsLifter but returns a minimal polynomial for each coordinate separately rather than finding a common number field. Same parameters (no `OptimizeFieldRep`).
algorithm: p-adic Newton lifting + LLL per coordinate.

description: Given an ordinary projective scheme X and a module M over the coordinate ring of the ambient of X (annihilated by the defining ideal of X), returns the coherent sheaf defined by graded module M on scheme X.
Returns the structure sheaf OX for X, defined by the coordinate ring RX as a module.
Returns the Serre twist OX(n), whose associated graded module is RX(n) (see Section 5, Chapter II of **[Har77]**). OX(1) is the sheaf corresponding to the class of a hyperplane divisor H on X.

Returns the canonical sheaf KX for X. X must be equidimensional and locally Cohen-Macaulay (conditions are not checked). For non-singular varieties, KX is the highest alternating power of the sheaf of Kähler differentials. Acts as a dualising sheaf; see Section 7, Chapter III of **[Har77]** and Chapter 21 of **[Eis95]** for module-theoretic background.
algorithm: Computed from the dual complex to the minimal free resolution of the coordinate ring of X.

description: Returns the nth Serre twist KX(n) of the canonical sheaf. For a non-singular variety of dimension d, the map corresponding to KX(d − 1) is the important adjunction map.
Returns the nth Serre twist of S, S(n) ≅ S ⊗_{OX} OX(n). If M is a module giving S, then M(n) gives S(n).

Returns the sheaf of 1-differentials Ω¹_{X/k} on X. Computes the natural representing module from the embedding of X in projective space (see Section 8, Chapter II of **[Har77]**). Parameter `Maximize` (BoolElt, default `false`): if true, the maximal module is computed and used.
algorithm: Module from the embedding; Gröbner-basis-based maximisation if `Maximize := true`.

description: Returns the sheaf of tangent vectors for X. Computes the natural representing module from the embedding in projective space (see Section 8, Chapter II of **[Har77]**). Parameter `Maximize` (BoolElt, default `false`): if true, the maximal module is computed. Combined with `IsLocallyFree`, provides an alternative method for checking non-singularity on locally Cohen-Macaulay varieties (often faster for high-codimension varieties than the Jacobian method).

P must be ordinary projective 4-space P⁴ over a field. Returns the locally free rank-2 sheaf on P representing the Horrocks-Mumford bundle (see **[HM73]**). The vanishing locus of a general global section is a two-dimensional Abelian variety in P⁴.
Returns the graded module that was used to define sheaf S.
Returns the ordinary projective scheme X on which sheaf S is defined.

Computes and returns the maximal module M_max giving sheaf S. The nth graded piece of M_max equals the global sections of S(n) as a finite-dimensional vector space over k; thus M_max ≅ ⊕_{n∈Z} H⁰(X, S(n)) as in **[Har77]**. Assumes the exact support of S has no irreducible components of dimension 0 and no embedded associated primes of dimension 0 (a further assumption — not checked — is equidimensionality). The module M_max is stored so that it is only computed once.
algorithm: Double-dual computation over a Noether normalisation A of the supporting algebra. M is re-expressed as an A-module, M_max computed over A, then recovered as a module over k[x₀,…,xₙ] by tracking multiplication maps. Gröbner-basis-based.

description: Returns the submodule of M_max generated in degrees ≥ 0, that is ⊕_{n≥0} H⁰(X, S(n)).
Procedure: computes and stores (but does not return) the maximal module M_max of the sheaf S.

Returns the tensor product S ⊗_{OX} T of two sheaves on the same scheme X. Parameter `Maximize` (BoolElt, default `false`): if true, the maximal module of the result is computed and used as the defining module. Note: tensor products of maximal modules can be far from maximal; setting `Maximize := true` is usually advisable.
algorithm: Module tensor product; Gröbner-basis maximisation when `Maximize := true`.

description: Returns the nth tensor power of S if n > 0, the (−n)th tensor power of the dual of S if n < 0, and OX if n = 0. Parameter `Maximize` (BoolElt, default `true`). The rank of the module presentation grows rapidly with n, so `Maximize := true` (the default) is strongly recommended.
algorithm: Iterated module tensor product; maximisation by default.

description: Returns the dual sheaf Hom_{OX}(S, OX).

Returns the sheaf H = Hom_{OX}(S, T) together with a map taking a homogeneous element of degree d in the module of H to the degree-d sheaf homomorphism it represents. The defining module M_H = Hom(M_max, N_max) is the maximal module of H.
Returns the sheaf direct sum S ⊕ T of two sheaves on the same scheme X.
Returns the restriction of sheaf S (on scheme X) to a subscheme Y of X. Parameter `Check` (BoolElt, default `true`): if true, verifies Y is a subscheme of X.

Given sheaves S and T on the same scheme X and a homogeneous module homomorphism h (as returned by `IsHomogeneous`) between a representing module of S and a representing module of T: returns the sheaf homomorphism from S to T(d), where d is the degree of h.
Returns the domain sheaf of homomorphism f.
Returns the codomain sheaf of homomorphism f.
Returns the degree d of homomorphism f (the uniform grading shift).
Returns the underlying homogeneous graded module homomorphism of f.
Returns the kernel of f and its inclusion homomorphism into the domain of f.
For f of degree d with domain S and codomain T: returns the image I (a subsheaf of T(d)), the restriction g: S → I (degree d), and the inclusion h: I → T(d) (degree 0).
Returns the cokernel of f and the quotient homomorphism from the codomain to it. (Here f is treated as a homomorphism from S(d) ← T rather than S ← T(d).)

Given a sequence of sheaf homomorphisms [h1, …, hn], returns the composition h1 ∗ h2 ∗ … ∗ hn. The domain of h2 must equal the codomain of h1 etc., and the underlying module homomorphisms must be composable.

Given an invertible sheaf S on scheme X (invertibility not checked): returns the rational map from X into the projective space associated to S, and the image of the map on X. Parameter `graphmap` (BoolElt, default `false`): if true, forces return of a `MapSchGrph` even when a `MapSch` would otherwise be returned.
algorithm: Graph of the map computed from the relation matrix of the minimal presentation of M₀, saturated with respect to a domain variable; Gröbner-basis-based.

description: Given an ordinary projective scheme X and an ideal I defining an effective Cartier divisor D on X (of codimension 1, locally principal; conditions not checked): returns the invertible sheaf L(D) (see Section 6, Chapter 2 of **[Har77]**). Parameter `GetMax` (BoolElt, default `true`): if true, the maximal module of L(D) is computed and a basis for the Riemann-Roch space is stored in the attribute `rr_space` of S as a pair (sequence of numerators [G₁,…,Gₙ], denominator G).
algorithm: `ColonIdeal` and `Saturation` operations; if `GetMax := true`, r is chosen so that H¹(IX(m)) vanishes for m ≥ r. Gröbner-basis-based.

Returns true iff S is a locally free sheaf on X of constant rank, and if so, also returns the rank. Parameter `UseFitting` (BoolElt, default `true`): selects the algorithm (see below).
algorithm: **Default (Fitting ideal method, `UseFitting := true`):** checks that the saturation of the d-th Fitting ideal of M (or M_max) is the full ring and that the (d−1)-th lies in the saturated ideal of X. Can be extremely slow. **Alternative (`UseFitting := false`, étale stratification):** assumes X equidimensional, locally Cohen-Macaulay, and connected (not checked). Uses Serre's criterion **[Ser55]** via a Noether normalisation: checks that all intermediate Ext(M_max, R₀)-modules are finite length (equivalently, equality tests for Hilbert polynomials of cokernels in the dual complex of the free resolution of M_max over R₀). Applied inductively over a chain of closed subschemes of X (the "étale stratification"). The stratification is stored with X for reuse. Note: may fail in small positive characteristic if the generic separability condition fails, potentially giving wrong results.

description: For S and T coherent sheaves on the same base scheme X: returns true iff S ≅ T, and if so, returns an isomorphism.
algorithm: Hilbert polynomial check, then Betti number check on M_max and N_max (necessary conditions); then searches for an invertible matrix in the finite-dimensional space of homomorphisms between M_max and N_max. The invertible-matrix-in-a-linear-space problem is difficult in general; current implementation is described as "rather weak".

description: Returns true iff S ≅ T(d) for some Serre twist d, and if so, returns an isomorphism and d.
algorithm: As `IsIsomorphic`, with the "with twist" case also determining the possible d from Hilbert polynomial and Betti number checks.

description: Returns true iff the maximal graded module M_max of S is a Cohen-Macaulay module over the coordinate ring of X. A scheme X is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay iff its coordinate ring is Cohen-Macaulay, which holds iff the coordinate ring equals the maximal module of OX.
algorithm: Freeness check if the structure of M_max over a Noether normalisation is already known; otherwise depth calculation from a minimal free resolution of M_max over the coordinate ring of the ambient.

description: Returns the dimension over the base field of the r-th cohomology group of the n-th Serre twist of S: dim Hʳ(X, S(n)). Uses the maximal module if already computed; otherwise uses the defining module. Calling `SaturateSheaf` before cohomology computations is often faster in practice.
algorithm: Calls the equivalent function for the maximal module (or defining module); local cohomology / Ext computations over the coordinate ring.

description: `X` an ordinary projective surface in `Pⁿ_Q` (n ≥ 2), `P2` over Q. Returns `false` or `true` and a birational parametrization `P2 → X`. First finds a birational projection to a hypersurface in P³, then calls `ParametrizeProjectiveHypersurface`. May be slow if the projection introduces bad singularities.

`p ∈ Q[x,y,z]`, `F = Q(u,v)`. Finds birational parametrizations of the (not necessarily irreducible) affine hypersurface `p = 0` over Q. Returns a sequence of triples `(X, Y, Z) ∈ F³` with `p(X,Y,Z) = 0`, one per parametrizable irreducible component.
algorithm: Calls `ParametrizeProjectiveHypersurface` on each irreducible component after homogenization.

description: `X ⊂ P³_Q` an irreducible degree-2 hypersurface; `P2` a projective plane. Returns `false` if not parametrizable over Q; otherwise `true` and a birational parametrization.
algorithm: Find a rational point on `X` (equivalent to finding an isotropic vector for the quadric form; reduced to two quadrics in three variables using lattice methods) then project. Based on **[Sch98, §3.1]**.

description: `X` a birationally ruled surface over Q with rational pencil `φ: X → Pⁿ` (image a rational normal curve); `P2` a projective plane over Q. Returns `false` if not parametrizable over Q; `true` and a birational parametrization otherwise. Handles rational scrolls and conic bundles.
algorithm: Algorithm of **[Sch00]** for surfaces with a pencil.

description: `X` an anticanonically embedded Del Pezzo surface (type `Sch` or `Srfc`, degrees 1–9) over Q; `P2` a projective plane over Q. Returns `false` if not parametrizable; `true` and a birational parametrization otherwise. Blows down exceptional lines to degree ≥ 5 then invokes the degree-specific intrinsics in §116.4.3. For degrees 1–4 singular cases, uses direct methods.
algorithm: Blow-down of exceptional lines to high degree **[Sch98, §3.5, Man86]** then Lie algebra method for degrees 5–9.

description: Del Pezzo surface of degree `9 − d` obtained by blowing up the projective plane `P` in the `d` points given as list `L`, set `S`, or length-`d` zero-dimensional scheme `Z`. Embedded by the anticanonical system. Reports error if points not in sufficiently general position.
Creates the degree-3 Del Pezzo surface from homogeneous cubic `f` in a 4-variable polynomial ring (grevlex order), in the P³ defined by that ring. Reports error if not smooth.
algorithm: Checks smoothness; constructs as a surface in P³.

description: Returns true if `Y` (in ordinary projective space) is an abstract Del Pezzo. If so, also returns the anticanonical embedding `X` and the map `Y → X`. Computationally expensive in high-dimensional ambients.
Set verbose level for Del Pezzo parametrization (values: 0/false, 1/true, 2).
`X` a degree-9 Del Pezzo in P⁹ over Q (defined by 27 quadrics). Returns whether parametrizable over Q and, if so, a parametrization `P2 → X` given by cubic polynomials.

`X` a degree-8 Del Pezzo in P⁸ over a number field (defined by 20 quadrics). Handles three types: (1) P² blown up at one rational point (always parametrizable); (2i) product of two Galois twists of P¹ (parametrizable iff both trivial ↔ isomorphic to P¹×P¹); (2ii) Galois twist of P¹×P¹ with transitive Galois action (infinite family parametrized by Q*/Q*², isomorphic to `x₀²−ax₁² = x₂x₃`). Also handles singular (degenerate) degree-8 case. Returns boolean and (if parametrizable) a map by cubic (case 1) or degree-4 polynomials (case 2).
algorithm: Lie algebra method **[dGP]**; singular case detected from Lie algebra computation.

description: `X` a (possibly degenerate/singular) degree-7 Del Pezzo in P⁷ over a number field. Always parametrizable; returns parametrization directly via Lie algebra without reduction to higher degree.

`X` a non-singular degree-6 Del Pezzo in P⁶ over Q or a number field K (defined by 9 quadrics). The connected component of Aut(X) is a 2-dimensional torus over K; X is parametrizable iff it is the trivial principal homogeneous space of its torus (equiv., X has a K-point; local-global principle holds). Parameter `ExistenceOnly BoolElt` (default `false`; if `true`, only checks local solubility without constructing a parametrization — much faster). Returns boolean and (if parametrizable) a parametrization of minimal degree (3, 4, or 6 depending on torus type).
algorithm: Lie algebra method **[HS06]**; torus identification; norm equations over degree-3 or degree-6 extensions.

intrinsic: Degree6DelPezzoType2_1, Degree6DelPezzoType2_2, Degree6DelPezzoType2_3, Degree6DelPezzoType3, Degree6DelPezzoType4, Degree6DelPezzoType6
signature: `Degree6DelPezzoType2_1(K, pt)` / `Degree6DelPezzoType2_2(K, pt)` / `Degree6DelPezzoType2_3(K, pt)` / `Degree6DelPezzoType3(K, pt)` / `Degree6DelPezzoType4(K, K1, pt)` / `Degree6DelPezzoType6(K, pt)`
description: Construct the specific degree-6 Del Pezzo surface `X` whose (connected) automorphism group is the torus `T` corresponding to field data `K` (and `K1` for Type4), containing the K-point `pt` in P⁶. The torus types classify the 6 possible 2-dimensional tori over k. Point `pt` must satisfy non-vanishing conditions specific to each type.
algorithm: Explicit torus-type construction from field extensions **[HS06]**.

description: Variant of `ParametrizeDegree6DelPezzo` that also handles the degenerate (singular) degree-6 case. Tests for singularity first (can be slow); for singular X, projects from a singular point to P⁵ and parametrizes the resulting rational scroll. For non-singular X, calls `ParametrizeDegree6DelPezzo`.
algorithm: `ParametrizeDegree6DelPezzo` for smooth case; scroll parametrization via `ParametrizePencil` for singular case.

description: `X` a (possibly singular) degree-5 Del Pezzo in P⁵ over a number field. Always parametrizable; returns parametrization directly without reduction to higher degree. Uses a geometric projection method (since the automorphism group is finite, the Lie algebra method is not applicable).

`X` a degree-3 irreducible hypersurface in P³ with finitely many ADE singularities (not checked). `P2` a projective plane over the same number field. Returns `true` and a birational parametrization with inverse if `X` is parametrizable over the base field; otherwise `false`. If a rational singular point exists, projection from it gives an immediate parametrization. Otherwise, a small number of special root subsystem configurations are handled individually (including adapted Lie algebra method for toric cases).
algorithm: Projection from rational singular point; or case analysis for conjugate-singularity configurations including toric Lie algebra method.

description: As above but `X` is an irreducible complete intersection of 2 quadrics in P⁴ with finitely many ADE singularities. If a rational singular point exists, projection maps X to a line or conic bundle in P³ which is then parametrized. Otherwise, special case analysis for D₅/E₆ root subsystem configurations.
algorithm: Projection from rational singular point to scroll/conic bundle; or special case methods.

description: Local minimization of a cubic surface (homogeneous polynomial over Z) at prime `p`. Returns new equation and transformation matrix. No stability check. Verbose: `MinRedCubSurf` (max 2).
Global reduction of a cubic surface (homogeneous polynomial over Z). Returns reduced polynomial and transformation matrix. Verbose: `MinRedCubSurf` (max 2).
Global minimize-and-reduce of a smooth cubic surface over Z. Returns minimized-reduced polynomial and transformation matrix (applied to `f` gives a scalar multiple). Verbose: `MinRedCubSurf` (max 2).
Local minimization of a degree-4 Del Pezzo (pair of quadrics over Z) at prime `p`. Returns new pair of quadrics and transformation matrix. Verbose: `MinRedDeg4delPezzo` (max 1).
algorithm: Local minimization; calls `ReduceQuadrics` for reduction step.

description: Global minimize-and-reduce of a degree-4 Del Pezzo (pair of quadrics over Z). Returns reduced pair of quadrics and transformation matrix. Verbose: `MinRedDeg4delPezzo` (max 1).

For a Del Pezzo surface `S` of degree 3 or 4: calls the appropriate minimize-reduce routine above and converts the result to a Del Pezzo surface. Returns the new surface and the transformation matrix. Verbose: `MinRedCubSurf`, `MinRedDeg4delPezzo`.
For a smooth cubic surface `f` over a finite field: returns the number of points and the Swinnerton-Dyer number (conjugacy class in the Weyl group W(E₆)) of the Frobenius.

For smooth or singular cubic surfaces `f`, `g` over a finite field: returns true if isomorphic, plus a list of transformation matrices (one per isomorphism class over the algebraic closure). Parameter `UseLines BoolElt` (default `false`): if `false`, uses singularities of the Hessian; if `true`, uses the 135 intersection points of the 27 lines (slower, needed when Hessian degenerates). Works only over finite fields due to required large field extensions.
algorithm: Analysis of a canonical finite set of points (Hessian singularities or line intersections).

description: From a separable degree-6 polynomial `p`, constructs a cubic surface having the roots of `p` as hexahedral coefficients. The resulting surface has a Galois-invariant set of 12 lines. See **[EJ10]**.
For a separable degree-6 polynomial `p`: evaluates the Cobles quartic at the roots of `p`. The result is the discriminant of the hexahedral cubic surface (up to a square factor).
Computes the 5 Salmon invariants of cubic surface `f`. Second return: discriminant.
Computes the degree-100 skew invariant I₁₀₀. Its square lies in the Clebsch ring; it vanishes iff the cubic surface has an Eckardt point.
Constructs a cubic surface with prescribed Salmon invariants `inv`. Requires the last invariant to be non-zero.
Salmon's 4 linear covariants of the cubic surface `f`.
The 4 classical covariants of `f`: (1) Hessian, (2) T, (3) Θ, (4) degree-9 surface intersecting `f` in exactly its 27 lines.

Given a form `f`, a user-defined invariant `inv` of forms of the same degree in one fewer variable, and a point `p`: evaluates the corresponding contravariant of `f` at `p` via the Clebsch transfer principle. Used for building contravariant polynomials by interpolation.

Computes 3 contravariants of cubic surface `f` (via Clebsch transfer from plane cubic invariants S, T, discriminant): (1) hyperplanes where `f ∩ hyperplane` has j-invariant 0; (2) j-invariant 1728; (3) S²−6T (degree-12 dual surface — hyperplanes where intersection is singular).

Applies polynomial `d` to polynomial `c` as a differential operator (xᵢ acts as ∂/∂xᵢ). In invariant theory, `d` is a contravariant and `c` is a covariant; the result is a new covariant/contravariant or an invariant.

The divisor group of the toric variety X (a parent object for divisors; not computed as an abstract group).

The divisor on X given by vanishing of the ith coordinate.

If m is in the monomial lattice of X: the principal divisor corresponding to m. If m is a form on the ray lattice: the Weil divisor corresponding to m.
The zero divisor on X.
A divisor D on X whose class modulo linear equivalence equals m (an element of the divisor class group). Parameter `effective` (default `true`): if `true`, D is chosen effective when possible.
A divisor D on X whose class modulo linear equivalence equals m (an element of the Picard lattice or divisor class lattice). Parameter `effective` (default `true`).
The canonical divisor of X.
The class of the canonical divisor of X. Parameter `group` (default `"Pic"`; alternatives `"Cl"` for divisor class lattice, `"ClZ"` for divisor class group).
Standard arithmetic on divisors D, D1, D2 (n ∈ Q, v a point of the ambient toric lattice).
The toric variety on which D is defined.
The divisor group in which D lies.
The multiplicities on rays of the fan determining the invariant divisor D.
The sequence of monomial lattice elements determining D on the toric affine patches of X. Requires D to be Q-Cartier.
Returns `true` iff some integer multiple of D is Cartier.
Returns `true` iff D is Cartier.
Returns `true` iff D is a Weil divisor (integer coefficients).
Returns `true` iff D is ample.
Returns `true` iff D is nef.
Returns `true` iff D is big.
The class in the Picard lattice of the Q-Cartier divisor D.
The movable (mobile) part of D.
The dual fan to the rational polyhedron of sections of D on X; if X is complete, gives the fan of Proj of the ring of sections of positive powers of D.
Proj (as a toric variety) of the ring of sections of D; the map of underlying lattices determining X → Proj(D) is also returned.
The relative (sheaf) Proj of sections of D. If D is Q-Cartier: the identity; for non-Q-Cartier D: a partial Q-factorialisation.
If C is a codimension-1 face of the fan of X: the dual toric lattice vector representing intersection with the toric subvariety corresponding to C.
Returns `true` iff some integer multiple of D is principal.
Returns `true` iff D is principal.
Returns `true` iff D is linearly equivalent to a Cartier divisor; if so, a representative Cartier divisor is also returned.
Returns `true` iff D and E are linearly equivalent.
The monomial (or rational monomial if D is not effective) defining D.
The monomial in the Cox ring corresponding to the monomial lattice element v as a section of D.
The Riemann–Roch space of D as a polytope in the monomial lattice of X.
A basis of the Riemann–Roch space of D: a sequence of rational functions on X.
algorithm: Lattice points of the Riemann–Roch polytope.

description: The dimension of the Riemann–Roch space of D.
The graded cone of sections of multiples of D; integral points of the ith graded piece represent sections of i*D.
The integral polyhedron whose lattice points correspond to sections of D.
The Hilbert series Σ_{m≥0} dim H⁰(X, mD). Requires sections to be finite-dimensional (true e.g. for X projective).
algorithm: Generating function of lattice point counts in dilations of the Riemann–Roch polytope.

description: The Hilbert quasi-polynomial for D: a sequence [p₀,…,p_{r-1}] of polynomials of quasi-period r such that dim H⁰(X,mD) = p_s(k) where m = kr + s.
The first l+1 coefficients of the Hilbert series of D (from 0D up to lD).
The ith coefficient of the Hilbert series of D.

The rational map between toric varieties X and Y determined by the lattice map f between their underlying toric lattices (or, if f is omitted, the identity map, assuming X and Y have the same toric lattice). Displayed in Cox coordinate radical form.
The blowup of the toric variety X at the toric lattice point v; the natural map from the blowup to X is also returned.
algorithm: Star subdivision at v on the fan; **[Ful93]**.

description: The identity map on X.
Returns `true` iff the map f between toric varieties is regular (a morphism).
algorithm: Fan map condition: each cone of the source maps into a cone of the target; **[Dan78, Ful93]**.

description: A sequence of subschemes of the domain of f at which f is not defined. (Subschemes may be empty.)

description: The toric variety Y (with fan in the same lattice as that of X, where D is a divisor on X) such that Y resolves the rational map given by the linear system of D.
The Mori cone of X (as an abstract cone): the cone generated by numerical classes of torus-invariant curves on X.
The nef cone of X (as an abstract cone).
The extremal rays of the Mori cone of X.
The images of all extremal contractions of rays in the nef cone of X.
The toric variety that is the image of the ith extremal contraction; the contraction morphism is returned as a second value.
The toric divisor giving the ith extremal contraction (the pullback of an ample divisor on the image).
A string describing the ith extremal contraction of X (or a sequence of all, if i is omitted): e.g., `"divisorial (K.C<0)"`, `"flip"`, `"fibration (K.C<0)"`, `"map to point"`.
Returns `true` iff the ith extremal ray gives an extremal contraction to a variety of strictly lower dimension.
Returns `true` iff the ith extremal ray gives a divisorial contraction.
Returns `true` iff the ith extremal ray gives a small (flipping) contraction; in that case `Flip(X,i)` provides the flipped variety.
The flipped variety of the ith extremal contraction, assuming it is of flipping type.
The (generalised) flip of the morphism given by the Q-Cartier divisor D, assuming the morphism is small.
The weights of a Gₘ-action whose variation would give the flip of the ith extremal contraction, assuming it is of flipping type.

A sequence of all toric varieties encountered by making any sequence of extremal contractions (and, if necessary, the corresponding flip) from X; also a sequence of records describing each map. Parameter `type` (default `"terminal"`; also `"canonical"`, `"all"`): controls which extremal rays are considered (only those whose images have terminal, canonical, or arbitrary singularities).
algorithm: Toric minimal model program; **[Rei83]**, and Mori theory for toric varieties.

description: The subscheme of the toric variety X defined by the polynomial f from the Cox ring of X.
algorithm: Standard scheme construction in Magma; Gröbner basis calculations in Cox coordinates.

description: The subscheme of the toric variety X defined by the sequence Q of polynomials from the Cox ring of X.

Creates a conic from a sequence of 3 or 6 coefficients. `[a, b, c]` → aX² + bY² + cZ²; `[a, b, c, d, e, f]` → aX² + bY² + cZ² + dXY + eYZ + fXZ. Optional parameter `Ambient` specifies the ambient projective space.
Creates a conic from a symmetric 3×3 matrix M; the equation is [X, Y, Z] M [X, Y, Z]ᵀ. Optional parameter `Ambient`.
Returns the conic defined by the polynomial f in the projective plane X.
Returns `true` iff the scheme S is a nonsingular plane curve of degree 2; if so, also returns a curve of type `CrvCon` with the same defining polynomial.
Returns the rational curve defined by the linear polynomial f in the projective plane X.
Returns `true` iff S is defined by a linear polynomial in some P²; if so, returns a curve of type `CrvRat` with the same defining polynomial.
Returns the defining polynomial of the conic or rational curve C.
Returns the defining ideal of the conic or rational curve C.
Returns the base ring of the curve C.
Returns the category `CrvRat` or `CrvCon`; both are special subtypes of `CrvPln`, which are subtypes of `Crv`.

Returns the discriminant of conic C. For equation a₁₁x² + a₁₂xy + a₁₃xz + a₂₂y² + a₂₃yz + a₃₃z² = 0, the discriminant is 4a₁₁a₂₂a₃₃ − a₁₁a²₂₃ − a²₁₂a₃₃ + a₁₂a₁₃a₂₃ − a²₁₃a₂₂. Over rings where 2 is invertible this equals 1/2 times the determinant of the associated symmetric matrix.

Returns the Legendre polynomial of C — a diagonalised defining polynomial of the form ax² + by² + cz². Once computed, it is stored as an attribute. The transformation matrix defining the isomorphism from C to the Legendre model is returned as the second value.
algorithm: Diagonalisation by completing the square / congruence reduction.

description: Returns the reduced Legendre polynomial of C (C must be over Q or Z) — a diagonalised integral polynomial with pairwise coprime, square-free coefficients. The transformation matrix is returned as the second value.
algorithm: Reduction of Legendre form by removing squares and cross-prime factors.

description: Returns the Legendre model of C — an isomorphic curve of the form ax² + by² + cz² = 0 — together with an isomorphism to this model.

Returns the reduced Legendre model of C (C must be over Q or Z) — a curve in diagonal form ax² + by² + cz² = 0 with pairwise coprime, square-free coefficients — together with the isomorphism from C to this model.
Returns a conic whose defining-polynomial matrix has smaller discriminant than that of C (where possible), plus a map from the new conic to C.
algorithm: Minimisation stage of Simon's algorithm **[Sim05]**, as used in `HasRationalPoint`.

description: Given a conic C over Q, returns the sequence of finite ramified primes — those at which C has intrinsic locally singular reduction. The parity of the sequence length encodes ramification at the infinite prime (not included in the returned sequence).
Given rational numbers or integers a, b and a prime p, returns 1 if the quadratic form ax² + by² − z² represents zero over Q_p and −1 otherwise.
algorithm: Classical norm residue symbol computation; see **[Cas78]**.

description: Computes the Hilbert symbol (a, b)_p, where a, b are elements of a number field and p is either a prime number (if a, b ∈ Q) or a prime ideal. Parameter `Al` (`MonStgElt`, default `"NormResidueSymbol"`): by default uses `NormResidueSymbol`; set to `"Evaluate"` to use the number-field algorithm instead.

C must be defined over Z, Q, a finite field, a number field, or a rational function field over a finite field of odd characteristic. Returns `true` iff a point on C exists, and if so also returns one such point.
algorithm: Over Q/Z: Simon **[Sim05]**; over number fields: Lagrange-variant lattice reduction; over function fields: **[CR06]**; over finite fields: random-x search.

description: Same base field requirements as `HasRationalPoint`. Returns a rational point on C over its base ring; errors if no such point exists.

Returns a randomly selected rational point of C. Parameter `Bound` (`RngIntElt`, default 10⁹): upper bound on the random integers fed to the parametrisation. Parameter `Reduce` (`BoolElt`, default `false`): if `true`, applies point reduction (§119.5.2) to the result.
algorithm: Parametrisation evaluation at a random parameter value.

description: For C over Q or a finite field: returns an indexed set of rational points. Over Q, parameter `Bound` (`RngIntElt`) must be given; returns points whose integral coordinates on the reduced Legendre model are bounded by `Bound`.
algorithm: Naive bounded search on the reduced Legendre model (over Q); enumeration (over finite fields).

description: Returns `true` iff the projective point p on a conic satisfies Holzer's bounds on the reduced Legendre model. If C is not already a reduced Legendre model, the test is done after passing to that model.
Returns a Holzer-reduced point derived from p.
Given a curve C of genus zero, returns a conic determined by the anti-canonical embedding (Riemann–Roch space of −K_C, dimension 3, degree 2 functions).
algorithm: Anti-canonical embedding via Riemann–Roch; see **[Sim05]** for the Q case.

description: Optimised routine for C defined over Z or Q. Returns a 3×3 matrix M such that for a point (x₀ : y₀ : z₀) on C, the point (x₁ : y₁ : z₁) = (x₀ : y₀ : z₀)M satisfies y₁² = x₁z₁ (i.e. lies on the standard conic). Action is on the right, consistently with Magma's scheme-map convention.
algorithm: Parametrisation via 2-uple embedding and change of variables; Simon **[Sim05]**.

description: Returns an isomorphism of schemes P → C (P a projective line, optionally specified; a rational point or place p may be specified to pin the parametrisation). If no p is given, the base field must be one of the types accepted by `HasRationalPoint`. Errors if C has no rational points.
algorithm: Conic parametrisation algorithm: 2-uple embedding composed with parametrisation matrix; over Q uses Simon **[Sim05]**.

description: As `Parametrization`, but for plane curves with only ordinary singularities (see §114.3.6); uses a more specialised procedure that is faster and can produce nicer parametrisations. The optional argument I is the adjoint ideal of C (avoids recomputation if already known).
algorithm: Adjoint ideal / ordinary-singularity method (faster than general function field machinery).

description: For non-singular rational curves of degree d in ordinary d-dimensional projective space (d ≥ 1): returns an isomorphism from P¹ (d odd) or a plane conic (d even) to C. Irreducibility of C is not checked.
algorithm: Adjoint maps; no function field machinery.

description: Given a rational curve C and two indexed sets S = {p₀, p₁, p∞} and T = {q₀, q₁, q∞} of distinct points over the base ring, returns the unique automorphism of C taking pᵢ to qᵢ.
Returns the quaternion algebra in which automorphisms of the conic C can be represented.
algorithm: Quaternion algebra construction from Legendre coefficients; see **[Lam73]**, **[Vig80]**.

description: Given a conic C and a unit a of the quaternion algebra associated to C, returns the automorphism of C corresponding to a (conjugation action on the trace-zero part).
Creates the elliptic curve E over K from a sequence of Weierstrass coefficients of length 2 (short form y² = x³ + ax + b) or 5 (general Weierstrass form). The discriminant must be nonzero.
Creates the elliptic curve defined by y² + h(x)y = f(x), or y² = f(x) if h is omitted. f must be monic of degree 3; h must have degree at most 1.
Creates an elliptic curve with given j-invariant: y² + y = x³ if j = 0 (char ≠ 3); y² = x³ + x if j = 1728 (or j = 0, char 3); otherwise y² + xy = x³ − (36/(j−1728))x − 1/(j−1728).
algorithm: Explicit Weierstrass model by j-invariant formula.

description: Given a genus-1 scheme C with an easily recognised rational point, returns an elliptic curve E and a birational map C → E. Handles hyperelliptic curves of genus 1 (f of degree 3 or 4), nonsingular plane cubics (checks for rational flex), and singular plane quartics with a unique cusp. Verbose parameter `EllModel` (max 3).
algorithm: Recognises rational branch points or points at infinity; uses linear transformations or Riemann–Roch as needed.

description: Given a genus-1 scheme C and a nonsingular rational point P, returns E and a birational map sending P to the origin. For degree-3 curves (char ≠ 2, 3): uses a linear transform if P is a flex; otherwise Nagell's algorithm **[Nag28, Cas91]**. For degree-4 curves with unique cusp: construction from **[Cas91]**. Otherwise: Riemann–Roch (potentially expensive).

Given a plane genus-1 curve C and a place pl of degree 1, returns E and a birational map via a Riemann–Roch computation (potentially expensive; differs from the point version which uses special methods for degree 3 or 4).
Given a finite field K, returns a representative supersingular elliptic curve over K.
Returns true if the given sequence of ring elements defines an elliptic curve (discriminant nonzero); also returns the elliptic curve when true.
Given a hyperelliptic curve C, returns true if C has degree 3; also returns the elliptic curve and isomorphisms to/from it. *Deprecated — use `Degree(C) eq 3` and `EllipticCurve(C)` instead.*
Given E over k and a field K that is an extension of k, returns E′ over K using the natural inclusion of k in K to map coefficients.
Given E over k and a field K, returns E′ over K using the standard coercion (useful when no ring homomorphism k → K is available, e.g. k = Q and K a finite field).
Given E over k and a ring map h : k → K, returns E′ over K by applying h to the coefficients.
Given E over a finite field K, returns the base extension of E to the degree n extension of K.
Returns an isomorphic E′ in simplified Weierstrass form y² = x³ + ax + b. Does not apply in characteristic 2 or 3.
algorithm: Change of variables to short Weierstrass form.

description: For E over a number field K (including Q), returns an isomorphic E′ over K with integral coefficients.
Returns a simplified model of E. Over Q: same as MinimalModel. In characteristic ≠ 2, 3: same as WeierstrassModel. In characteristic 2 or 3: see chapter 4 of **[Con99]**.
algorithm: Depends on base field; see **[Con99]** for char 2, 3.

description: For E over Q or a number field K with class number 1, returns a global minimal model E′ (integral model with minimal discriminant valuation at all non-zero prime ideals). Errors if no global minimal model exists.

For E over a number field K and a prime ideal P (or integer prime p when K = Q), returns an E′ isomorphic to E that is minimal at P. Parameter `UseGeneratorAsUniformiser` (default false): if true and P is principal, uses an ideal generator as uniformiser to keep the model integral at other primes.
algorithm: Local minimisation at P using a uniformiser.

description: Returns true iff E is in simplified Weierstrass form.
Returns true iff E is an integral model.
Returns true iff E is a simplified model.
Returns true iff E is a minimal model.
For E over a number field and P a prime ideal of an order of the coefficient ring, returns true iff the defining coefficients of E have non-negative valuation at P.
Returns the quadratic twist of E by d. Isomorphic to E iff (char 2 and Tr(d) = 0) or (char ≠ 2 and d is a square). Does not always work in characteristic 2.
For E over a finite field, returns a quadratic twist (a non-isomorphic curve whose trace is the negation of Trace(E)).
For E over a finite field, returns the sequence of all non-isomorphic quadratic twists; the first entry is isomorphic to E.
For E over a finite field K, returns the sequence of all non-isomorphic elliptic curves over K that are isomorphic to E over some extension field; the first entry is isomorphic to E.
algorithm: Classification by j-invariant and automorphism group.

description: Returns true iff E and F are isomorphic over an extension field (tests only j-invariants).
Returns true iff E and F are isomorphic over a quadratic extension; if so, also returns d such that F is isomorphic to `QuadraticTwist(E, d)`.

For a rational elliptic curve E, determines the minimal quadratic twist. Handles odd primes of bad reduction by iteratively twisting by p if that reduces the discriminant; handles p = 2 and sign by minimising the 2-adic valuation of the conductor, then choosing the twist making (−1)^(v₂(c₆)) odd(c₆) ≡ 3 (mod 4). Returns also the integer d by which E was twisted.
algorithm: Local minimisation prime-by-prime; see algorithm description in text.

description: Returns the sequence [a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄, a₆] of Weierstrass coefficients of E (always 5 elements, even if E was defined by a length-2 sequence).
Returns [b₂, b₄, b₆, b₈] where b₂ = a₁² + 4a₂, b₄ = a₁a₃ + 2a₄, b₆ = a₃² + 4a₆, b₈ = a₁²a₆ + 4a₂a₆ − a₁a₃a₄ + a₂a₃² − a₄².
Returns [c₄, c₆] where c₄ = b₂² − 24b₄, c₆ = −b₂³ + 36b₂b₄ − 216b₆.
Returns the discriminant Δ = −b₂²b₈ − 8b₄³ − 27b₆² + 9b₂b₄b₆; also satisfies 1728Δ = c₄³ − c₆².
Returns the j-invariant j = c₄³/Δ. Two curves over the same base field are isomorphic over some extension iff their j-invariants are equal.
Returns the polynomials x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆ and a₁x + a₃ derived from the invariants of E.
Returns the category `CrvEll` of elliptic curves.
The base ring of E; the parent of its coefficients and the coefficient ring of the default point set.
Returns true iff E and F are defined over the same ring and have the same coefficients.
Logical negation of eq.
Returns true iff there exists an isomorphism E → F over the base field; if so, also returns the isomorphism. Requires the ability to take roots in the base field.
For E and F over Q or a finite field, returns true iff E and F are isogenous over that field. For Q: also returns the isogeny. For finite fields: uses point counting (no isogeny returned).
algorithm: Over Q: isogeny search; over finite fields: point counting.

description: Returns the homogeneous defining polynomial for E.

Returns the n-th division polynomial as a univariate polynomial over the base ring of E. For even n, has multiplicity two at the nonzero 2-torsion points; the second return value is this polynomial divided by the 2-torsion polynomial; the third return is the cofactor (equal to the 2-torsion polynomial if n even, else 1). If a polynomial g is passed as third argument, computation is done efficiently modulo g.
Returns the multivariate 2-torsion polynomial 2y + a₁x + a₃ of E as a bivariate polynomial.
Creates the subgroup scheme of G (which may be an elliptic curve) defined by univariate polynomial f. No checking that the rational points actually form a group.
Returns the subgroup scheme of n-torsion points of the subgroup scheme G (G may be an elliptic curve).
Returns `SchGrpEll`, the category of elliptic curve subgroup schemes.
Returns the elliptic curve E of which G is a subgroup scheme.
Returns the base ring of G (same as the base ring of its curve).
