chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Cassels–Tate pairing on 2-coverings of E over **Q**, a number field, or F(t). C and D must be y²=q(x) with q quartic, locally solvable. Returns value in Z/2Z. Verbose: `CasselsTate` (max 2).
algorithm: Algorithms of Steve Donnelly (forthcoming paper); over **Q** reduces to solving a conic.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Pairing between a 4-covering C (intersection of two quadrics in P³) and a 2-covering D, over **Q**. Returns Z/2Z.
algorithm: Donnelly; key step is solving a conic over a degree-4 field.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: 4-descent on y²=f(x) or a hyperelliptic curve C. Returns a set of 4-coverings (intersections of quadrics). Parameters: `RemoveTorsion` (default false), `IgnoreRealSolubility` (default false), `RemoveGensEC`, `RemoveGensHC`, verbose flags `FourDescent`/`LocalQuartic`/`MinimiseFD`/`QISearch`/`ReduceFD`/`QuotientFD`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Associated elliptic and hyperelliptic curves for a quadric intersection `qi`, with maps to them. Optional: `E`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Quadric intersection in P³ from a pair of symmetric 4×4 matrices F.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Write an elliptic curve E or hyperelliptic curve C as a quadric intersection.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Determines whether C is a quadric intersection (in P³ with two quadric equations), also returning the pair of matrices.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Search for points on quadric intersection C of naive height ≤ B; asymptotic time O(B^{2/3}). Parameters: `OnlyOne` (default false), `ExactBound` (default false), verbose `QISearch`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Pre-images on a two-covering (hyperelliptic curve or quartic) of a point on the elliptic curve. Faster than generic machinery.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Pre-images on a four-covering (quadric intersection) of a point on the associated elliptic or hyperelliptic curve.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Further 2-descent on a curve C from `FourDescent`. Returns sequence of 8-descendant curves D and maps D→C. Parameters: `BadPrimesHypothesis` (default false), `DontTestLocalSolvabilityAt` (default {}), `StopWhenFoundPoint` (default false), verbose `EightDescent`/`LegendresMethod`. Requires class group / unit computations in degree 4 (and sometimes degree 8) number fields.
algorithm: Tom Fisher's 8-descent algorithm (Magma 2.17); partly replaces Stamminger.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: 3-Selmer group elements as plane cubics with covering maps. Returns one cubic per inverse pair of nontrivial elements, with covering maps. Parameters: `Method` (default `"HessePencil"`), verbose `Selmer`/`ThreeDescent`.
algorithm: Calls `ThreeSelmerGroup` then `ThreeDescentCubic` on each element **[SS04, CFO+08, CFO+09, CFO+]**.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: 3-Selmer group of E/Q as an abelian group with map to the natural affine algebra. Parameters: `ThreeTorsPts`, `MethodForFinalStep` (default `"UseSUnits"`; alternatives `"Heuristic"`, `"FindCubeRoots"`), `CompareMethods` (default false), verbose `Selmer`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For E/Q and element α in the 3-Selmer group: returns a plane cubic C and map C→E. Parameters: `ThreeTorsPts`, `Method` (default `"HessePencil"`; alternatives `"FlexAlgebra"`, `"SegreEmbedding"`), verbose `ThreeDescent`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Descent by 3-isogenies for E/Q admitting Q-rational 3-isogeny E→E1. Returns: cubics for Sel(E→E1), maps to E1, cubics for dual Sel(E1→E), maps to E, the isogeny. Optional: `Isog`, verbose.
algorithm: Calls `ThreeIsogenySelmerGroups` then `ThreeIsogenyDescentCubic`; only quadratic field computations.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Selmer groups for E→E1 and dual E1→E isogenies. Returns: group and map for E→E1, group and map for E1→E, the isogeny. Optional: `Isog`.
algorithm: Selmer group computation in quadratic fields.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For a degree-3 isogeny φ between elliptic curves over Q and element α ∈ H¹(Q, E[φ]): returns a plane cubic C and covering map C→E of degree 3. Verbose `ThreeDescent`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Full 3-descent by first and second 3-isogeny descents; restricts to cubic extensions (sextic fields not needed). Verbose `Selmer`.
algorithm: Composition of two 3-isogeny descents **[SS04, CFO+08, CFO+09, CFO+]**.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Jacobian of a nonsingular projective plane cubic C over **Q** as an elliptic curve.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For E/Q and plane cubic C with same invariants as E: returns element α in the algebra A associated to the 3-Selmer group representing the same class. α is only determined up to inverse.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Sum in H¹(Q, E[3]) of two plane cubics with the same invariants (same Jacobian). Returns another plane cubic. Parameters: `E`, `ReturnBoth` (default false; if true returns both possible cubics).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Classifies the Galois action on E[3]. Possible values: `"Generic"`, `"2Sylow"`, `"Dihedral"`, `"Generic3Isogeny"`, `"Z/3Z-nonsplit"`, `"mu3-nonsplit"`, `"Diagonal"`, `"mu3+Z/3Z"`.
algorithm: Group-theoretic classification of the mod-3 representation.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Tuple of one representative from each Galois orbit in E[3] \ O, defined over the appropriate field. Parameter: `OptimisedRep` (default true).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For plane cubic C with same invariants as E: tuple of matrices M_i corresponding to `ThreeTorsionPoints`, describing the action-by-translation on C in PGL3.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: From a 2-covering and a 3-covering of E (curves or genus one models): the 6-covering representing their sum in the 6-Selmer group, plus covering map C6→C3.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: From a 3-covering and a 4-covering of E: two 12-coverings representing their sum and difference in the 12-Selmer group, plus covering maps C12→C4.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For plane cubic C over Q: returns sequence of curves in P⁸ (defined by 27 quadrics) and degree-9 maps making them 3-coverings of C (the 3-Selmer set of C). Parameters: `ExtraReduction` (default 10), verbose `Selmer`/`ComputeL`. Requires Galois to act transitively on flex points; otherwise use `pIsogenyDescent`.
algorithm: Creutz's second 3-descent algorithm **[Cre10]**; class group/unit computations in the degree-9 étale algebra of flex points.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Computes the 3-rank of the 3-Selmer set of plane cubic C over Q. Returns −1 if the set is empty (C(Q) = ∅ and class is not 3-divisible in Sha).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: φ-descent on E/Q for p ∈ {5,7} using Fisher's algorithm. Kernel generated by Q-rational p-torsion point P, or the point is chosen by specifying p, or by giving a Q-rational point λ on X₁(p). Returns: ranks of φ- and φ∨-Selmer groups, sequence of genus-one normal curves of degree p representing inverse pairs of nontrivial elements of φ∨-Selmer group, and the isogenous curve (plus E if λ was given).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Isogeny descent on genus-one normal curve C of prime degree p ∈ {3,5}. C must be a plane cubic (p=3) or intersection of 5 quadrics in P⁴ with flex points on coordinate hyperplanes. Verbose `Selmer`. Returns: sequence of genus-one normal curves representing the φ-Selmer set, and covering maps.
algorithm: Second isogeny descent, algorithm of Creutz **[Cre10, CM12]**.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Determines the F_p-dimension of the "fake" φ-Selmer set of genus-one normal curve C of degree p ∈ {3,5,7}. Returns −1 if empty. Verbose `Selmer`. For p=7, only the fake Selmer set is computable.
algorithm: Creutz **[Cre10, CM12]**; feasible for p=7 (no coverings produced).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Attempts to find a point on rank-1 rational E using Heegner points. Returns true and the point, or false. Parameters: `NaiveSearch` (default 1000), `Discriminant`, `Cover` (2- or 4-cover), `DescentPossible` (default true), `IsogenyPossible` (default true), `Traces`, verbose `Heegner`. Assumes Manin constant = 1.
algorithm: Gross–Zagier method **[GZ86]**; tricks due to Watkins.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Utility versions: input is a hyperelliptic curve (quartic), quartic polynomial, or quadric intersection. Calls `HeegnerPoint` on the underlying elliptic curve then maps back to the covering. Parameters: `NaiveSearch` (default 10000), `Discriminant`, `Traces`, verbose.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Modular parametrization ∫_z^∞ f_E(τ)dτ for a point z in the upper half-plane. With bound B, uses first B terms of q-expansion. Optional `Traces`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Same as above for an array Z of complex points.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
signature: `ModularParametrization(E, f, B : parameters)` / `ModularParametrization(E, f : parameters)` / `ModularParametrization(E, F, B : parameters)` / `ModularParametrization(E, F : parameters)`
description: Modular parametrization at a positive definite binary quadratic form f (or array F). Optional `Precision`, `Traces`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Negative fundamental discriminants in range [lo, hi] satisfying the Heegner hypothesis for E. Parameters: `Fundamental` (default false), `Strong` (default false).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For E of conductor N and negative discriminant D satisfying the Heegner hypothesis: representatives for CM points on X₀(N). Returns sequence of 3-tuples (Q, m, T) where Q is a quadratic form, m a multiplicity, T a torsion point; the sum of m(φ(Q)+T) gives a Heegner point. Parameters: `UsePairing`, `UseAtkinLehner` (default true), `Use_wQ` (default true), `IgnoreTorsion` (default false). Requires ManinConstant = 1.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For level N and discriminant D: sequence of binary quadratic forms for Heegner points. Parameter: `AtkinLehner` (default []).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: (Conjectural) Manin constant of rational E; in most cases 1.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For integer Q with gcd(Q, N/Q)=1: torsion point corresponding to the period ∫_{i∞}^{w_Q(i∞)} f_E(τ)dτ.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For E/Q and suitable discriminant D: images on E of CM points on X₀(N) associated to D. Returns tuple ⟨p_D, m⟩ where p_D is an irreducible polynomial (x-coordinates lie in the ring class field) and m is the multiplicity. Also returns one conjugate point. Parameters: `ReturnPoint` (default false), `Precision` (default 100), verbose. Not rigorous (involves complex recognition).
algorithm: **[GZ86]**; heuristic check by reduction mod small primes.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Sequence of periods of the Weierstrass ℘-function for rational E; first element is the real period. Accepts non-minimal model. Parameter: `Precision`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: From two complex numbers ω₁, ω₂ (with ω₂/ω₁ in upper half-plane, corresponding to an integral model), returns the minimal model over Q. Parameter: `Epsilon` (default 0.001; proximity to integers for −27c₄ and −54c₆).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Real period of the Weierstrass ℘-function for E to `Precision` digits.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For rational E and complex z: pair [℘(z), ℘′(z)]. For small precision uses algorithm from **[Coh93]**; for high precision uses Newton iteration on EllipticLogarithm. Returns sequence (not a point).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For rational E and sequence S = [p, q]: elliptic exponential of p·RealPeriod + q·imaginary period.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Elliptic logarithm φ(P) of point P (as complex number), with −ω₁/2 ≤ Re(φ) < ω₁/2 and −ω₂/2 ≤ Im(φ) < ω₂/2. Accepts non-minimal model. Parameter: `Precision`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For E and sequence S = [z₁, z₂] approximating a point P: elliptic logarithm φ(P). Parameters: `Precision`, `Check` (default true).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: p-adic elliptic logarithm of P at prime p to `Precision` (default 50) digits. Order of P must not be a power of p.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Global root number of E/Q: sign in the functional equation of L(E, s). Product of local root numbers at bad primes.
algorithm: Local root numbers via Halberstadt's method; product formula.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Local root number at prime p. For p > 3: straightforward from valuation of discriminant. For p = 2, 3: careful analysis of reduction type.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Analytic rank of rational E: heuristic, computes derivatives of L(E,s) at s=1 until one is nonzero; returns rank and first nonzero L^{(r)}(1)/r!. Parameter: `Precision` (default 5; time increases sharply above 50 digits). Verbose `AnalyticRank`.
algorithm: L-function derivatives via local power series; heuristic.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Assuming BSD, approximation to Reg(E) ·

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Same but taking the precomputed first nonzero L^{(r)}(1)/r! = v.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Modular degree deg(φ) of rational E via L(Sym²E, 2). Formula: deg(φ) = L(Sym²E,2)/(2π·Ω)·(Nc²)·∏ E_p(2). Assumes Manin constant = 1 (except cases noted in **[SW02]**). Verbose `ModularDegree`.
algorithm: Algorithm of **[Wat02]**: real-number approximations converging to an integer.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: All integral points on E/Q modulo negation, plus representations in terms of a Mordell–Weil basis. Parameters: `FBasis` (precomputed free generators), `SafetyFactor` (extends the final search).
algorithm: Linear forms in elliptic logarithms; `MordellWeilShaInformation` for generators.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: All S-integral points on E/Q modulo negation. Same parameters as `IntegralPoints`.
algorithm: Linear forms in elliptic logarithms + p-adic logarithms for p ∈ S.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: All integral points (modulo negation) on y² = ax⁴+bx³+cx²+dx+e where e is a square. Input: sequence [a,b,c,d,e].
algorithm: Via `IntegralPoints` on the associated elliptic curve.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: All integral points on the quartic y² = ax⁴+bx³+cx²+dx+e given a rational point P = [x,y].
algorithm: As above with the given point as starting generator.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: S-integral points on y² = ax⁴+bx³+cx²+dx+e (a must be a square) for set S of primes.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: S-integral points on C : ay² = bx⁴+cx²+d for set S; requires C nonsingular. Input: [a,b,c,d].

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: S-integral points on C : ay³+bx³+cxy+d = 0 for set S; requires C nonsingular. Input: [a,b,c,d].
algorithm: Linear forms in elliptic logarithms for genus-1 cubic.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Returns a database object. Parameter: `BufferSize` (default 10000).

description: Sets the internal disk-read buffer to n bytes.

description: Largest conductor stored in D.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Smallest and largest conductors stored.

description: Total number of curves in D.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Number of curves with conductor N.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Number of curves in the i-th isogeny class for conductor N.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Number of isogeny classes for conductor N.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
signature: `EllipticCurve(D, N, I, J)` / `EllipticCurve(D, N, S, J)`
description: J-th curve of isogeny class I (integer or label string) for conductor N.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Curve with Cremona label S (e.g. `"101a"` or `"101a1"`).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: A random curve from D.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Cremona label of E (e.g. `"101a1"`). E must be over Q with conductor in range.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Sequence of curves in isogeny class I (or label S) for conductor N.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: All curves for conductor N.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Curves with label S (conductor or conductor+class).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: All curves in D (slow; prefer iteration).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Conductor of E defined over a number field (computed by `LocalInformation`).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Places of K of bad reduction for E (dividing discriminant of E).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Places of L of bad reduction for E/K where K ⊆ L.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Tate's algorithm at prime ideal P: returns tuple ⟨P, v_P(d), f_P, c_P, KodairaSymbol, s⟩ and a local minimal model E_min. Optional: `UseGeneratorAsUniformiser` (default false).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Sequence of `LocalInformation(E, P)` tuples for all P dividing discriminant of E.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Reduction of E (integral at p, good reduction at p) to an elliptic curve over the residue field of p, plus the reduction map.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For E over a number field: whether E has CM, plus discriminant of the CM order if yes. Not suited to very high-degree j-invariants or discriminants beyond a few thousand.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Bound on the torsion subgroup size by looking at the first n non-inert primes of low ramification degree with good reduction.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: p-power torsion of E over its base field as an abelian group and map. Optional: `Bound` (default −1).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Torsion subgroup of E over a number field; uses `TorsionBound`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Uses all relevant Magma machinery (2-descent, Cassels–Tate pairing, analytic routines when conductor has small norm) to determine Mordell–Weil group and Sha. Same arguments and returns as for E/Q (§122.2.5). Replaces the obsolete `PseudoMordellWeilGroup`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Upper bound on rank of E(K) from 2-descent or 2-isogeny descent. Optional: `Isogeny`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Absolute logarithmic height of the x-coordinate of P ∈ E(K).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Néron–Tate height ĥ(P) for P on E/K. Parameters: `Precision` (default 27), `Extra` (default 8; remedies precision loss when 2ⁿP near point at infinity).
algorithm: Sum of local heights; Precision parameter controls output precision.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Height pairing matrix for an array of points. Same parameters as `Height`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Local height λ_{Pl}(P) at a place Pl (finite or infinite) of K. Parameters: `Precision` (default 0), `Extra` (default 8).
algorithm: Local height formula; archimedean: Extra remedies precision near ∞.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Same arguments and returns as over Q; additionally returns a map from an abstract group (either `TwoSelmerGroup(E)` or a quotient) to the sequence of 2-coverings. Parameter: `MinRed` (controls minimisation/reduction, may be expensive over fields with large discriminant), plus RemoveTorsion, RemoveGens, WithMaps, verbose.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Obtains a single 2-cover for element e in a cubic extension A/F.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For isogeny φ : E → E1 over K (2-isogeny or multiplication-by-2): returns the connecting homomorphism µ : E1(K) → H¹(K, E[φ]) and the map τ : H¹(K, E[φ]) → homogeneous spaces. Elements of H¹ are in A*/A*². Parameter: `Fields` (for multiplication-by-2; used in `AbsoluteAlgebra`).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: φ-Selmer group Sel^(φ)(E/K) as a finite abelian group S, with map AtoS : A → S. Standard map E1(K) → Sel(φ) is µ composed with AtoS. Parameters: `Hints` (x-coordinates to try first), `Raw` (default false; if true returns also toVec, FB, Hints), `Bound` (default −1; if positive passed to ClassGroup), verbose `Selmer`.
algorithm: Class group and unit group computations **[Cas66]**; conditional on precomputed class group data if available.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: 2-Selmer group of E over Q or a number field. Calls `SelmerGroup` for multiplication-by-2. Same options and returns. Verbose `EllSelmer`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For E/K: determines the subset of E(K) whose images under Ecov : E → P¹ are Q-rational. Arguments: MWmap : A → E (e.g. from PseudoMordellWeilGroup), Ecov : E → P¹. Returns V (found points), R (index bound). Parameters: `InertiaDegreeBound` (default 20), `SmoothBound` (default 50), `PrimeBound` (default 30), `IndexBound` (default −1), `InitialPrimes` (default 50), verbose `EllChab`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: p-adic version: bounds the set of points in E(K) whose Ecov-images are Q-rational. Returns N (upper bound), V (found points), R (index bound), L (coset collection). Parameters: `Cosets`, `Aux`, `Precision`, `Bound`, verbose `EllChab`.
algorithm: p-adic Chabauty method of **[Bru03, Bru02]**; see **[Bru04]** for examples.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For a separable commutative algebra over Q (or finite field): returns the isomorphic direct sum of absolute fields as a Cartesian product, plus isomorphisms. Parameter: `Fields` (suggest existing field representations). Result is cached (recomputed if Fields given). Verbose `EtaleAlg`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: p-Selmer group of semi-simple algebra A: direct sum of p-Selmer groups of irreducible summands, with embedding in A*. S must be prime ideals of the underlying number field. Verbose `EtaleAlg`.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For prime ideal P of a number field K: map K* → K*_P / K*²_P, codomain as finite abelian group.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For commutative algebra A over K and prime P of K: map A* → A*/A*² ⊗ K_P. Also returns sequence of records (one per number field in AbsoluteAlgebra(A)) with fields i, p, map, vmap.
algorithm: Direct sum of `LocalTwoSelmerMap(Q)` over extensions Q of P.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Local root number of E/K at prime ideal P. Formulae due to Rohrlich, Halberstadt, Kobayashi, and the Dokchitser brothers.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Global root number of E/K: product of local root numbers over all places (−1 from each infinite place). Conjectural sign in functional equation L(E/K,s) ↔ L(E/K,2−s).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Analytic rank of E/K: heuristic, computes L^{(r)}(1)/r! derivatives until nonzero. Also returns first nonzero value. Assumes analytic continuation and functional equation. Parameter: `Precision` (default 6).

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Assuming BSD: approximation to Reg(E/K) ·

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: For E/K and a sequence Pts of purported Mordell–Weil basis points: conjectural order of Sha(E/K) from BSD. Returns 0 if points are dependent/insufficient rank; returns n²·

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Search for elliptic curves with conductor equal to ideal N (first form) or with conductor supported only by primes in S (second form). Returns sequence of non-isomorphic curves found (possibly isogenous). `Effort` (integer) controls effort roughly linearly; Effort=400 uses all techniques. Parameters: `Full` (default false), `Max`, `Primes`, `Traces`, verbose `ECSearch`.
algorithm: Multi-technique search; effort incremented exponentially when early stopping specified.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Conductor of E defined over a p-adic field.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Tate's algorithm for E over a p-adic field: returns ⟨P, v_P(d), f_P, c_P, KodairaSymbol, s⟩ and an integral minimal model E_min. P is the uniformizer of the ground field.

chapter_title: Elliptic Curves over Q and Number Fields
description: Local root number of E defined over a p-adic field.
Returns a sequence of places where the given model of E has bad reduction.

The conductor of E over a function field F. Returned as a divisor of F in general; as a sequence of tuples ⟨f, e⟩ (place specified by field element f, multiplicity e) when F is a rational function field.

Runs Tate's algorithm at the place Pl (or the place specified by irreducible polynomial or 1/t for rational function fields). A model of E (over a rational function field) minimising Max([Degree(aᵢ)/i]) over the Weierstrass coefficients a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄, a₆.

description: Evaluates a pair of covariants (depending on integer r) at a genus one model of degree prime to r. subsection: 125.18.2.1 Isomorphisms, Isogenies and Endomorphism Rings of Analytic Jacobians
description: For period matrices (small or big): finds a nonsingular integral `M` with `α(P₁, 1) = (P₂, 1)M` (small) or `αP₁ = P₂M` (big), defining an isogeny. Returns `true`/`false`, `M`, and (big case) `α`.

subsection: 125.18.2.1 Isomorphisms, Isogenies and Endomorphism Rings of Analytic Jacobians
description: For analytic Jacobians with big period matrices: finds a nonsingular integral `M` with `αP₁ = P₂M`. Returns `true`/`false`, `M`, `α`.

subsection: 125.18.2.1 Isomorphisms, Isogenies and Endomorphism Rings of Analytic Jacobians
description: The endomorphism ring of the analytic Jacobian of period matrix `P`, as a matrix algebra; for a big period matrix also a list of `α`-matrices with `αP = PM` for each generator `M`.

subsection: 125.18.2.1 Isomorphisms, Isogenies and Endomorphism Rings of Analytic Jacobians
description: The endomorphism ring of the analytic Jacobian `A` as a matrix algebra; second return: the `α`-matrices for each generator.
For a small period matrix `t` of a genus-`g` analytic Jacobian `A`: a set `S` of `2g − 1` complex numbers such that `y² = x(x−1)∏_{s∈S}(x − s)` (Rosenhain normal form) has Jacobian isomorphic to `A`.
The Delaunay triangulation for `sites` (a sequence of pairs of real numbers, all in the same real field). Returns, for each site `i`, the list of indices of sites to which `i` is joined.

The Voronoi cells for `sites`. Returns `siteedges` (as `Delaunay`), `dualsites` (triples `⟨x, y, m⟩`; `m = 0` for a finite point, else a point "at infinity" in direction `(x, y)`), and `cells` (for each site, an index list into `dualsites` describing the surrounding cell, with the first/last indices indicating infinite sides).

First principal form: takes two sequences `A` and `B` of rationals of the same length, which must be disjoint modulo 1 and each Galois-invariant (e.g. if 1/6 appears, so must 5/6). Returns hypergeometric data with α = `A`, β = `B` (switched if necessary so β holds the smallest rational in [0, 1)).
Second principal form: takes two products `F` and `G` of cyclotomic polynomials, coprime and of the same degree. The polynomials determine α and β. α and β are switched if necessary.
Third form: a sequence of integers `G` with Σᵥ v·G[v] = 0. Here Pα(T)/Pβ(T) = Πᵥ(Tᵛ − 1)^{G[v]}, and α, β are recovered by Möbius inversion. Negating all entries of G corresponds to swapping α and β.
Fourth form: a list of nonzero integers (with repetition) corresponding to the sequence G of the previous form; negative integers indicate where G[v] is negative. The sum of all members must be 0.
Fifth form: two arrays `F` and `G` of integers specifying which cyclotomic polynomials appear in α and β respectively.
Utility form: takes a sequence `E` of two sequences and passes them to the appropriate intrinsic above.
Given hypergeometric data `H`, adds 1/2 to every element in α and β and returns new hypergeometric data. The new α and β may be switched due to twisting.
algorithm: Direct shift of α, β by 1/2.

description: Given hypergeometric data `H`, returns its primitive associated data. Most easily described via `GammaList`: divide all elements by their gcd.

Generates all possible hypergeometric data of degree `d`, returned as a sequence of pairs of rational sequences of length `d`. Parameters: `Weight` (restrict to data of this weight; default: `false`), `TwistMinimal` (only return twist-minimal data; default: `false`), `CyclotomicData` (return cyclotomic data sequences rather than rationals; default: `false`), `Primitive` (if `true`, only primitive data; if a positive integer, data with that imprimitivity; default: `0`).
Returns the weight of the given hypergeometric data `H`. Computed as w + 1 = maxₓ D(x) − minₓ D(x) where D(x) = #{α : α ≤ x} − #{β : β ≤ x}.
Returns the degree of the given hypergeometric data `H` (the common length n of α and β).
Returns the (products of cyclotomic) polynomials corresponding to α and β for hypergeometric data `H`.
Returns two arrays of integers specifying which cyclotomic polynomials occur for α and β. For example, Φ₃Φ₄²Φ₆ is represented by [3,4,4,6].
Returns two arrays of rationals giving α and β of the hypergeometric data `H`.
Returns the scaling parameter M of the given hypergeometric data `H`. Defined by Mₙ = Πᵈ
algorithm: ₙ d^{d·μ(n/d)} for the nth cyclotomic polynomial, combined across the products for α and β and divided; equivalently M = Πᵥ v^{γᵥ}.

description: Returns an array of integers γᵥ where Pα(T)/Pβ(T) = Πᵥ(Tᵛ − 1)^{γᵥ} and Σᵥ v·γᵥ = 0.
Returns a list of integers: sgn(γᵥ)·v appears in the list
True if hypergeometric data instances `H1` and `H2` have the same α and β.
True if hypergeometric data instances `H1` and `H2` do not have the same α and β.
Returns `true` if the given hypergeometric data `H` is primitive, and also returns the index of imprimitivity (the gcd of the elements in the GammaList).

subsection: 126.2.3 Functionality with L-series and Euler Factors
description: The heart of the package. Given hypergeometric data `H`, a rational `t ≠ 0, 1`, and a prime `p`, computes the pth Euler factor of the hypergeometric motive at `t`. The prime `p` must not be wild (must not divide the denominator of any α or β). Parameters: `Precision` (number of terms to compute; 0 = full polynomial; default: 0), `Check` (if `false`, suppress use of the local functional equation; default: `false`), `Fake` (compute hypergeometric traces for t with vₚ(Mt) = 0, including wild primes, without the local functional equation; default: `false`).
algorithm: p-adic Γ-function formula for Gauss sums, as indicated by Cohen. Local functional equation used to expedite computation (unless disabled). See **[Kat90]**.

subsection: 126.2.3 Functionality with L-series and Euler Factors
description: Given hypergeometric data `H` and rational `t ≠ 0, 1`, constructs the L-series of the associated motive. Wild prime Euler factors must be supplied by the user; tame/multiplicative Euler factors and γ-factors are computed automatically. Parameters: `BadPrimes` (sequence of triples `<p, conductor_exponent, factor>` for bad primes; default: `[]`), `GAMMA` (γ-factors; default: `[]`), `Identify` (attempt to identify weight 0 motives as Artin representations and weight 1 motives as (hyper)elliptic curves; default: `true`).
algorithm: Euler product from `EulerFactor`; functional equation framework from Magma's L-series machinery.

subsection: 126.2.3.1 Identification of Hypergeometric Data as Other Objects
description: Given hypergeometric data `H` of weight 0 and rational `t ≠ 0, 1`, attempts to determine the associated Artin representation. Implemented for all such `H` of degree ≤ 3, and for some of degree 4 and higher; requires `GammaList(H)` to have cardinality 3. Parameter: `Check` (if `true`, Euler factors at good primes up to 100 are verified; default: `true`).

subsection: 126.2.3.1 Identification of Hypergeometric Data as Other Objects
description: Given hypergeometric data `H` of degree 2 and weight 1 (10 such families exist), returns the associated elliptic curve over a function field, as catalogued by Cohen. For imprimitive data of index r, returns generically an elliptic curve over an extension of degree r (or an array when xʳ − 1/Mt splits).
algorithm: Cohen's catalogue of degree-2 weight-1 families.

subsection: 126.2.3.1 Identification of Hypergeometric Data as Other Objects
description: As `EllipticCurve(H)` but specialised at rational `t ≠ 0, 1`.

subsection: 126.2.3.1 Identification of Hypergeometric Data as Other Objects
description: Given hypergeometric data `H` of degree 4 and weight 1 where the data is known to correspond to a hyperelliptic curve, returns the associated curve over a function field. There are 18 cases giving a genus-2 curve from `CanonicalCurve` (36 with twists), plus a few others with higher genus canonical curves admitting a genus-2 quotient. Returns `false` if no such curve can be constructed.

subsection: 126.2.3.1 Identification of Hypergeometric Data as Other Objects
description: As `HyperellipticCurve(H)` but specialised at rational `t ≠ 0, 1`.
algorithm: Catalogue of degree-4 weight-1 cases; specialisation.

subsection: 126.2.3.1 Identification of Hypergeometric Data as Other Objects
description: Given hypergeometric data `H` and rational `t ≠ 0, 1`, returns any known associated object or `false`. Currently returns: an Artin representation (weight 0); an elliptic curve over Q (weight 1, degree 2); an elliptic curve over a number field (weight 1, degree 2r with imprimitivity r), possibly multiple curves; or a hyperelliptic curve over Q (weight 1, degree 4).

Given hypergeometric data `H`, constructs the canonical associated scheme over a function field (the parameter t not specialised). The scheme is determined from the GammaList, with a variable for every element; it is the intersection of Σ Xᵢ = Σ Yⱼ = 1 with the monomial equation above.
As `CanonicalScheme(H)` but with the rational parameter `t ≠ 0, 1` specialised.

Given suitable hypergeometric data `H`, attempts to construct an associated plane curve over a function field. Possible when the GammaList has 4 elements; sometimes possible with 6 elements (when the largest absolute-value element equals the negation of the sum of two others). Returns `false` if not possible.
algorithm: Plane curve from GammaList Jacobi sums.

description: As `CanonicalCurve(H)` but with the rational parameter `t ≠ 0, 1` specialised.
Instructs the package to cache all computed p-adic Γ-function values when the prime power q is less than `n`. The qth table entry has (q − 1) elements.
Clears the table of cached p-adic Γ-function values.
Returns the Riemann ζ-function as an `LSer`. Parameter: `Precision` (digits of precision; default = precision of the default real field).
algorithm: Functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**; this is weight 1, gamma `[0]`, conductor 1, all `aₙ = 1`, sign 1, pole at s = 1 with residue −1.

description: Dedekind zeta function ζ(K, s) of a number field K, defined as `Σ Norm(I)⁻ˢ` over nonzero ideals I of the maximal order. Parameters: `Method` (`"Artin"`, `"Direct"`, or `"Default"`); `ClassNumberFormula` (bool, default `false`; if `true` computes the residue at s = 1 algebraically via Signature, Regulator, ClassGroup, TorsionSubgroup); `Precision`.
algorithm: Direct method: approximate residue from functional equation (faster unless discriminant is small and precision very high). Artin method: factors ζ(K, s) as a product of Artin L-series **[Dok04, Dok02]**.

description: L-series of an Artin representation A (see Chapter 44). Parameter: `Precision`.
algorithm: Functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**; coefficients from character values of the Artin representation.

description: L-series L(E, s) of an elliptic curve E defined over **Q** or a number field. Parameter: `Precision`. Note: over general number fields, analytic continuation and functional equation are conjectural. Computation time grows as `√conductor`; for only the leading term at s = 1 over **Q**, use `AnalyticRank` or `ConjecturalRegulator` instead.
algorithm: Functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**; local factors from TraceOfFrobenius and RootNumber.

description: L-series L(E/K, s) for elliptic curve E/Q and number field K. Technically the tensor product of the ℓ-adic representations of E/Q and K/Q. Parameters: `Method` (same as for `LSeries(FldNum)`; "Direct" forced when E and K have simultaneous wild ramification at 2 or 3); `Precision`.
algorithm: Tensor product of ℓ-adic representations **[Dok04]**; analytic continuation and functional equation conjectural.

description: Twisted L-series of elliptic curve E/Q by Artin representation A. Not allowed when E and A are simultaneously wildly ramified at 2 or 3. Parameter: `Precision`.
algorithm: Twist via tensor product of ℓ-adic representation of E with the Artin representation; functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**.

description: L-series of a hyperelliptic curve C defined over **Q**. Parameters: `Precision`; `ExcFactors` (sequence of `⟨prime, conductor_exponent, local_factor⟩` triples for bad primes where the Euler factor is known in advance).
algorithm: Functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**; local Euler factors computed from Jacobian at good primes.

description: Dirichlet L-series L(χ, s) = Σ χ(n)/nˢ for a primitive Dirichlet character χ : (Z/mZ)* → C*. Character values must lie in Z, Q, or a cyclotomic field. Parameter: `Precision`. See §19.8 for Dirichlet characters.
L-series of a cuspidal Hilbert modular newform. (No additional parameters documented beyond the form itself.)
algorithm: Functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**; coefficients from the Hilbert modular form eigenvalues.

description: L-series of a primitive Hecke (Grössencharacter) on ideals. See §34.9 for Hecke characters. Parameter: `Precision`.

L-series L(f, s) = Σ aₙ/nˢ for a modular form f with q-expansion Σ aₙqⁿ. It is assumed (not checked) that L(f, s) satisfies the standard functional equation. Parameters: `Embedding` (map or user function embedding the coefficient ring into C; required when f is defined over a number field); `Precision`.
algorithm: Functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**. The user must ensure the functional equation holds; `CheckFunctionalEquation` should be called.

description: Compute L(s₀) for complex s₀, or the Dth derivative L⁽ᴰ⁾(s₀) if `Derivative := D > 0`. If it is known that L(s₀) = … = L⁽ᴰ⁻¹⁾(s₀) = 0, setting `Leading := true` substantially reduces computation time (useful when determining the order of vanishing).
algorithm: Functional equation / approximate functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**; see also **[Lav67, Tol97, Coh00]** §10.3.

description: For an L-function of even weight 2k (in Magma's sense), returns L(k).

Compute L*(s₀) or its Dth derivative L*⁽ᴰ⁾(s₀) (parameter `Derivative := D`, default 0), where L*(s) = (conductor/πᵈ)^(s/2) γ(s) L(s) is the completed L-function satisfying L*(s) = sign · L̄*(weight − s).

Compute the first n+1 terms of the Taylor expansion of L about s₀: L(s₀) + L′(s₀)x + L″(s₀)x²/2! + … + L⁽ⁿ⁾(s₀)xⁿ/n! + O(xⁿ⁺¹). Parameter: `ZeroBelow := k` asserts the first k terms vanish, reducing computation time.
algorithm: Repeated differentiation of the functional equation integral **[Dok04]**.

description: Product L(s) = L₁(s)·L₂(s) of two L-series of the same weight with weakly multiplicative coefficients. Parameters: `Poles` (list of poles of L₁*(s)L₂*(s) with Re ≥ weight/2); `Residues` (residues at those poles); `Precision`.
algorithm: Coefficient-wise product; Euler factors multiply. Functional equation derived from those of L₁ and L₂.

description: Quotient L(s) = L₁(s)/L₂(s), assuming the quotient is a genuine L-function with finitely many poles. (Not checked.) Parameters: `Poles`, `Residues`, `Precision`.
algorithm: Coefficient-wise division of Euler factors; poles at zeros of L₂*(s) must be supplied by user.

signature: `TensorProduct(L1, L2, ExcFactors)` / `TensorProduct(L1, L2)` / `TensorProduct(L1, L2, ExcFactors, K)` / `TensorProduct(L1, L2, K)`
description: Tensor product L(V₁⊗V₂, s) for L₁ = L(V₁, s) and L₂ = L(V₂, s) associated to ℓ-adic representations V₁, V₂ (à la Serre). Both must have integer conductor, weakly multiplicative coefficients, and an underlying Hodge structure (recovered from γ-shifts). `ExcFactors` is a list of `⟨p, v⟩` or `⟨p, v, Fₚ(x)⟩` tuples specifying conductor valuation and inverse local factor at primes of simultaneous bad reduction; if omitted for a prime, Magma assumes (V₁⊗V₂)^Iₚ = V₁^Iₚ ⊗ V₂^Iₚ. The sign cannot be derived from the signs of the factors and is computed numerically from the functional equation unless supplied via `Sign`. Optional field argument `K`: tensor product over K rather than Q. Parameters: `Precision`, `Sign`.
algorithm: Euler-factor-by-Euler-factor tensor product; Hodge structure combinatorics for gamma factors **[Dok04]**. For motivic L-functions the standard functional equation is expected.

description: General L-series constructor. Compulsory arguments: real positive `weight`; `gamma` (sequence of rationals: the γ-shifts λᵢ; e.g. `[0]` for ζ(s), `[0,1]` for an elliptic curve over Q, `[0,…,0,1,…,1]` with r₁+r₂ zeros and r₂ ones for Dedekind ζ of a field with r₁ real and r₂ complex places); real positive `conductor`; `cffun` specifying the Dirichlet coefficients (a finite sequence `[a₁,…,aₙ]`; a function `f(n)` returning aₙ; a function `f(p,d)` returning the inverse local factor at p up to degree d; or `0` meaning coefficients will be set later via `LSetCoefficients`). Optional parameters: `Sign` (complex number of absolute value 1, or 0 to compute numerically, or a function `s(p)` or `s(L,p)` computing it to precision p); `Poles` (sequence of poles z of L*(s) with Re(z) ≥ weight/2; default []); `Residues` (sequence of residues at those poles, same length as `Poles`, or [] to compute numerically); `Parent` (any Magma object, used only for printing); `CoefficientGrowth` (function `f(x)` or `f(L,x)` bounding |aₙ| ≤ f(n)); `Precision`; `ImS` (largest Im(s) for which L(s) will be evaluated); `Asymptotics` (bool, default `true`: use asymptotic expansions as well as Taylor series).
algorithm: Functional equation method **[Dok04, Dok02]**; approximate functional equation via theta functions (Lavrik **[Lav67]**, Tollis **[Tol97]**, Cohen **[Coh00]** §10.3).

description: Tests the functional equation numerically by evaluating the two theta functions at a real point t and subtracting; should return 0 to current precision. Computes sign and residues if not yet known. If sign was 0 (unknown), returns `|Sign| − 1`. Optional parameter `t` (real, 1.05 < t < 1.2, default 1.2). A value significantly far from 0 indicates an incorrect parameter (conductor, sign, etc.) or insufficient coefficients.
algorithm: Approximate functional equation: evaluates `Σ aₙ Γ((weight−s+λᵢ)/2, n·t/√N)` versus the conjugate sum at `weight−s` **[Dok04]**.

description: Set or replace the coefficient function of an existing `LSer` object L. `cffun` may be: a finite sequence `[a₁,…,aₙ]`; a function `f(n)` returning aₙ; or a function `f(p,d)` returning the inverse local factor Fₚ(x) at prime p up to degree d (as a polynomial or power series of precision O(xᵈ⁺¹)). Invoking `LSeries(…, cffun)` is equivalent to `LSeries(…, 0)` followed by `LSetCoefficients(L, cffun)`.
Number of Dirichlet coefficients aₙ required to compute L-values at current precision. May be called before coefficients are set.
algorithm: Derived from the conductor and precision via the Dokchitser bound **[Dok04]**.

description: Returns the vector `[* a₁, …, aₙ *]` of the first N Dirichlet coefficients.
algorithm: Evaluates the coefficient function set on L.

description: The p-th Euler factor of L, as a polynomial or power series. Optional parameters: `Degree` (truncate series to that length); `Precision` (for complex-valued coefficients).
Conductor of the L-series (real number, usually an integer). Evaluation time is proportional to √conductor.
Sign in the functional equation (complex number of absolute value 1, or 0 if not yet computed). Calling `CheckFunctionalEquation` or any evaluation function sets the sign.
Sequence of γ-shifts λ₁,…,λd for L(s); each represents a factor Γ((s+λᵢ)/2) in the functional equation.

Returns a tuple of length 7: `(weight, gamma_shifts, conductor, coefficient_function, sign, poles_of_L*, residues_of_L*)`. Sign = 0 means not computed; Residues = [] means not computed. The tuple contains enough data to recreate L via the general `LSeries` call.
If L is internally represented as a product `Π Lᵢ(s)^nᵢ`, returns the sequence `[...<Lᵢ, nᵢ>...]`.

Change the working precision (in decimal digits) of the L-series L to `precision`. Also accepts the same optional parameters as the general `LSeries` constructor: `CoefficientGrowth`, `ImS`, `Asymptotics`.

Set verbose level for all L-series functions. Levels: 0 = quiet (default; only prints loss-of-precision warnings); 1 = prints sign and residues when computed from functional equation; 2 = messages for new L-function construction, coefficient generation, and expansion computation; 3 = progress indicator (every 1000 coefficients, every 5000 series terms). Frequencies stored in `L'vprint_coeffs` and `L'vprint_series` attributes.

Returns the L-series corresponding to the mth symmetric power of L. Parameter: `BadEulerFactors` (sequence of `⟨p, f, E⟩` triples, where p is a prime, f the conductor exponent, and E a polynomial giving the inverse Euler factor at p).
algorithm: For GL(1): primitivization and power of the underlying character. For GL(2) / elliptic curves: bad Euler factors from **[MW06, DMW09]**; general case requires user to supply bad factors; Hodge structure combinatorics for gamma factors.

description: Set verbose level for Weil polynomial routines. Maximum value 2.
For a polynomial f with rational coefficients, checks that all complex roots have absolute value 1. Does not use floating-point approximations.

Given Frobenius traces on the i-th étale cohomology over Fq, returns a list of possible Weil polynomials of degree `deg`. For even i, determines the sign in the functional equation from absolute values of roots when possible; otherwise returns both candidates. Contradictory data returns an empty sequence. Optional parameter: `KnownFactor` (a known polynomial factor).
algorithm: Lift traces to symmetric functions; test functional equation and root-on-unit-circle conditions.

description: Counts zeros of f (with multiplicity) that are q times a root of unity; this is an upper bound for the Picard rank of the corresponding algebraic surface (equals Picard rank conditionally on the Tate conjecture).
algorithm: Root counting on the unit circle.

description: For Weil polynomial f corresponding to H² of an algebraic surface with Hodge number h²·⁰, evaluates the Artin–Tate formula. Returns: arithmetic Picard rank; absolute value of discriminant(Pic) × order(Br), conditional on the Tate conjecture.
For the characteristic polynomial f of Frobenius on an étale cohomology group, returns the characteristic polynomial of the `deg`-fold iterated Frobenius.
algorithm: Polynomial substitution x → x^deg (adapting the Newton power-sum structure).

description: Checks conditions that the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius on H² of an algebraic surface must satisfy: valuation of roots at all places (including p and ∞), functional equation, and Artin–Tate conditions **[EJ10]**. Returns `true` or `false`. Parameters: q (base field size), h20 (Hodge number h²·⁰); optional `SurfDeg` (degree of surface; −1 = unknown).
algorithm: Valuations, functional equation check, Artin–Tate conditions per **[EJ10]**.

description: A model of the modular curve `X_0(N)`, in an affine plane specified by `X`. The string `t` must be one of "Atkin", "Canonical", or "Classical", with `N` a level in the corresponding modular curve database.
algorithm: Defined by the affine modular polynomial from the named database.

description: An affine model of the modular curve `X_0(N)` of level `N` from a database `D` of modular curves.
Given a modular curve `X = X_0(N)` and an elliptic curve `E`, with compatible base rings, the sequence of points over the base field of `E` corresponding to `E` with additional level structure.
The level of the modular curve `X` as an integer.
The genus of the modular curve `X`.
The type of the model for `X`, presently limited to "Atkin", "Canonical", or "Classical". Used to determine the algorithm by which parametrized isogenies are computed.

A sequence of integers `[N, M, P]` classifying the class of `X`, defining a congruence subgroup `Γ(N,M,P) = { (a b; c d) : c ≡ 0 mod N, b ≡ 0 mod P, a ≡ 1 mod M }` of PSL₂(**Z**), where `M` divides LCM(N,P). For the models presently available this is `[N,1,1]`, where `N` is the level of `X = X_0(N)`.
Given a prime `N` represented in the database of Atkin modular curves, the Atkin modular polynomial Ξ_N(X,Y).
Given a prime `N` represented in the database of canonical modular curves, the canonical modular polynomial Ψ_N(X,Y).
Given an integer `N` represented in the database of classical modular curves, the defining classical modular polynomial Φ_N(X,Y).

Given an identifier string `t` (one of "Atkin", "Canonical", "Classical"), the corresponding database object of modular curves `X_0(N)`. The Atkin database is split into objects of levels 200(i−1)+1 ≤ N < 200i for `i` in 1,…,5 (only the first two provided by default; more available from the Magma website). The canonical database contains a subset of curves for prime levels below 200; the classical database contains only levels below 60.
Returns `true` if and only if `N` is a level represented in the modular curve database `D`.
Returns `true` if and only if the data file given by the string `t` and integer `i` exists.

Given an elliptic curve `E` and a point `P` on some `X_0(N)` corresponding to a cyclic level structure on `E`, returns an isogeny f : E → F corresponding to `P`. Defined so the pull-back of the invariant differential of `F` is the invariant differential on `E`.
Given an elliptic curve `E` and a point `P` on some `X_0(N)` corresponding to a cyclic level structure on `E`, returns the subgroup scheme of `E` parametrized by `X_0(N)`.
The function field of the modular curve `X`.
Given a modular curve `X` over a field, the *j*-invariant as a function on the curve.
Given one of the standard models `X` for `X_0(N)`, the base model curve `X(1)` and the morphism π : X_0(N) → X(1).

Given a projective modular curve `X = X_0(N)`, the Atkin-Lehner involution of the modular curve as a map of schemes. Currently the only Atkin-Lehner involution returned is that for `N` equal to the level of `X`.
algorithm: Defined via the canonical / Atkin-Lehner involution of the model.

description: Given a negative discriminant `D`, the Hilbert class polynomial, defined as the minimal polynomial of j(τ), where **Z**[τ] is an imaginary quadratic order of discriminant `D`.

Given a negative discriminant `D` not congruent to 5 modulo 8, the Weber class polynomial, the minimal polynomial of f(τ) where f is a particular normalized Weber function generating the same class field as j(τ). The f used depends on `D` mod 8 (and `D/4` mod 8 when even) and on whether 3 divides `D`. A root f(τ) is an algebraic integer (a unit outside of 2) generating the ring class field; the *j*-root is recovered by j(τ) = F(f(τ)) with `F` a returned rational function A(Bxʳ + C)³/xʳ, r

Given a negative discriminant `D` and the corresponding Weber class polynomial `f`, the Hilbert class polynomial for `D`. Parameter `Al` (`MonStgElt`, default "Roots"): "Roots" computes complex approximations to the roots of the Hilbert polynomial from approximations to the roots of the Weber polynomial via the rational function `F`; the other method is algebraic, using resultants and `F`.

Given a level `N` and a (possibly empty) sequence of integers `A` representing Atkin-Lehner involutions, computes a model for a quotient of `X_0(N)` by `A`. Returns `P¹` for a genus 0 curve, an elliptic or hyperelliptic curve, or the canonical embedding in `P^{g−1}` (coordinates = cusp forms invariant under the specified involutions). Parameters: `Raw` (`BoolElt`, default `false`; when not `true`, an initial "semi-reduction" is performed), `Reduce` (`BoolElt`, default `false`; if `true`, a complete LLL-reduction of the equations — impractical for genus greater than ~50).
algorithm: Canonical embedding via invariant cusp forms; optional LLL reduction.

section: 128.10 Modular Curves of Given Level and Genus
description: Set the printing level for verbose output for the intrinsics in this section. Legal values for `v`: `true`, `false`, 0, 1, 2 (`false` = 0, `true` = 1).

section: 128.10 Modular Curves of Given Level and Genus
description: For level `N`, a list of all hyperelliptic curves of genus `g ≥ 2` which are new modular curves for `X_1(N)` if `gamma` equals 1 (default) or `X_0(N)` if `gamma` equals 0. Each curve is returned as a univariate polynomial f(x) with y² = f(x) a Weierstrass equation. description: As above, with `E` over a subfield of K with j-invariant j(p) (≠ 0, 1728); E₁ is E or its base change to K.

A procedure that prints a mini-program giving expressions for the modular functions corresponding to t (genus 0), to x, y (subhyperelliptic), or to the weight-2 cusp forms f₁,…,f_r (other cases) on X₀(N), in terms of forms/functions of basic type. The mini-program is a sequence of assignment statements v = ⟨expr⟩ built from terms — integers, q = e^{2πiz}, previously-assigned variables, eta products `e{⟨d r⟩…}`, binary-form theta functions `th0/th1/th2/th3{A B C}`, quaternion theta functions `thQ{N}`, Eisenstein series `E{p}`, elliptic-curve cusp forms `f{a₁ a₂ a₃ a₄ a₆}` — possibly modified by operators D, [d] (d-shift), ⟨d⟩ (twist). The final line is `[t,1]`, `[x,y,1]`, or `[f₁,…,f_r]`.

description: q-expansions to precision `r` as Laurent series in the Laurent series ring `R` over **Q**, for the sequence of modular forms/functions of level N defining the model: `[t]` (genus 0), `[x,y]` (elliptic/hyperelliptic), or `[f₁,…,f_r]` (otherwise). t, x, y have negative power terms (poles at cusp ∞); the fᵢ are power series.
algorithm: Computes q-expansions from the `qExpansionExpressions` recipe via fast basic-type routines.
