description: The minimal polynomial of the Galois conjugates of the CM points corresponding to `μ` and their complex values, for `G` a triangle group. `μ` must be Galois-stable (F(μ) Galois over `F`, `F` the defining base field of `G`). The returned polynomial is the "best guess" rational approximation to the polynomial with the CM points as roots.
algorithm: Shimura reciprocity law (computing Galois conjugates), then rational recognition of the minimal polynomial.

description: The space `M_2(Γ_0(N), Z)` of weight-2 modular forms on `Γ_0(N)` over **Z** (same as `ModularForms(N, 2)`).
The space `M_k(Γ_0(N), Z)` of weight-`k` modular forms on `Γ_0(N)` over **Z**.

For a Dirichlet character `eps` and integer `k`: a space of weight-`k` modular forms over **Z** which, under base extension, becomes the direct sum of the spaces `M_k(Γ_1(N), eps1)` of weight `k` and nebentypus `eps1`, where `eps1` runs over all Galois conjugates of `eps`.
The weight-`k` space over **Z** formed as the direct sum of `ModularForms(eps, k)` over all `eps` in the sequence `chars` of Dirichlet characters.
Same as `ModularForms(G, 2)`.
The space `M_k(G, Z)` for a congruence subgroup `G`. The groups `Γ_0(N)` and `Γ_1(N)` are supported, created via `Gamma0(N)` and `Gamma1(N)`.
Shortcut returning the `CuspidalSubspace` of the corresponding full space of modular forms.
The space of half-integral weight forms on `Gamma0(N)` of weight `w`. Here `N` should be a multiple of 4 and `w` a positive element of `Z + 1/2`.
The space of half-integral weight forms on `Gamma1(N)` with character `chi` and weight `w`. The modulus of `chi` should be a multiple of 4, and `w` a positive element of `Z + 1/2`.
The space of half-integral weight forms on the congruence subgroup `G` and weight `w`. Here `G` must be contained in `Gamma0(4)`, and `w` is a positive element of `Z + 1/2`.

The base extension of `M` to the ring `R`, plus the induced map `M → BaseExtend(M, R)`. The only requirement on `R` is a natural coercion map from `BaseRing(M)` to `R`; when `BaseRing(M)` is the integers, any `R` is allowed.
The base extension of `M` to `R` using the map `φ : BaseRing(M) → R`, plus the induced map `M → BaseExtend(M, R)`.
The `i`-th basis vector of the space of modular forms `M`.
Coercion of `f` into the space of modular forms `M`. Here `f` can be a modular form, a power series with absolute precision, or something coercible into `RSpace(M)`.
The modular form associated to the elliptic curve `E` over **Q** (see 132.18).
The canonical basis of the space of modular forms or half-integral weight forms `M`.
algorithm: Hermite normal form over **Z**, then base change.

description: A sequence containing the `q`-expansions (to precision `prec`) of the elements of `Basis(M)`.

An integer `b` such that `f + O(q^b)` determines any modular form `f` in `M`. With `Exact := true` (default `false`), or if a `q`-expansion basis has already been computed, the result is best-possible (the smallest such `b`); otherwise it is a Sturm bound similar to (and sometimes sharper than) the bounds in section 9.4 of **[Ste07]**.
algorithm: Sturm bound **[Ste07]**; `Exact := true` gives the smallest determining precision.

description: An abstract free module isomorphic to `M` over the same base ring (unless `Ring` is specified), plus a map to/from `M`. Needed to use linear-algebra functions on `M` (a space of modular forms is not a subtype of vector space in Magma). Parameter: `Ring`.
The `q`-expansion (at the cusp `∞`) of the modular form (or half-integral weight form) `f` to absolute precision `prec`. An element of the power series ring over the base ring of the parent of `f`.
The `n`-th coefficient of the `q`-expansion of the modular form `f`.
The default printing precision for elements of the space `M` of modular forms (hard-coded default value 12).
Set the default printing precision for elements of the space `M` of modular forms (hard-coded default value 12).

The sum of the modular forms `f` and `g`; or the sum of a modular form `f` and a power series `g` (the `q`-expansion of `f` must be coercible into the parent of `g`). `g + f`, `f − g`, `g − f` also defined.
The difference of the modular forms `f` and `g`.
The product of the scalar `a` and the modular form `f`.
The product of the scalar `1/a` and the modular form `f`.
The power `f^n` of the modular form `f`, where `n ≥ 1` is an integer.
The product of the modular forms `f` and `g`. The only condition is that the base fields of `f` and `g` be the same; the weight of `f*g` is the sum of the weights of `f` and `g`.
Returns `true` iff `M` is an ambient space (those constructed in 132.2.1).
Returns `true` if `M` is contained in the cuspidal subspace of the ambient space.
Returns `true` if `M` is contained in the Eisenstein subspace of the ambient space.
Returns `true` if `f` is an Eisenstein newform or was computed using the intrinsic `EisensteinSeries` (see 132.10).
Returns `true` if `M` is a space of modular forms for `Γ_0(N)`.

Returns `true` if `M` was created explicitly as a space of modular forms for `Γ_1(N)`, or if the `AmbientSpace` of `M` is such a space. (Returns `false` for any `ModularForms(chars, k)`, even if `chars` consists of all mod-`N` Dirichlet characters.)
Returns `true` if `M` is contained in the new subspace of its `AmbientSpace`.

Returns `true` if `f` was created using `Newforms`. (Sometimes `true` in other cases where `f` is obviously a newform. In number theory, "newform" means "normalized eigenform that lies in the new subspace".)
Returns `true` iff `M` is the ring of all modular forms over a given ring.
The full space of modular forms, in which `M` was created as a subspace.
The ring over which `M` was defined.
The number of Galois-conjugates of the modular form `f` over the prime subfield of (the fraction field of) the base ring of `f`.
The dimension of the space `M` of modular forms or half-integral weight forms.
algorithm: For spaces from the `ModularForms` constructors, counts the relevant Eisenstein series and applies a dimension formula for the cusp forms.

description: The dimension of `M` (which must be a full space or the cuspidal subspace of a full space), as given by the formulas in Cohen and Oesterlé ('Modular Forms in One Variable, VI', Lecture Notes in Math. 627).

The dimension of the full space of modular forms (or half-integral weight forms) with level `N`, character `chi` (trivial if not specified) and weight `k`, by the Cohen–Oesterlé formulas. Parameter: `Cuspidal` (default `false`); if `true`, the dimension of the space of cusp forms is returned.
A sequence containing exactly one representative from each Galois-conjugacy class of Dirichlet characters associated to `M`.
For `f` a newform created with `Newform`: a Dirichlet character that is, up to Galois conjugacy, the Nebentypus character of `f`.
The sequence `[a_1, …, a_n]` such that `f = a_1 g_1 + … + a_n g_n`, where `g_1, …, g_n` is the basis of the parent of `f`.
The level of the modular form `f` (resp. the space `M`).
The weight of the modular form `f`, if it is defined.
The weight of the space `M` of modular forms.

A list of tuples describing a basis of the given space of forms of weight 1/2. Each tuple is a pair `<f, t>`, where `t` is an integer and `f` a Dirichlet character; the tuple designates the sum over all integers `n` of `f(n) q^(t n²)`.
The trivial subspace of the space of modular forms `M`.
The subspace of forms `f` in `M` such that the constant term of the Fourier expansion of `f` at every cusp is 0.
The Eisenstein subspace of the space of modular forms `M`.

The projection of a given modular form to the `EisensteinSubspace` (resp. the `CuspidalSubspace`). The sum of the two projections equals the original form (after coercion). The base ring of the given form must contain the rationals.
The new subspace of the space of modular forms `M`.
For a space `M` of weight-1 forms, the subspace spanned by the cusp forms attached to dihedral Galois representations.
The matrix representing the `n`-th Hecke operator `T_n` with respect to `Basis(M)`. (Currently `M` must be a space with trivial character and integral weight `≥ 2`.)
The image under the Hecke operator `T_n` of the given modular form `f`.

The characteristic polynomial of the `n`-th Hecke operator `T_n`. In some situations more efficient than `CharacteristicPolynomial(HeckeOperator(M, n))`. `M` can be an arbitrary space of modular forms. Parameter: `Proof` (default `true`).
The matrix representing the `q`-th Atkin–Lehner involution `W_q` on `M` with respect to `Basis(M)`. (Currently `M` must be a cuspidal space with trivial character and integral weight `≥ 2`.)
The image under the involution `w_q` of the given modular form `f`.
List of the Eisenstein series associated to the modular forms space `M` (i.e. lying in `M ⊗ C`).
Returns `true` if the modular form `f` was created using `EisensteinSeries`.

The data `<χ, ψ, t, χ', ψ'>` that defines the Eisenstein series (modular form) `f`. Here `χ` is a primitive character of conductor `S`, `ψ` is primitive of conductor `M`, and `MSt` divides `N` (the level of `f`). The series associated to `(χ, ψ, t)` has `q`-expansion `c_0 + Σ_{m≥1} (Σ_{n|m} ψ(n) n^{k−1} χ(m/n)) q^{mt}`, where `c_0 = 0` if `S > 1` and `c_0 = L(1−k, ψ)/2` if `S = 1`.

For a space `M` of modular forms of weight 1/2, returns the basis of the space as described by Serre and Stark. A list of tuples is returned; each tuple contains a character `ψ` and an integer `t`, and the corresponding modular form is the theta series defined as the sum over all integers `n` of `ψ(n) q^(t n²)`.

For a space `M` of weight 1, the cuspidal eigenforms in `M` corresponding to dihedral Galois representations, broken up according to character. A list of tuples is returned; each tuple contains an element of the `DirichletCharacters` of `M`, followed by a list of eigenforms.
The number of Galois conjugacy-classes of newforms associated to `M`, which must have base ring **Z** or **Q** (i.e. newforms lying in `M ⊗ C`). Parameter: `Proof` (default `true`).
The `j`-th Galois-conjugate newform in the `i`-th Galois-orbit of newforms in `M` (base ring **Z** or **Q**). Parameter: `Proof` (default `true`).
The first Galois-conjugate newform in the `i`-th orbit in `M` (base ring **Z** or **Q**). Parameter: `Proof` (default `true`).
Sorted list of the newforms associated to `M`, divided into Galois orbits. Parameter: `Proof` (default `true`).

The newforms associated to `M` with prespecified eigenvalues. Here `I` is a sequence `[⟨p_1, f_1(x)⟩, …, ⟨p_n, f_n(x)⟩]` of pairs, each a prime not dividing the level of `M` and a polynomial. Returns the newforms `Σ a_n q^n` in `M` such that `f_n(a_{p_n}) = 0`. (Only works when `M` is cuspidal and defined over **Q** or **Z**.)
The Galois-conjugacy class(es) of newforms described by the string `label`.

The mod `p` reductions of the modular form `f`, where `p ∈ Z` is prime and `f` is a modular form over a number field (or the rationals or integers). Because of denominators, the list of reductions might be empty. (The current algorithm is not close to optimal for `f` over a field of large degree.)
algorithm: Reduction of newform `q`-expansions modulo primes above `p`.

description: The `p`-adic embeddings of the modular form `f`.
The complex embeddings of the modular form `f`.

A group `C` measuring all possible congruences (to precision `prec`) between some modular form in `M1` and some modular form in `M2`. With `W_1 = q-exp(M1) ∩ Z[[q]]` and `W_2 = q-exp(M2) ∩ Z[[q]]`, and `V` the saturation of `W_1 + W_2` in `Z[[q]]`, then `C = V/(W_1 + W_2)`.
algorithm: Saturation of the sum of `q`-expansion lattices.

description: Analogous to `CongruenceGroup`, but considering congruences that hold for all `q`-expansion coefficients `a_n` with `n` coprime to the levels of both `M1` and `M2`.
algorithm: As above, restricted to anemic coefficients.

description: A bound on the degree of the characteristic series modulo `p^m` of the Atkin `U_p` operator on the space of overconvergent `p`-adic modular forms of (even) weight `k` and level `Γ_0(N)`. This bound is due to Daqing Wan and depends only on `k` modulo `p−1` rather than `k` itself.

The characteristic series `P(t)` modulo `p^m` of the Atkin `U_p` operator on overconvergent `p`-adic modular forms of level `Γ_0(N)` and weight `k`; `p ≥ 5` prime not dividing `N`. When `m ≤ k−1`, by Coleman's theorem `P(t)` is also the reverse characteristic polynomial mod `p^m` of `U_p` on classical forms of level `Γ_0(Np)` and weight `k`; and when `m ≤ (k−2)/2`, the reverse characteristic polynomial mod `p^m` of `T_p` on classical forms of level `Γ_0(N)` and weight `k`. Parameter: `WeightBound` (even integer, default 6) bounding the weight of generators chosen for certain classical spaces (level `N ≥ 2`); the algorithm may fail to terminate for some small levels unless `WeightBound` is large enough, but the output is provably correct whenever it terminates.
algorithm: Algorithms 1 and 2 of **[Lau11]**; Coleman's theorem links to classical spaces.

description: A sequence containing `OverconvergentHeckeSeries(p, N, k, m)` for each weight `k` in `kseq`; these weights must be congruent to each other modulo `p−1`. More efficient than computing them separately, since much of the work is shared. Parameter: `WeightBound` (default 6).

The relations of degree `d` satisfied by the `q`-expansions of the forms in the space `M` of modular forms; `q`-expansions are computed to precision `prec`. If `prec` is too small, the intrinsic might return relations not really satisfied. To be sure, `prec` must be at least `PrecisionBound(M2)`, where `M2` has the same level as `M` and weight `d` times the weight of `M`.
The modular form associated to the elliptic curve `E` (which must be defined over the rationals).
The `q`-expansion of the newform associated to `E`, to the specified precision. (Exactly the same as `qExpansion(ModularForm(E), prec)`.)
An elliptic curve `E` with associated modular form `f`, when `f` is a weight-2 newform on `Γ_0(N)` with rational Fourier coefficients.
algorithm: The Cremona database is used to identify the isogeny class. A from-scratch routine is available via `EllipticCurve(M : Database := false)` for the relevant space of modular symbols (not optimized for large level).

description: The sequence of characteristic-0 spaces of modular symbols associated to the space `M` of modular forms, when this makes sense.
The sequence of characteristic-0 spaces of modular symbols with given `sign` associated to `M`, when this makes sense.
Space of modular symbols of level `N`, weight 2, trivial character, over the rationals.
Space of level `N`, weight `k`, trivial character, over the rationals.
Space of level `N`, weight `k`, trivial character, over the field `F`.
Space of level `N`, weight `k`, trivial character, given `sign` (an integer), over the rationals.
Space of level `N`, weight `k`, trivial character, given `sign`, over the field `F`.
Space of weight `k` and character `ε` (an element of a Dirichlet group); `ε` determines the level and base field, so these need not be specified.

Space of weight `k` and character `ε`, with given `sign`. Possible values of `sign` are `−1`, `0`, `+1`, corresponding to the `−1` quotient, the full space, and the `+1` quotient `M/(∗−1)M` (where `∗` is `StarInvolution(M)`).
The space of modular symbols described by a label string `s` (and given `sign`).
algorithm: Parses the label and constructs the corresponding space (cuspidal subspace for the `[Level]k[Weight]` form).

description: Coercion of `x` into the space `M`. Here `x` may be a modular symbol that lies in a subspace of `M`, a 2-tuple describing a modular symbol, a sequence of such 2-tuples (then `M!x` is the sum of the coercions), or anything coercible into `VectorSpace(M)`.
algorithm: Coercion / linear combination of Manin symbols.

description: The modular symbol associated to the 2-tuple `x = ⟨P(X,Y),[u,v]⟩`, where `P(X,Y) ∈ F[X,Y]` is homogeneous of degree `k − 1` (here `F` is the base field and `[u,v]` defines an element of `P¹(Z/NZ)`).
algorithm: Choose lifts `u, v` with `GCD(u,v)=1`, take `g ∈ SL₂(Z)` with lower row `(u, v)`; the symbol is `g(P(X,Y){0,∞})`.

description: An expression for the modular symbol `x` in terms of Manin symbols, represented as 2-tuples `⟨P(X,Y),[u,v]⟩`.
algorithm: Writes `x` as a linear combination of Manin symbols.

description: A basis for the space of modular symbols `M`.

If `M = AmbientSpace(M)`, returns a basis `x₁,…,xₙ` such that `Zx₁ + ⋯ + Zxₙ` is the `Z`-submodule of `M` generated by all modular symbols `XⁱYᵏ⁻²⁻ⁱ{α,β}` (`i = 0,…,k−2`, `α,β ∈ P¹(Q)`). If `M ≠ AmbientSpace(M)`, returns a `Z`-basis for `M ∩ (Zx₁ + ⋯ + Zxₙ)`. The base field of `M` must be `Q`.
algorithm: Integral structure on modular symbols (the natural `Z`-lattice spanned by `XⁱYᵏ⁻²⁻ⁱ{α,β}`).

description: The vector space `V` underlying `M`, together with the maps `V → M` and `M → V`.
The subspace of the linear dual of `VectorSpace(AmbientSpace(M))` isomorphic to `M` as a module over the Hecke algebra.
algorithm: Linear-dual representation (may fail in positive characteristic where `Tₚ` is not semisimple).

description: The lattice generated by the integral modular symbols in the vector-space representation of `M`; the lattice generated by all `XⁱYᵏ⁻²⁻ⁱ{a,b}`. The base field of `M` must be `RationalField()`.

The degeneracy map `M₁ → M₂` associated to `d`. With `N_i` the level of `M_i`, suppose `d` divides either the numerator or denominator of `N₁/N₂` in reduced form. If `N₁ | N₂`, returns `α_d : M₁ → M₂`; if `N₂ | N₁`, returns `β_d : M₁ → M₂`. Error if neither divisibility holds.
The matrix of `DegeneracyMap(M1,M2,d)` with respect to `Basis(M1)` and `Basis(M2)`. Both `IsAmbient(M1)` and `IsAmbient(M2)` must be true.

The level-`N′` space associated to `M` (level `N`). If `N | N′`, returns `Σ_{d|N′/N} α_d(M)`; if `N′ | N`, returns `Σ_{d|N/N′} β_d(M)` (and, if `Conductor(DirichletCharacter(M))` does not divide `N′`, the 0 space).
The subspace of `M₁` associated to `M₂`. With `N₁` the level of `M₁`: if `ModularSymbols(M2,N1)` is defined, let `M₃` be that space; if `M₃ ⊆ M₁`, return `M₃`, else error.

Decomposition of `M` with respect to the Hecke operators `Tₚ` with `p` coprime to the level and `p ≤ bound`. If `bound` is too small, constituents are not guaranteed irreducible. Results are cached, so successive calls give possibly finer decompositions. Parameter `Proof` (default `true`).

Unsorted decomposition of `M` into factors corresponding to the Galois-conjugacy classes of newforms of level some divisor of the level of `M`. Requires `IsCuspidal(M)`. Often significantly faster than `Decomposition`. Parameter `Proof` (default `true`).

The space corresponding to the Galois-conjugacy class of newforms associated to `M` (the newform level may be a proper divisor of the level of `M`). `M` must have been created via `NewformDecomposition`.
Sort the sequence `D` of spaces with respect to the `lt` comparison operator.
Returns `true` iff `Decomposition(M)` has cardinality 1.

Ordering on spaces: (1) if both built via `NewformDecomposition` and `Level(AssociatedNewSpace(M1))` differs from that of `M2`, the `M_i` with larger associated level is first; (2) smaller dimension first; (3) for weight 2 trivial character, order by `W_q` eigenvalues starting with the smallest `p | N` (eigenvalue `+1` less than `−1`); (4) order by `abs(trace(a_p))` for `p ∤ N`, positive trace smaller on ties. Rule (3) extends the ordering of (most of) **[Cre97]**.
The cuspidal subspace of `M`; the kernel of `BoundaryMap(M)`.
Returns `true` iff `M` is contained in the cuspidal subspace of the ambient space.
The Eisenstein subspace of `M`; the complement in `M` of the cuspidal subspace of `M`.
Returns `true` iff `M` is contained in the Eisenstein subspace of the ambient space.
The new subspace of `M`; the intersection of `NewSubspace(M,p)` over all prime divisors `p` of the level. `M` must be cuspidal.
Returns `true` iff `M` is contained in the new cuspidal subspace of the ambient space.

The `p`-new subspace of `M`; the kernel of the degeneracy map from `M` to the space of level (level of `M`)/`p` with restricted character. If the character does not restrict, `NewSubspace(M,p) = M`. `M` must be cuspidal.

The kernel of `I` on `M`. With `Tₚ` the `p`th Hecke operator, and `I = [⟨p₁,f₁(x)⟩,…,⟨pₙ,fₙ(x)⟩]` a sequence of (prime, polynomial) pairs: the subspace obtained by intersecting the kernels of `fₙ(T_{pₙ})`. Only primes `pᵢ` not dividing the level are used.
The space complementary to `M` in the ambient space, so the ambient space equals the direct sum of `M` and `Complement(M)`.
A matrix representing the boundary map from `M` to the vector space whose basis consists of the weight-`k` cusps. (There is no intrinsic that lists these cusps.)

Given spaces `M1`, `M2` specifying newforms `f₁`, `f₂`, and a prime `p`: determines whether some Galois conjugate (over `Q`) of `f₂` is the twist of `f₁` by a nontrivial Dirichlet character of `p`-power conductor; if so, also returns a character `χ` with `f₂ = f₁^χ`.
algorithm: Compares Hecke eigenvalues up to a Sturm bound **[BS02]**.

description: Given a space `M` specifying a newform `f` and a prime `p`: determines whether some Galois conjugate of `f` is a twist of some newform of lower level by a Dirichlet character of `p`-power conductor. If so, returns `false` together with that lower-level newform (as a space) and the Dirichlet character.
algorithm: Twist search down to lower level **[BS02]**.

description: A matrix representing the `n`th Hecke operator `Tₙ` with respect to `Basis(M)`.
The characteristic polynomial of `Tₙ`. For prime `n`, the Deligne bound on eigenvalue sizes is used, so this is frequently much faster than `CharacteristicPolynomial(HeckeOperator(M,n))`.
A matrix representing `Tₙ` with respect to `Basis(Lattice(M))`.

A matrix representing `Tₙ` on the dual vector-space representation of `M`. Much more efficient than `HeckeOperator(M,n)` when `dim M` is small relative to `dim AmbientSpace(M)`. Not guaranteed to be the transpose of `HeckeOperator(M,n)` (computed w.r.t. `Basis(DualVectorSpace(M))`).

A matrix representing the `q`th Atkin-Lehner involution `W_q` on `M`, when defined (`M` has trivial character and even weight). For each divisor `q` of `N` with `gcd(q, N/q)=1`, choose `x,y,z,w` with `qxw − (N/q)yz = 1`, set `g = (dx y; Nz qw)`, and define `W_q(x) = g(x)/q^{(k−2)/2}`. Normalised to be an involution when possible (may be impossible if `k > 2` and the characteristic divides `q`).
The action of the Atkin-Lehner involution on the dual representation of `M`, when defined.
The conjugation involution `∗` sending `XⁱYʲ{u,v}` to `(−1)ʲ XⁱYʲ{−u,−v}`.
The conjugation involution `∗` on the dual representation of `M`.

Multiplication by `XᵖY − XYᵖ`, an analogue of the `θ`-operator (on mod-`p` modular forms, `θ : f ↦ q df/dq`). Both `M1`, `M2` must be over a field of positive characteristic `p`, with the same level and character, and `weight(M2) = weight(M1) + p + 1`.

A positive integer `n` such that `T₁,…,Tₙ` generate the Hecke algebra as a `Z`-module. For trivial character the default bound is `(k/12)·[SL₂(Z):Γ₀(N)]` (follows from **[Stu87]**, as explained in **[AS02]**); for nontrivial character the default is twice this, though it is **not known** to be large enough in all such cases — one may wish to increase it via `SetHeckeBound`.
Sets the bound `n` used internally for which `T₁,…,Tₙ` generate the Hecke algebra as a `Z`-module. Setting it too low can produce incorrect results.
The Hecke algebra `TQ` over `Q` such that `Generators(TQ)` generates `Z[T₁,T₂,…]` as a `Z`-module. If `Bound` is set, only computes the algebra generated by `Tₙ` with `n ≤ Bound`.
The discriminant of the Hecke algebra associated to `M`. If `Bound` is set, computes the discriminant of the subalgebra generated by `Tₙ`, `n ≤ Bound`.

The order generated by the Fourier coefficients of one of the `q`-expansions of a newform corresponding to `M`, plus a map from the coefficient ring of `qExpansion(A)` to the order. If `Bound` is set (default `−1`), only `aₙ` with `n ≤ Bound` are used.

The number field generated by the Fourier coefficients of one of the `q`-expansions of a newform corresponding to `M`, plus a map from the coefficient ring of `qExpansion(M)` to the field. `M` must be defined over `Q`.

The intersection pairing of the homology classes corresponding to the weight-2 cuspidal modular symbols `x` and `y`. The symbols must have the same parent, which must have trivial character and not be a `+1` or `−1` quotient.

The `q`-expansion of one of the Galois-conjugate newforms associated to the irreducible cuspidal space `M`, to absolute precision `prec` (defaults to the highest precision computed in previous calls, or 8 if none). Coefficients lie in a quotient of a polynomial extension of the base field of `M`. Usually `M` must have been defined using `NewformDecomposition`.

The reduced row-echelon basis of `q`-expansions for the space of modular forms associated to `M` (over base field `K`), to absolute precision `prec`. Parameter `Al` (default `"Newform"`): `"Newform"` computes a basis by finding a newform decomposition, computing `q`-expansions, and taking images under degeneracy maps; `"Universal"` uses the algorithm of Section 4.3 of **[Mer94]** (no newform decomposition needed, but requires more Hecke operators and is usually less efficient in practice).
algorithm: Newform algorithm (default) or Merel's universal Fourier expansion **[Mer94]**.

description: The reduced integral basis of `q`-expansions for the space of modular forms associated to `M` (or to the given sequence of spaces), to absolute precision `prec`. The base field must be the rationals or a cyclotomic field. Parameter `Al` (default `"Newform"`).

The sequence of Hecke eigenvalues `[a₂, a₃, a₅, a₇, …, a_p]`, where `p` is the largest prime `≤ prec`. With `K` the base field, the `a_ℓ` lie in `K` or an extension (constructed as a number field or a quotient of `K[x]`). `M` must correspond to a single Galois-conjugacy class of newforms.
The special value `L(M, j)`, where `j` is an integer in the critical strip (`1 ≤ j ≤ k−1`). `M` must have sign 0; `prec` is the number of `q`-expansion terms used.
algorithm: Approximation via `q`-expansions of the conjugate newforms.

description: The leading coefficient `a_r` of the Taylor expansion of `L(M, s)` about the critical integer `j`, together with the order of vanishing `r` of `L(M, s)` at `s = 1`.

The volume of `A_M(R)`. With `S ⊂ C[[q]]` the cusp forms associated to `M` and a basis `f₁,…,f_d` of `S ∩ Z[[q]]`, the period map `Φ` sends `x ∈ H` to `(⟨f₁,x⟩,…,⟨f_d,x⟩) ∈ Cᵈ`; the cokernel of `Φ` is `A_M(C)`, and the standard measure on `Cᵈ` induces the measure used. See Section 3.12.16 of **[Ste00]**.
The volume of the subgroup of `A_M(C)` on which complex conjugation acts as `−1`.

The rational number `L(A,j)·(j−1)! / ((2π)^{j−1}·Ω)`, where `1 ≤ j ≤ k−1` and `Ω` is `RealVolume(M)` when `j` is odd and `MinusVolume(M)` when `j` is even. If `Bound` is set (default `−1`), `LRatio` is only a divisibility upper bound. If `Sign(M)` is not 0, the result is only correct up to a power of 2.
The odd part of `LRatio(M, j)` (hopefully faster to compute than the full odd part of `LRatio(M, j)`).
algorithm: Odd part of the period ratio.

description: The winding element `Y^{k−2}{0,∞}`.
The winding element `X^{i−1}Y^{k−2−(i−1)}{0,∞}`.
The element `Σ_{a ∈ (Z/mZ)*} ε(a) X^{i−1}Y^{k−2−(i−1)}{0, a/m}`.

The image under `RationalMapping(M)` of the lattice generated by the images of the `j`th winding element under all Hecke operators `Tₙ`. If `M` is the ambient space, the image under `RationalMapping(M)` is not taken. Parameter `Bound` (default `−1`).
algorithm: Hecke-image lattice of the winding element.

description: The image under `RationalMapping(M)` of the vector space generated by all images of `WindingElement(M,j)` under all Hecke operators `Tₙ`. If `M` is the ambient space, the rational period mapping is not applied. Parameter `Bound` (default `−1`).
algorithm: Hecke-image submodule of the winding element.

description: The Hecke submodule of `Φ(M)` generated by the image of the `j`th `ε`-twisted modular winding element, where `Φ = RationalMapping(M)`. In characteristic 0, if `M` is new of weight 2, sign `+1` or `−1`, corresponding to `{f_i}` Galois-conjugate newforms, the dimension of the twisted winding submodule equals the number of `f_i` with `L(f_i, eps, 1) ≠ 0`.
algorithm: Hecke-image submodule of the twisted winding element.

description: The cyclic subgroup of the complex torus attached to `M` generated by the image under the period map of the modular symbol `x`.
An abelian group isomorphic to the finite group generated by the images `π(s[i])` in the complex torus attached to `M`, where `π = PeriodMapping(M)`.

The kernel of the modular isogeny. With `T` the complex torus attached to `M`, the modular isogeny is the natural map from the dual of `T` into `T` induced by autoduality of `CuspidalSubspace(AmbientSpace(M))`.

The congruence group `S/(V+W)` of cusp forms corresponding to `M`, where `S = Sₖ(Γ₀(N),Z)`, `V` is the sub-`Z`-module for `M`, and `W` its orthogonal complement. Encodes congruences between forms in `V` and its complement. Parameter `Bound` (default `−1` ⇒ `HeckeBound(M)+1`, a provably correct answer); if too small, only an upper bound.
An abelian group encoding the intersection of the complex tori for `M1`, `M2` (which must share an ambient space). When finite, it is isomorphic to `A_{M1}(C) ∩ A_{M2}(C)`.
An abelian group encoding the intersection of the collection of complex tori for the sequence `S` of spaces.
The period mapping attached to `M`, computed using `prec` terms of the `q`-expansions of the modular forms associated to `M`.
The complex period lattice associated to `M`, using `prec` terms of the `q`-expansions.
The value `r_j(f) = ∫₀^{i∞} f(z) zʲ dz`.
A surjective linear map from the ambient space of `M` to a vector space whose kernel equals the kernel of the period mapping.

A surjective linear map from the ambient space of `M` to a vector space, kernel equal to the kernel of the period mapping, chosen so that the image of `IntegralBasis(CuspidalSubspace(AmbientSpace(M)))` is the standard `Z`-lattice. `M` must be defined over `Q`.
algorithm: Integral normalisation of the rational mapping.

description: The modular degree of `M`; the square root of `#ModularKernel(M)` (`M` weight 2, trivial character). When `M` corresponds to an elliptic curve `E = A_M`, this is the degree of the induced map `X₀(N) → E`.
The congruence number `r`; the index in `Sₖ(Γ₀(N),Z)` of the sum `L+W` of the lattice `W` of cusp forms for `M` and the complementary lattice `L`. Parameter `Bound` (default `−1`).

An upper bound `gcd{#A(F_p) : 3 ≤ p ≤ maxp, p ∤ N}` on the order of the torsion subgroup of the abelian variety `A` attached to `M` (an isogeny invariant, hence also a bound for the dual `A^∨`). For a lower bound, use `#SubgroupOfTorus(M,WindingElement(M))`.

subsection: 133.16.2 Tamagawa Numbers and Orders of Component Groups
description: The order of the component group at `p`; the order of the group of `F̄_p`-points of the component group of the reduction mod `p` of the Néron model of the abelian variety attached to `M`. `p` must exactly divide the level. If `Sign(M)` is not 0, only the odd part is returned.
algorithm: Monodromy pairing on the character group **[Ste01, KS00, Mes86]**.

subsection: 133.16.2 Tamagawa Numbers and Orders of Component Groups
description: The order of the group of `F_p`-rational points of the component group of `M`. `M` must be associated to a single Galois-conjugacy class of newforms.

subsection: 133.16.2 Tamagawa Numbers and Orders of Component Groups
description: The number of connected components of `A_M(R)`.

subsection: 133.16.2 Tamagawa Numbers and Orders of Component Groups
description: The number of connected components of the subgroup `A_M(C)⁻` of `A_M(C)` on which complex conjugation acts as `−1`.
The space `M` of modular symbols associated to the elliptic curve `E` (with given `sign`).

An elliptic curve over `Q` in the isogeny class associated to `M`. Parameter `Database` (default `true`): uses the Cremona database; set `false` to compute from scratch (not optimized for large level).

Given an elliptic curve over `Q` and a prime `p` of multiplicative or good ordinary reduction, computes the `p`-adic `L`-series. `E` must be a global minimal model. Parameters: `CoefficientPrecision` (default 3), `SeriesPrecision` (default 5), `QuadraticTwist` (default 1; computes the series for the twist by a fundamental discriminant `D` coprime to the conductor), `ProperScaling` (default `true`; ensures correct scaling of the `p`-adic `L`-series).
algorithm: Computes modular symbols (`~N³` time) and evaluates `~2(p−1)pⁿ` of them.

description: The dimension of `Sₖ(Γ₀(N))` of weight `k` cusp forms for `Γ₀(N)`.
The dimension of the new subspace of `Sₖ(Γ₀(N))`.
The dimension of `Sₖ(Γ₁(N))`.
The dimension of the new subspace of `Sₖ(Γ₁(N))`.
The dimension of `Sₖ(Γ₁(N))(ε)` of weight `k`, character `eps` (level `N` = modulus of `eps`). Computed using the formula of Cohen and Oesterlé **[CO77]**.

Given a product `D` of an odd number of primes and an integer `m` with valuation at most 1 at each prime divisor `p` of `D`, return the Brandt module of level `(D, m)` over the integers. If unspecified, the conductor `m` is taken to be 1. Parameter `ComputeGrams` (default `true`): when `false`, the `h × h` array of reduced Gram matrices of the quaternion ideal norm forms (`h` = left class number of level `(D, m)`) is not computed; instead the basis of quaternion ideals is stored and the degree-`p` ideal homomorphisms are computed to find the Hecke operator `T_p` for each prime `p`. Setting `false` is more space-efficient; computing the Gram matrices is preferable for moderate levels where many Hecke operators are wanted.
algorithm: Classical Brandt-matrix construction via reduced Gram matrices of quaternion ideal norm forms, with Hecke operators from theta series; or, with `ComputeGrams := false`, ideal-homomorphism enumeration **[Mes86]**.

description: Given a definite order `A` in a quaternion algebra over **Q**, returns the Brandt module on the left ideal classes for `A`, as a module over `R`. If unspecified, `R` is taken to be the integers. Parameter `ComputeGrams` as above.
algorithm: As above, over the left ideal classes of `A`.

description: Forms the Brandt module with coefficient ring base-extended to `R`.

An alternative to `BrandtModule(D, N)` using a *different algorithm*, preferable when `N` is not very small. Constructs the Brandt module attached to an Eichler order of level `N` inside the maximal order `M`; the algorithm avoids explicitly working with the Eichler order.
algorithm: New ideal-free algorithm: works inside the maximal order, avoiding explicit construction of the Eichler order and its ideals.

description: Given a sequence or module element `x` compatible with the Brandt module `M`, forms the corresponding element in `M`.
For a Brandt module `M` and integer `i`, returns the `i`-th basis element.
Scalar multiplication of a Brandt module element `x` by an element `a` in the base ring.
Given a Brandt module element `x` and an element `T` of the algebra of Hecke operators of degree compatible with the parent of `x` or its ambient module, returns the image of `x` under `T`.
The sum of two Brandt module elements.
The difference of two Brandt module elements.
Returns `true` if `x` and `y` are equal elements of the same Brandt module.
Returns the sequence of coefficients of the Brandt module element `x`.
Returns the inner product of `x` and `y` with respect to the canonical pairing on their common parent.
Returns the inner product of the Brandt module element `x` with itself.
The category, `ModBrdt` or `ModBrdtElt`, of the Brandt module `M` or of the Brandt module element `x`.
The parent module `M` of a Brandt module element `x`.
Returns `true` if `M` is the parent of `x`.
The level of the Brandt module — the product of the discriminant and the conductor, equal to the reduced discriminant of its defining quaternion order.
The discriminant of the quaternion algebra **H** with respect to which `M` is defined (the product of the primes ramifying in **H**).
The conductor, i.e. the index of the defining quaternion order of `M` in a maximal order of its quaternion algebra.
The ring over which the Brandt module `M` is defined.
The basis of the Brandt module `M`.
The full module of level `(D, m)` containing a given module of this level.
Returns `true` if and only if the Brandt module `M` is its own ambient module.
The rank of the Brandt module `M` over its base ring.
The degree of `M`, defined to be the dimension of its ambient module.
The matrix `(⟨uᵢ, uⱼ⟩)` defined with respect to the basis `{uᵢ}` of the Brandt module `M`.
The Gram matrix of the ambient module of the Brandt module `M`.

Constructs the quaternionic ideals corresponding to the basis of `M`. Only implemented when `M` was constructed using `BrandtModule(M, N)` (the new algorithm, which avoids constructing these ideals explicitly).

The Eisenstein subspace of `M`. When the level of `M` is square-free this is the submodule generated by a vector of the form `(w/w₁, …, w/wₙ)`, if it exists in `M`, where `wᵢ` is the number of automorphisms of the `i`-th basis ideal and `w = LCM({wᵢ})`.

The cuspidal subspace, defined to be the orthogonal complement of the Eisenstein subspace of `M`. If the discriminant of `M` is coprime to the conductor, the cuspidal subspace consists of the vectors `(a₁, …, aₙ)` with `Σᵢ aᵢ = 0`.
algorithm: Orthogonal complement of the Eisenstein subspace.

description: The Brandt module orthogonal to `M` in the ambient module of `M`.
algorithm: Orthogonal complement w.r.t. the canonical inner product.

description: The intersection of the Brandt modules `M` and `N`.

A decomposition of `M` with respect to the Atkin–Lehner operators and Hecke operators up to the bound `B`. Parameter `Sort` (default `true`): when `true`, returns a sequence sorted under the operator `lt`.
algorithm: Simultaneous diagonalisation under Atkin–Lehner and Hecke operators `Tₙ`, `n ≤ B`.

description: Sort the sequence `D` of spaces of Brandt modules with respect to the `lt` comparison operator.
Returns `true` if and only if `M` is contained in the Eisenstein subspace of the ambient module.
Returns `true` if and only if `M` is contained in the cuspidal subspace of the ambient module.
Returns `true` if and only if `M` does not decompose into complementary Hecke-invariant submodules under the Atkin–Lehner operators, nor under the Hecke operators `Tₙ` for `n ≤ B`.
Returns `true` if and only if `M1` is contained in the module `M2`.

For two indecomposable subspaces, returns `true` if and only if `M1 < M2` under the ordering: (1) by dimension (smaller is less); (2) an Eisenstein subspace is less than a cuspidal subspace of the same dimension; (3) by Atkin–Lehner eigenvalues, starting with the *smallest* prime dividing the level and with '+' less than '−'; (4) by `|Tr(T_{pⁱ}(Mⱼ))|`, `p` not dividing the level and `1 ≤ i ≤ g` with `g = Dimension(M1)`, the positive one being smaller in the event of equality. Parameter `Bound` (default 101): returns `false` if all primes up to `Bound` fail to differentiate the arguments.
algorithm: Lexicographic ordering on dimension / Eisenstein-vs-cuspidal / Atkin–Lehner / Hecke-trace data. Condition (4) differs from the modular-symbols version but permits comparison of arbitrary Brandt modules.

description: The complement of `lt` for Brandt modules `M1` and `M2`. Parameter `Bound` (default 101).
A matrix representing the `n`-th Hecke operator `Tₙ` with respect to `Basis(M)` for the Brandt module `M`.
algorithm: Theta series of the Brandt/Gram matrices (default), or `p`-neighbour ideal enumeration **[Mes86]** when `ComputeGrams := false`.

description: The Atkin–Lehner operator on `M`, where `p` is a prime dividing the discriminant of `M`.
The theta series associated to the pair `(x, y)` of elements of a Brandt module, as an element of a power series ring.
algorithm: Theta series of the pairing of `x` and `y`.

description: A sequence of power series elements, to precision `prec`, spanning the image of the theta functions associated to pairs in the Brandt module `M`.
algorithm: Spans the theta-function image of pairs in `M`.

description: The dimension of the Brandt module of level `(D, N)`.
The dimension of the Brandt module of level `(D, N)` over **F**_q[t].
The dimension of the new subspace of the Brandt module of level `(D, N)`.
Constructs the Brandt module attached to an Eichler order of level `N` in the maximal order `M`.
The defining quaternion order of the Brandt module `M`.
Level, discriminant, conductor (as over the integers).
The quaternionic ideals corresponding to the basis of `M`.
The Gram matrix of the ambient module of `M`.
A matrix representing the `n`-th Hecke operator `Tₙ` with respect to `Basis(M)`.
The common eigenvectors for the Hecke operators on the Brandt module `M`, as elements of `M`.
For a Hecke eigenform `f` in a Brandt module, the eigenvalue for the Hecke operator at the prime `p`.

The module `M` of supersingular points on `X₀(N)` over `\overline{F}_p`; equivalently the free abelian group on the supersingular elliptic curves in characteristic `p` enhanced with level `N` structure. Requires `N` and `p` coprime. Parameter `Brandt` (`BoolElt`, default `false`): forces computation via quaternion arithmetic (Brandt modules) even when the graph method would apply (and be faster).
algorithm: Mestre–Oesterlé method of graphs when `N ∈ {1,2,3,5,7,13}` **[Mes86]**; otherwise Brandt modules **[Piz80, Koh01]**. `Brandt := true` forces the Brandt-module algorithm.

description: The Hecke module `M` of divisors of degree 0 on the supersingular points on `X₀(1)` over `\overline{F}_p`; equivalently the free abelian group on the supersingular `j`-invariants in characteristic `p`.
The `i`-th basis element of the module `M`.
The coercion of `x` into the module `M`.

The cuspidal submodule `X` of `M`: the submodule of divisors of degree 0 on the supersingular points (the subspace of elements whose coefficients sum to 0). "Cuspidal" because `X ⊗ `**Q** is isomorphic as a Hecke module to the space `S₂(Γ₀(Np); `**Q**`)`^{p-new} of `p`-new cuspforms with rational Fourier coefficients.
The Eisenstein submodule of `M`: the orthogonal complement of the cuspidal subspace of `M` with respect to the monodromy pairing.
algorithm: Orthogonal complement under the monodromy pairing.

description: The orthogonal complement of the module `M` in the ambient space with respect to the monodromy pairing.

The kernel of `I` on the module `M`: the subspace obtained by intersecting the kernels of the operators `f_n(T_{p_n})`, where `I` is a sequence `[⟨p₁, f₁(x)⟩, …, ⟨p_n, f_n(x)⟩]` of pairs (prime number, polynomial).
Decomposition of the module `M` with respect to the Hecke operators `T₁, T₂, …, Tₙ`.
algorithm: Simultaneous Hecke-operator decomposition (a few operators usually suffice for a complete decomposition).

description: A basis for `M` as a **Z**-module.
The (auxiliary) level of the module `M`; for `SupersingularModule(N, p)` this is, by definition, `N`.
The base ring of `M` (currently always **Z**).
The sum of the coefficients of the module element `P`, written with respect to the basis of the ambient space of the parent of `M`.
The dimension of the module `M`.
A sequence of integers defining the module element `P`.
The level of the module `M`; for `SupersingularModule(N, p)` this is, by definition, `Np`.
The equation of `X₀(N)` used when applying the Mestre method to compute with the supersingular module `M`.
The prime of the module `M`; for `SupersingularModule(N, p)` this is, by definition, `p`.
The Brandt module associated to the supersingular module `M` (exists even when the underlying computations on `M` use the Mestre–Oesterlé graph method).
The space of modular symbols corresponding to the supersingular module `M`. Parameter `Proof` (`BoolElt`, default `true`).
The `+1` or `−1` quotient (per `sign`) of the space of modular symbols corresponding to `M`. Parameter `Proof` (`BoolElt`, default `true`).
The **Z**-module `V` underlying the supersingular module `M`, together with an invertible map `V → M`.
`true` if `M` is the full module of supersingular points and not a submodule.
`true` if the supersingular modules `M₁` and `M₂` are equal.
`true` if the module elements `P` and `Q` are equal.
`true` if the supersingular module `M₁` is a subset of `M₂`.
`true` if the underlying computations on `M` are done using Brandt modules.
`true` if the underlying computations on `M` are done using the Mestre–Oesterlé method of graphs.
Sum, difference, and left scalar multiple of module elements.
The submodule generated by all sums of elements in the supersingular modules `M₁` and `M₂`.
The intersection of the supersingular modules `M₁` and `M₂`.
A matrix representing the `n`-th Hecke operator `Tₙ` with respect to `Basis(M)` for the supersingular module `M`.
A matrix representing the Atkin–Lehner involution `W_q` on the supersingular module `M`. The number `q` must equal either `Prime(M)` or `AuxiliaryLevel(M)`.
The monodromy pairing of elements `P` and `Q` of a supersingular module.
The diagonal entries that define the monodromy pairing on the ambient space.

The modular abelian variety `J₀(N)` of level `N` and weight 2 (or weight `k ≥ 2`), i.e. the Jacobian of `X₀(N)`. Parameter `Sign` (`RngIntElt`, default 0) selects the `+1` or `−1` quotient of homology.

subsection: 136.2.2 Creating the Modular Jacobians J₁(N) and J_H(N)
description: The modular abelian variety `J₁(N)` of level `N` and weight `k` (or 2), i.e. the Jacobian of `X₁(N)`. Parameter `Sign` (default 0). Note: finding the integral structure on the isogenous `J_s(N)` is much faster; computing with `J₁(N)` itself may be expensive.

subsection: 136.2.2 Creating the Modular Jacobians J₁(N) and J_H(N)

description: Let `c` be the product of Tamagawa numbers at bad primes. Returns a divisor of `c`, an integer some power of which is a multiple of `c`, and `true` if the divisor is provably equal to `c`. `A` over `Q`, attached to a newform.
algorithm: As above, over all bad primes.

description: An elliptic curve over `Q` isogenous to the dimension-1 variety `A`, if one exists. (For weight > 2 use `EllipticInvariants`.)

A modular abelian variety over `Q` isogenous to the elliptic curve `E`. Parameter `Sign` (`RngIntElt`, default 0). (Can be slow: small-coefficient curves may have large conductor, hence a large `J₀(N)` quotient.)
The invariants `c₄, c₆, j` and an elliptic curve of the dimension-1 variety `A`, using `n` terms of `q`-expansion.
The elliptic periods `w₁, w₂` of the `J₀(N)`-optimal elliptic curve associated to `A`, using `n` terms (`w₁/w₂` has positive imaginary part).

The space of Hilbert modular forms over field `F` (a number field or the rationals) on Γ₀(N) with weight `k`. The level `N` should be an ideal in the maximal order of `F`; `k` should be a sequence of deg(F/**Q**) integers, all at least 2 and all of the same parity. If `k` is not specified, the weight is taken to be parallel weight 2, i.e. `[2, 2, ..., 2]`. Parameter `QuaternionOrder` (`AlgAssVOrd`) lets the user specify the order used; otherwise it is chosen automatically (and hidden). The quaternion algebra may be definite (ramified at all infinite places of `F` ⇒ Algorithm I) or indefinite (ramified at all infinite places except one ⇒ Algorithm II). Indefinite algebras may only be used for parallel weight 2, and the algebra must be unramified at all finite primes (for full cuspidal spaces). In the definite case the order must be maximal; in the indefinite case it must be an Eichler order of discriminant equal to the level `N`.
algorithm: Realises the space as automorphic forms on a quaternion order via the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence; definite ⇒ Brandt-module Algorithm I **[Dem07, DD08]**, indefinite ⇒ Shimura-curve Algorithm II **[GV11, Voi09]**.

description: The field on which the space `M` was defined.
The weight of the space `M`.
The central character of the weight representation defining `M`. Significant only for higher-weight spaces (not parallel weight 2).
The level of the space `M`.
The nebentypus of the space `M`.
True if `M` was created as (a subspace of) a space of cusp forms. In the current implementation always `true`.
True if `M` was created as (a subspace of) a new space (e.g. via `NewSubspace` or `NewformDecomposition`), or if `M` is known to satisfy `NewLevel(M) = Level(M)`.
The level at which `M` is known to be new (see `NewSubspace`).

The dimension of the space `M`. Parameter `UseFormula` (`BoolElt`, default `true`): determines the dimension either by "dimension formulae" or by explicitly constructing the space; by default formulae are used when available and cheap, and can be forced on/off via `UseFormula`.
algorithm: Dimension formulae are implemented for parallel weight 2 (sums over certain cyclotomic extensions of the base field of `F`). Formula results are guaranteed only under GRH (they may involve conditionally computed class numbers); if the space is later explicitly computed, the dimension is verified unconditionally.

description: The quaternion order used internally to compute the space `M`.

Indicates which of the two algorithms is used to compute `M`. Equivalent to `IsDefinite(Algebra(QuaternionOrder(M)))`. Calling this causes a `QuaternionOrder` for `M` to be chosen (if not already set).
The space of Hilbert modular forms containing `f`.
The field over which the Hilbert modular form `f` is defined. This is either equal to, or an extension of, the base field of `Parent(f)`.
A matrix representing the Hecke operator T_P on the space `M`.
algorithm: Double-coset Hecke action via the quaternion order (Algorithm I/II).

description: A matrix representing the Atkin–Lehner operator w_P on the space `M`.

Degeneracy maps in the "downward" direction, as maps from `M` to itself. Here `M` has level `N`, `P` is a prime dividing `N`, and `Q` equals either `P` or the unit ideal `(1)`. Returns a matrix representing a map from `M` to `M` whose image equals a copy of the space of level `N/P`. When `Q = (1)`, this is the double-coset operator defined by cosets of an element of determinant 1 (a "norm" map); when `Q = P`, the double-coset operator defined by cosets of an element of determinant `Norm(P)`.

Procedures that delete data obtained during the precomputation phase of the "definite" algorithm (Algorithm I). This data is used to compute Hecke (and other) operators for given primes and is re-usable for all spaces computed with the same quaternion order `O` (often the same for all weights and levels over a given number field). The data is stored by default since it is the most expensive part of the Hecke computation, but is very memory-intensive; these procedures reclaim that memory.

Given a cuspidal space `M` of level `N` and an ideal `I` dividing `N`, the subspace of `M` consisting of forms new at the ideal `I` (or new at `N`, if `I` is not given) — the complement of the space generated by all images under degeneracy maps of spaces of level `N/P` for primes `P` dividing `I`. `I` must be squarefree and coprime to `N/I`. The new subspace is not necessarily an explicit subspace of `M`: in many cases it is obtained explicitly by computing degeneracy maps, otherwise it is computed independently of `M` using an automatically chosen quaternion order. Parameter `QuaternionOrder` (`AlgAssVOrd`) overrides the automatic choice (allowable orders as for `HilbertCuspForms`, but here the quaternion algebra may be ramified at finite primes dividing `I`; when indefinite, the ramified finite primes must be precisely those dividing `I`). In the non-parallel weight case, set `RationalBasis := false` to defer computing a rational basis (later set it with `SetRationalBasis`).
algorithm: New subspace via degeneracy maps, or computed independently on a separate quaternion order; a different algorithm and order may be chosen for the new subspace than for the containing space.

description: Procedure that changes the basis of `M` to a rational basis (full explanation in §137.5). If the basis of `M` is already known to be rational, nothing is done; in particular this has no effect on parallel-weight-2 spaces. After invocation, the basis of `M` is never modified again.
A bound on the absolute value of the Hecke eigenvalue at the prime `P` that must hold for all newforms in the space `M`.
Given a space `M` created as a `NewSubspace`, decomposes `M` into subspaces that are irreducible modules under the Hecke action.
algorithm: Simultaneous diagonalisation under the Hecke action.

description: The list of new eigenforms in `M` with rational eigenvalues, i.e. the 1-dimensional components of `NewformDecomposition`. `M` need not be a new space. Avoids constructing the new subspace of `M` and uses bounds on the eigenvalues.
algorithm: Targeted search for rational (degree-1) eigenforms using eigenvalue bounds.

description: An eigenform contained in the space `M`, which should be an irreducible module under the Hecke action (e.g. a space obtained from `NewformDecomposition`).
A list containing an eigenform from each space in `NewformDecomposition(M)`.
Given a space `M` constructed using `NewformDecomposition`, the number field over which the `Eigenform` of `M` is defined.
The eigenvalue of the Hecke operator T_P acting on the eigenform `f` (which should be a Hilbert modular form constructed using `Eigenform`).

chapter_title: Modular Forms over Imaginary Quadratic Fields

The admissible representation of GL₂(Q_p) associated to the cuspidal eigenform specified by the space of modular symbols `M`. `M` must be cuspidal and contain only a single Galois conjugacy class of newforms (such spaces are created with `NewformDecomposition`).
The central character of π (an admissible representation on GL(Q_p)): a Dirichlet character of `p`-power conductor.
The conductor of π, written multiplicatively.
The space of modular symbols from which π was created.

Returns `true` if the conductor of π cannot be lowered by twisting by a character of Q_p^×. If π is not minimal, also returns a minimal representation π′ and a Dirichlet character χ with π = π′ twisted by χ. Equivalent to `IsMinimalTwist(DefiningModularSymbolsSpace(pi))` being true.
algorithm: Reduction to `IsMinimalTwist` of the defining modular symbols space.

description: `true` iff the admissible representation π belongs to the principal series.
`true` iff the admissible representation π is supercuspidal.

For a principal series representation π of GL₂(Q_p): two Dirichlet characters of `p`-power conductor representing the restriction to Z_p^× × Z_p^× of the character of the split torus of GL₂(Q_p) associated to π.

For a minimal supercuspidal representation π of GL₂(Q_p): a cuspidal inducing datum `(K, Ξ)` giving rise to π. Since Ξ factors through a finite quotient `K/K₁` of `K`, the function returns a representation of `K/K₁`, from which one deduces the representation on `K`, hence π.
algorithm: Construction of the inducing datum (see §139.1.4), **[BH06]** Ch. 15.

description: For a minimal representation π of GL₂(Q_p): the representation of the Weil group associated to π under the local Langlands correspondence (see §139.1.5). Returns four objects `G, α, L, ρ`: `L/Q_p` is a finite Galois extension through which the representation factors, `G` an abstract group, α a bijective map identifying `G` with Gal(L/Q_p), and ρ a `G`-module describing the Weil representation on Gal(L/Q_p). Parameter `Precision` (`RngIntElt`, default 10). See Chapter 90 for group modules.

For an ordinary minimal supercuspidal representation π of GL₂(Q_p): the associated admissible pair `(E, χ)` (see §139.1.5). Returns a quadratic field extension `E/Q_p` and a character χ of the unit group of `E` (χ can only be evaluated on units of `E`).

Constructs an abstract simplicial complex with the faces in the list `f`. The argument should be a sequence of sets; there is no requirement on the element type, but several constructions require integer entries (see `Normalization`).
algorithm: Subset closure of the given faces.

description: Constructs a 1-dimensional simplicial complex isomorphic to the graph `G`.
Constructs a simplicial complex with an `n`-simplex for each `n`-clique in the graph `G`.
Returns the dimension of the highest-dimensional face of the simplicial complex `X`. (A face with `n` elements has dimension `n − 1`.)

Returns the faces of degree `d` (number of elements `d`, one more than the dimension). The order returned for each degree is also the correspondence between faces and the basis of the corresponding module in the chain complex built from the complex. Returns an empty sequence if there are no faces of the requested degree.
Returns the facets of `X` — the faces that are not subsets of any other face. This is what the normal printing mode of a complex outputs.

Relabels the vertices (elements of the face sets) of `X` using `1, 2, 3, …`, ensuring the complex is built on subsets of the integers — a prerequisite for several functions. The functional first signature copies `X` and returns a new complex; the procedural `~` signature modifies `X` in place.
Shifts all integer vertices of the normalized complex `X` by an offset `n`. Functional `vs` procedural (`~`) signatures as above.
Returns the simplicial complex generated by all simplices lying in the boundary of `X`. Useful for building a complex representing the `n`-sphere (e.g. the boundary of an `(n+1)`-simplex).
Returns the topological sum (disjoint union) of two simplicial complexes. Requires both complexes to be normalized (see `Normalization`).

Compares two simplicial complexes. Does **not** attempt to find an isomorphism; ensures the vertices lie in the same universe and then does a set comparison on the set of faces. (Shifting/relabelling breaks equality.)
Returns the cartesian product of two simplicial complexes. Works on any complexes; the new vertices are pairs of vertices from the component complexes.
algorithm: Cartesian product of vertex sets / faces.

description: Constructs the join of two complexes: the complex generated by faces of the form `{x₁,…,xᵣ, y₁,…,yₛ}` for `{x₁,…,xᵣ} ∈ S` and `{y₁,…,yₛ} ∈ T`. Requires both complexes to be normalized.

Adds either a single simplex `s` (a set) or a sequence of simplices to a simplicial complex. The functional versions return a new complex with the added simplices; the procedural (`~`) versions change `X` in place.
Removes a face `f` and all faces containing `f` from `X`. If `f` is not a face, `X` is returned unchanged. Functional `vs` procedural (`~`) signatures as above.

In the complex `X`, identifies all vertices paired in the sequence `e` (a sequence of pairs of elements of the face sets). The identification eliminates the first component of each pair, replacing it with the second wherever it occurs in `X`. Functional `vs` procedural (`~`) signatures as above.
Constructs the barycentric subdivision of `X`: abstractly, the complex whose faces are chains `X₁ ⊂ … ⊂ Xₙ` of faces of `X`. The new complex has more faces but the same homotopy type as the old.
algorithm: Order complex of the face poset.

description: Returns the `q`-skeleton of `X`: the complex consisting of all faces of `X` of dimension at most `q`.
Constructs a graph isomorphic to the 1-skeleton of `X`.
Constructs the cone over `X`: generated by all faces of `X` with an additional vertex included in each face. Any cone is acyclic (all homology groups vanish). Requires a normalized complex.
algorithm: Adjoin apex vertex to every face.

description: Constructs the suspension (double cone) over the normalized complex `X`. The suspension shifts all homology groups up by one dimension.

Returns a simplicial complex triangulating the `n`-sphere.

Returns a triangulation of a torus as an abstract simplicial complex.
Returns a triangulation of a cylinder as an abstract simplicial complex.
Returns a triangulation of the Möbius strip as an abstract simplicial complex.
Constructs the lens space `L(p, 1)`, which has a 1-dimensional homology generator of order `p`.
Constructs a triangulation of the projective plane.

Calculates the reduced homology of `X` with coefficients in the ring `A`. If no ring is given, defaults to integer coefficients. The procedural (`~`) form caches the results of the calculation in the complex object. Returns the homology modules (in falling dimension) and the connecting maps from the chain modules.
algorithm: Reduced homology of the simplicial chain complex over `A`.

description: Calculates and returns the `q`-th homology group of `X` with coefficients in `A` (default integers). If homology is cached in `X`, the cached result is returned. Does **not** compute the entire homology in order to return one group.
algorithm: Single-degree homology of the chain complex.

description: Returns the `q`-th Betti number, the free rank of the `q`-dimensional homology group with coefficients in `A` (default integers). Compensates for homology being reduced: `BettiNumber(X, 0) eq Rank(HomologyGroup(X, 0)) + 1`.
Returns the torsion coefficients of the `q`-th homology group of `X` with coefficients in `A` (default integers).
Computes the Euler characteristic of the complex. If homology is cached, it is used; otherwise the characteristic is computed from the ranks of the chain groups.
algorithm: Alternating sum of homology ranks (cached) or chain-group ranks.

description: Returns the `q`-th boundary matrix of the chain complex corresponding to `X` with coefficients in `A`.

Constructs a reduced chain complex of free `A`-modules corresponding to `X`. The produced complex includes one extra rank-1 module on each end, with the zero map leading to it, simulating the maps to/from the zero module that would terminate an ordinary simplicial chain complex.

Prints generators of the homology groups of `X` with coefficients in `A`, together with their order, in order of dimension. The three-argument form expects `H, M` to be the result of `H, M := ChainComplex(A, smp);`. Recalculates homology each time unless already cached via `Homology(A, smp)`. Each generator is printed with a prefix giving its order (so torsion elements are recognizable). Defaults to integer coefficients.
algorithm: Condensed bases of the homology groups with chain representatives.

section: 142.2 Construction of Incidence and Coset Geometries
description: Construct the incidence geometry `IG` having the (labelled) graph `G` as incidence graph. If `G` is unlabelled, the elements of `IG` are the vertices and edges of `G`, the types are `{@ 1, 2 @}` (type 1 = vertices, type 2 = edges), and a type-1 element `x` is incident to a type-2 element `y` iff vertex `x` lies on edge `y`. `true` iff the polyhedra `P` and `Q` are equal (same toric lattice, identical supports).
The intersection of the cones `C` and `D`; they must lie in the same toric lattice.
The intersection of the polyhedra `P` and `Q`; they must lie in the same toric lattice.
`true` iff the support of polyhedron `P` is contained in that of `Q`; both must lie in the same toric lattice.
The Minkowski sum of the cones `C` and `D`, or of the polyhedra `P` and `Q`.
The polyhedron constructed as the Minkowski sum of the polytope `P` and the cone `C`.
The convex hull of the Cartesian product of the polyhedra `P` and `Q`.
The dilation of the polyhedron `P` by the rational number `k`.
The negation of the polyhedron `P`.

section: 143.3 Basic Combinatorics of Polytopes and Polyhedra
description: The cone `C` such that `C + v` is a supporting cone of the polyhedron `P`, where `v` is a vertex of `P`.
The integral toric lattice points, the strictly interior lattice points, or the boundary lattice points of the polytope `P`.
The number of integral toric lattice points of the polytope `P`.
The rational generating function of the Ehrhart series for the polytope `P`.

A sequence representing the Ehrhart (quasi-)polynomial for `P`: a sequence of polynomials `[p_0,…,p_{r−1}]` of length `r`, the quasi-period, so that the number of lattice points of the dilation `nP` is `p_s(k)` where `n = kr + s` is the Euclidean division of `n` by `r` (`s` is the least residue of `n` mod `r`). Since Magma indexes sequences from 1, `p_i = EhrhartPolynomial(P)[i+1]`.
The first `l + 1` coefficients of the Ehrhart series for `P` (starting with `0P` up to and including `lP`).
The number of lattice points in the (non-negative, integral) dilation `kP` of the polytope `P`.
The subgroup of `GL(n, Z)` (acting on the ambient lattice) which leaves the polyhedron `P` unchanged.
A sequence of polytopes that make a triangulation of the polytope `P`.
A sequence of polytopes that make a triangulation of the boundary of the polytope `P`.

If `C` lies in a toric lattice `L`, a finite sequence of elements of `L` that generate `C` as a monoid. Parameter `level` (`RngIntElt`, default `infinity`) restricts the search for generators to that given level; this assumes that `C` is graded.
If `C` lies in a toric lattice `L`, a finite sequence of elements of `L` that generate `C` over `Q⁺`. The list is forced minimal for `MinimalRGenerators`.

The set of integral lattice points in the cone `C` contained in the hyperplane given by the section determined by the dual lattice element `H` at height given by the rational number `h`. The intersection of `H` with `C` is required to be compact.

The polytope defined as the convex hull of the vertices of the polyhedron `P`. This is the smallest polytope which can occur as a factor in an expression of `P` as the Minkowski sum of a polytope and a cone.
The polyhedron defined as the convex hull of the integral points contained in the polyhedron `P`.
The tail cone of the polyhedron `P`.
`true` iff the polyhedron `P` is empty.
`true` iff the cone `C` or polyhedron `P` has dimension equal to that of its ambient lattice.
`true` iff the cone `C` is strictly convex; i.e. there exists a hyperplane `H` such that `C` lies on one side of `H` and meets `H` in the single point 0.
`true` iff the cone `C` or polyhedron `P` is simplicial.
`true` iff the polyhedron `P` is a simplex.
`true` iff the polyhedron `P` is simple.
`true` iff the polyhedron `P` is an affine linear space.
`true` iff the cone `C` is supported at the origin of its ambient toric lattice.
The dimension of the toric cone `C` or polyhedron `P`.
The index of the sublattice generated by the minimal **R**-generators of the cone `C` in its linear span.

`true` iff the integral polytope `P` is shellable; i.e. if there exists a polytope `S` such that each lattice point `u ∈ P` lies on the boundary of `v + i*(S − v)` for some `0 ≤ i ≤ k`, where `v` is the barycentre of the vertices of `P`. If `true`, also returns `S`, `v`, and `k`.
The ambient toric lattice of the toric cone `C` or polyhedron `P`.

Make a cone or polyhedron identical to `C` or `P` but lying in the toric lattice `L`; the identification of the existing ambient toric lattice with `L` is by identification of the two standard bases and requires the dimensions of the two spaces to be equal.
Create an `n`-dimensional toric lattice `Q^n ⊃ Z^n`. The integer `n` must be non-negative.
The unique one-dimensional toric lattice of scalars `Q ⊃ Z`.
The dual lattice of the toric lattice `L`.

The direct sum of the toric lattices `L` and `M`. Also returns the embedding of `L`, the embedding of `M`, the projection onto `L`, and the projection onto `M`. The argument may also be a sequence `Q` of toric lattices, giving three return values: the direct sum, a sequence of inclusion maps, and a sequence of projection maps.

The direct sum of the toric lattice `L` with itself `n` times. Also returns a sequence of injections and a sequence of projections. Identical to `DirectSum([L,L,...,L])` with the sequence of length `n`.
The dimension of the toric lattice `L`.
The point `(a,b,…)` as an element of the toric lattice `L`, where `Q = [a,b,…]` is a sequence of rational numbers or integers. (If `L` is omitted, it will be created.)
The `i`-th standard basis element of the toric lattice `L`.
The standard basis elements of the toric lattice `L` as a sequence of points of `L`.
The point `(a,b,…)` as an element of the dual of the toric lattice `L`, where `Q = [a,b,…]`.
The zero vector in the toric lattice `L`.
The sum and difference of toric lattice points `P` and `Q` (or points of the dual), the rational multiple `nP`, and the quotient `P/n`, where `n ∈ Q`.
`true` iff the toric lattice points `P` and `Q` are the same point of the same lattice.
`true` iff the toric lattice points `P` and `Q` are rational multiples of one another; the factor `Q/P` is returned in that case.
The rational factor `P/Q` in the case that the toric lattice points `P` and `Q` are rational multiples of one another.
`true` iff the toric lattice point `v` lies in the toric lattice `L`.
`true` iff the toric lattice point `v` is the zero vector.
`true` iff the coefficients of the toric lattice point `v` are integral.
`true` iff the toric lattice point `v` is a primitive integral vector; i.e. `v` is not divisible as an integral vector in its ambient toric lattice.
The first toric lattice point on the ray spanned by `v`.
`true` iff the toric lattices `L` and `K` are the same object in Magma (not merely isomorphic).

A toric lattice `L₁` isomorphic to the sublattice of `L` generated by the sequence `Q` of elements of `L`, together with an embedding map of `L₁` in `L`. The constructor `sub< L | Q >` can also be used, although `Q` must be a sequence of elements of `L`.
The toric sublattice of `Q^n ⊃ Z^n` (as a toric lattice) generated by the sequences of integers of length `n` comprising the sequence `Q`.

A toric lattice isomorphic to the quotient of `L` by the linear span of the cone `C`, or by the elements `v ∈ L` comprising the sequence `Q`, or by the single primitive vector `v ∈ L`. The projection map of `L` to the quotient is also returned.
A toric lattice `L₁` isomorphic to the toric lattice generated by `L` together with the vector `v ∈ L` (or by a sequence of vectors of `L`). The inclusion map of `L` in `L₁` is also returned.
`true` iff the toric lattice `L` was constructed as a sublattice of another toric lattice.
`true` iff the toric lattice `L` was constructed as a superlattice of another toric lattice (by the addition of a rational vector).
`true` iff the toric lattice `L` was constructed as the direct sum of other toric lattices.
`true` iff the toric lattice `L` was constructed as the quotient of another toric lattice.
If the toric lattice `L` was constructed as the extension of a toric lattice `K` by the addition of a vector, return `K`.
If the toric lattice `L` was constructed as a sublattice of a toric lattice `K`, return `K`.

If the toric lattice `L` was constructed as a direct sum, return a sequence of the toric lattice summands used (and parallel sequences of their embedding maps in `L` and the projections from `L` to them).
The zero map between toric lattices `L` and `K`.
The identity map on the toric lattice `L`.
The map between toric lattices `L` and `K` determined by the matrix `M` (with respect to the standard bases of `L` and `K`).
The toric lattice map from `L` to the toric lattice `M` determined by the sequence `Q` of toric lattice points, where `M` is the toric lattice containing the points of `Q`.
The defining matrix of the lattice map `f`.
The image of the cone `C`, polyhedron `P` or lattice element `v` under the toric lattice map `f`; the type of the object is preserved.
The preimage of the cone `C`, polyhedron `P` or lattice element `v` by the toric lattice map `f`; the type of the object is preserved.
The inclusion of the kernel of the toric lattice map `f`, regarded as a distinct toric lattice, into the domain of `f`; or the same for the dual subspace annihilated by lattice element `v`.
A basis for the kernel of the toric lattice map `f`, or the dual of the sublattice annihilated by the lattice element `v`.
A basis for the image of the toric lattice map `f`.
`true` iff the cokernel of the toric lattice map `f` is torsion free.
The factorial `n!` for non-negative small integer `n`.
The number of permutations of `n` distinct objects taken `k` at a time.
The binomial coefficient `C(n, r)` = `(n choose r)`.
Given a sequence `Q = [r_1,…,r_k]` of positive integers with `n = r_1 + … + r_k`, the multinomial coefficient `n! / (r_1! ⋯ r_k!)`.
For integer `n`, the `n`-th Fibonacci number `F_n`, defined by `F_0 = 0`, `F_1 = 1`, `F_n = F_{n−1} + F_{n−2}` for all integers `n`. `n` may be negative, with `F_{−n} = (−1)^{n+1} F_n`.
For a small non-negative integer `n`, the `n`-th Catalan number `C_n`, defined by `C_0 = 1`, `C_{n+1} = C_n · (4n + 2)/(n + 2)`.
For integer `n`, the `n`-th Lucas number `L_n`, defined by `L_0 = 2`, `L_1 = 1`, `L_n = L_{n−1} + L_{n−2}` for all integers `n`. `n` may be negative, with `L_{−n} = (−1)^n L_n`.

The `n`-th member of the generalized Fibonacci sequence defined by `G_0 = g0`, `G_1 = g1`, `G_n = G_{n−1} + G_{n−2}` for all integers `n` (`n` may be negative). Fibonacci and Lucas numbers are the special cases `(g0, g1) = (0, 1)` and `(2, 1)` respectively.
algorithm: Two-term linear recursion (extended to negative indices).

description: The Stirling number of the first type, `[n k]` (`c(n, k)`), for non-negative integers `n`, `k`.
The Stirling number of the second type, `{n k}` (`S(n, k)`), for non-negative integers `n`, `k`.

The `n`-th Bell number, the number of partitions of a set of size `n`. (Not to be confused with `NumberOfPartitions(n)`, which gives the number of partitions of the *integer* `n`.) Equals the sum of `StirlingSecond(n, k)` for `k` from `0` to `n` inclusive.
The number `E(n, r)` of permutations `p` of `{1,…,n}` having exactly `r` ascents (places where `p_i < p_{i+1}`).
The `n`-th harmonic number `H_n = Σ_{i=1}^{n} 1/i`.
The `n`-th Bernoulli number `B_n` as a rational number.
A real approximation to the `n`-th Bernoulli number `B_n`.
The `n`-th Bernoulli polynomial `B_n(x) = Σ_{k=0}^{n} (n choose k) B_k x^{n−k}`, where `B_n` is the `n`-th Bernoulli number.
algorithm: Closed form in terms of Bernoulli numbers.

description: The set of all subsets of the set `S`.
The set of subsets of the set `S` of size `k`. If `k` is larger than the cardinality of `S`, the result is empty.
The set of multisets consisting of `k` not necessarily distinct elements of the set `S`.
The set of sequences of length `k` with elements from the set `S`.
The set of permutations (stored as sequences) of the elements of the set `S`.
The set of permutations (stored as sequences) of each of the subsets of the set `S` of cardinality `k`.
The total number of partitions of a positive integer `n`.
The sequence of all partitions of a positive integer `n`.
The sequence of all partitions of `n` into `k` parts.
The sequence of all partitions of `n` whose parts are restricted to elements of the set `M` of positive integers.
The sequence of all partitions of `n` into `k` parts, with parts restricted to elements of the set `M`.
True if the sequence `S` consists of weakly decreasing positive integers; trailing zeros are allowed and the empty sequence is accepted (as a partition of zero).
A weakly decreasing sequence of positive integers which is a random partition of `n`.
For a partition `P` (sequence of positive integers): the sum of its parts.
The lexicographical order of partition `P` among partitions of the same weight. Ordering: `P₁ > P₂` iff `P₁` is greater in the first part in which they differ; the first index is zero.
The ordered monoid with `n` ordered generators.
The ordered monoid of words over the positive integers.
The identity element (null word) of ordered monoid `O`.
The `i`-th generator of `O`.
The word `w₁ ⋯ w_n` from a sequence of elements of `O`.
For `O` over the positive integers: the word `i₁ ⋯ i_n` from a sequence of integers.
True if words `w1`, `w2` from the same ordered monoid are equal.
Product (concatenation) of two words from the same ordered monoid.
True if `w1` and `w2` (from the same monoid) can be transformed into one another by elementary Knuth transformations.
The `i`-th generator in the product expressing word `w`.
For a word `w` over the positive integers: `w` as a sequence of integers.
The length of word `w`.
A sequence of non-negative integers whose `i`-th entry is the number of occurrences of the `i`-th generator in `w`.
True if `w` is a reverse lattice (Yamanouchi) word: for every `n > 0`, the content of the last `n` letters of `w` is a partition.
A weakly increasing subsequence of `w` of maximal length (not necessarily unique).
A sequence of `k` distinct increasing subsequences of `w` using the maximal number of entries of `w`; empty sequences are returned once all entries are used (not necessarily unique).
The plactic monoid obtained by factoring ordered monoid `O` by Knuth equivalence.
The plactic monoid obtained by factoring the ordered monoid over the positive integers by Knuth equivalence.
For a plactic monoid `P`: the ordered monoid on which `P` is based.
The identity element (null word) of plactic monoid `P`.
The `i`-th generator of `P`.
The product `u₁ ⋯ u_n` of a sequence of elements of `P`.
For `P` over the positive integers: the element corresponding to the Knuth equivalence class of `i₁ ⋯ i_n`.
For a word `w` from the ordered monoid `P` is based on: the element of `P` corresponding to the Knuth equivalence class of `w`.
For a sequence of elements of the underlying ordered monoid: the element of `P` for the class of `w₁ ⋯ w_n`.
For a plactic monoid `P` and a tableau `t` over the same ordered monoid: the element of `P` uniquely associated to `t`.
True if elements `u1`, `u2` of the same plactic monoid are equal.
Product of `u1`, `u2` (inherited from word concatenation in the ordered monoid).
The length of plactic-monoid element `u` (invariant under Knuth equivalence).
The content of `u` (sequence of generator-occurrence counts; invariant under Knuth equivalence).
Given an ordered monoid `O` or a plactic monoid `P` (with `O` the ordered monoid `P` is based on): the tableau monoid of tableaux whose labels are the generators of `O`.
The tableau monoid over the positive integers.
For a tableau monoid `M`: the ordered monoid from which `M` gets its labels.

For a sequence `Q` of sequences of non-negative integers: the tableau with the elements of `Q` as its rows (zeroes indicate skew entries). Must have weakly increasing rows and strictly increasing columns.
For a sequence `Q` of words from some ordered monoid: the (non-skew) tableau with the words of `Q` as its rows. Must have weakly increasing rows and strictly increasing columns.

For a partition `S` and a sequence `Q` of sequences of positive integers: a skew tableau with inner shape `S` and the non-skew part of each row given by the entries of `Q`. Must satisfy the tableau row/column conditions.
For a partition `S` and a sequence `Q` of words from some ordered monoid: a skew tableau with inner shape `S` and rows given by the words of `Q`.

For a word `w` from an ordered monoid (or an element `u` of a plactic monoid): the tableau obtained by row-inserting the entries of `w` (from the left) into the empty tableau. For `u`, any word of its Knuth class is used (well defined).
